review_text:
Review - 99% Satisfied. Just received the cooler. I'm a truck driver and I believe this unit will be just right for my needs. Size wise, perfect. I like that it is a flat top as I use the top as a table next to my seat and I also like the idea it can be used as an upright or chest. I was however disappointed that it did not have an AC plug like many other cheaper brands do. For the price, this should have been a feature. I wished it had an on/off switch so I wouldn't have to keep plugging and unplugging it to turn it on and off (not a big issue). Cord storage is real tight - they don't give you much room to store the power cord. It took me forever to get the cord out the way the manufacture had it stuffed. This is a preliminary review as I have not used the product at this time. I will update later after seeing how it performs. I do have high expectations it will serve me well.
Update 01/17/20: After using cooler on the road 2 weeks - kept milk, drinks and foods consistently cold. During the night, truck powers off to conserve battery; however, contents maintains temperature. The only other issue I have with this cooler is that I wished manufacturer had placed a LED light on the cooler to show when its powered. It does have one on the plug but that doesn’t mean the cooler is running if the connection is disconnected. The only way to tell if it’s still running is to feel the air flow from the fan. Still happy with the purchase.

Now, however, I prepare the drink according to the directions found on the label. I put a tablespoon of the granules into a mug and fill halfway with boiling water. Then, I add half of a mug of unsweetened almond milk that I heat in the microwave for about 45 seconds. Finally, I do half a dropperful of liquid stevia and two splashes of Nut Pods creamer. Great helmet except one nagging problem. I needed a new helmet with led light to use when riding my e-scooter. This one feels so light even with a led light. I especially like the dial adjuster that tightens the helmet fit more precisely. The magnetic visor allows you to easily snap on or off or keep overhead.

The only problem is power button on the light, its not easy to turn on or off. You need to press very precisely in a very small area. I will need to use the light every time I scooter so this might be an annoyance. They included an extra battery and a helmet backpack.

Overall, I think its a very impressive deal for the money.

I raved about this helmet except I noticed that I a peculiar problem. Since I've owned this I've worn the visor from time to time. A surprising pattern has been happening and I can only attribute to the visor. I get airborne debris in my eyes only when I wear the visor. When it would happen early on I would just complain internally and forget about it. Then I started paying attention to how often I get these problems and sure enough only when I used the visor. I have noted my rides with visor on/off, sunglasses on/off and no eye protection at all. I get the most debris in the eye with the visor on. I'm guessing the curve of the visor creates a vortex that directs floating debris into the internal space of the visor and right into my eyes. I loved the idea of a large visor that allows for a wide optical view. In fact, its supposed to be protect my eyes from UV rays as well as debris. Instead I no longer use the visor and went back to wearing sunglasses.

product_name: Blackview Smart Watch for Android Phones and iOS Phones, All-Day Activity Tracker with Heart Rate Sleep Monitor, 1.3" Full Touch Screen, 5ATM Waterproof Pedometer, Smartwatch for Men Women
product_category: Cell Phones & Accessories | Activity & Fitness Trackers
review_text:
Overpromises and Underperforms- Edit: Won't Send a Replacement Charger Cable. Edit: 6 months on, the charging cable has become unreliable. I contacted the manufacturer for a replacement. They won't send it unless I supply an order number. I received this as a gift and the person who gave it to me can't find the order number. So now I am screwed because I can't get a new cable. Don't buy form this company!
The good stuff. It is a watch. It keeps time. The face is pretty easy to read. There is a choice of 4 formats for the face. No options for anything different than one of those 4. The battery is rechargeable and lasts for days and days. The charger cable is kind of cool because it connects by means of magnets and the polarity of the magnets prevents you from connecting it incorrectly. The watch looks okay and is pretty comfortable to wear. The band is really long, which would be great if you have really thick wrists.
The marketing hype:
- It says it is waterproof on the box and on the product description, encouraging the owner to wear it while swimming, but the manual cautions about keeping the watch dry. Which is it?
- The package says that you can "receive calls, app messages and SMS messages from this fitness watch". That is an extreme exaggeration. First of all, the watch does not have a speaker, so you are not going to hear any call. Possibly you would get a notification of an incoming call, although I have not been able to get that working. Any notification you get will be a wrist vibration that is nearly undetectable. I have yet to get a notification from anything except an event that was on my calendar, and the description of the event was truncated to a single letter, so I was unable to figure out what the notification was.
The Verifit Pro App. To be fair, much of the functionality of the watch is directly linked to the associated app. You download it from the appstore and install it on your smartphone. Then you "bind" your watch to that phone and the watch and phone exchange data. You WILL need to do this. To get the watch to do much of anything beyond telling time and counting steps, you will need to turn on watch functionality through the app settings. You will need to use the app to actually access some of the functions, such as the sleep monitoring. You will also need to use tha app if you want to set any alarms on the watch. You can initiate a timer from the watch, and you can turn an alarm on and off from the watch, but it will not let you create an alarm from the watch. (Remember, there is no speaker on the watch, and the notification is a slight vibration on your wrist.) The Timer function will not let you do anything else or view the current time of day while it is running. If you try to navigate away, it wants to turn off the timer. The Music Controller function works IF you happen to be using one of the supported services to play music on your linked phone. I was able to use it with Google Play Music and Amazon Music. You can move backwards and forwards on the current album, but it will not allow you to select a new piece of music. Only navigate the current list or stop playing. It does not allow you to control volume.
The very few other reviewers of this product have questioned the accuracy of readings. I can't speak to that. The sleep monitor does seem to be accurate about when I went to sleep and when I woke up. I have no idea how the watch knows when I am in deep sleep or light sleep. The pulse rates the watch has reported seem like they are reasonable, but short of counting beats and comparing them with the watch, I don't know how I would know.
Documentation - or lack thereof. There is a booklet in the watch package. It is about a quarter of an inch thick, but only 15 pages of it are in English, and broken English, at that. I had hoped that there would be more helpful information in the Verifit Pro app, and there is a bit, but nowhere near what there should be. (It's an APP. There could be tutorials and ideas for how to use the watch effectively, but no. There are a few Q and A lists. I even tried going to the Blackview web page to see if they offered any videos or anything. From their webpage it is as if they only make smartphones. Nothing there.
Summary: This smartwatch mostly works. It overpromises and underperforms, but I would guess that most of the competing products in its price range do the same thing. If you want a smartwatch and don't want to pay a boatload of money for it, this would fill the bill. It will tell time, and provide some other functions, just not what the description would lead you to believe. Be prepared to sit with the watch and the smartphone app and try things in order to figure out how to set it up and how to use it because the documentation is sketchy.

product_name: SL-Track Massage Chair Zero Gravity Full Body Electric Shiatsu Massage Chair Recliner with Built-in Heat Foot Roller Air Massage System Stretch Vibrating Audio for Home Office,Black
review_text:
E730 Model-Good Value for the $800 Spent. For a little background on me, I used to be a manager at Brookstone and have sold several different models of massage chairs. I don't claim to be an expert, but I know a thing or two. Now for the review:

I've owned this chair (E730) for a little over 5 months now for $800 from the Cavalier Store.

Shipping process:
I don't remember exactly how long shipping took, but I remember it being right in the middle of the delivery window. The shipping company would not step foot on my property and would not come through the gate to the backyard. I'm in Chicago so they left it in the alley and I dragged it through the gate by myself. The company called me a day before and told me approximately when it would arrive so that I could be home to sign for it.

Getting it inside and assembly:
This thing is heavy and big. You definitely need two strong people to carry it. It comes two pieces: the main unit and the foot massager. It was a challenge to fit it through some of the door frames. I had to take two of the doors off so make sure it will fit through yours. Assembly was pretty easy, just follow the instructions and connect a few hoses together for the airbags.

The massages pros:
The massage is really nice. I think it's a little on the harder side so it may not be the best for people who are sensitive, but I love a good hard massage. The airbags feel really nice, especially on your calves. I really like some of the pre-programed massages. The zero gravity really take a load off your back. I used to get massages about once a month and I've stopped going completely since buying this chair. The chair looks nice and the faux leather is really nice too.

Cons: The machine definitely has some quirks to it. For instance, if the timer runs out or if you want to switch from one pre-programed massage to another and you are in zero gravity, the chair will go fully upright and then you can put it back into zero gravity again. The user interface is moderately featured, but is lacking in some areas. I wish there was more customization. For instance, there are a number of manual options, but no way to program a custom massage. There is not a way to designate which airbags to use, it's either all or none. The airbags on your feet can be a little too strong. I don't know if this is just my machine, but the body scanning has not worked at all since day one. It's stuck on the tallest height setting and I cannot change the settings to fit someone smaller. But I'm 5' 10" and it's perfect for me. I haven't reached out to any kind of support to try to resolve this issue. Other than that, I've had no mechanical issues with it. Lastly, there are bluetooth speakers on the outside of the chair, but they are absolute garbage. But who buys a massage chair for its speakers?

Overall rating 7.5/10. It was well worth the $800 I spent on it. I see that it's going for about $1300 now, I'm not sure it's worth it at that price, but it's a solid machine.

A word of advice for any massage chair shopper, BUY THE WARRANTY! I haven't had to use it yet, but many massage chairs, even from well known name brands breakdown and you don't want to spend all this money just for it to die in a few years.

product_name: Hyke & Byke Zion Hiking & Backpacking Tent - 3 Season Ultralight, Waterproof Tent for Camping w/Rain Fly and Footprint - 2 Person - Forest Green
review_text:
I wish I had better news.. Tent arrived packed well, but is definitely not 3 lbs like it states all over the place. 6lbs 1 oz with dyneema cord and Ti stakes. Strings and strands in areas, but stitching was intact. Set up was 15 min. exact in the dark with zero instruction. Tent stakes are sturdy and well made, still used titanium that I already had. Guyed it out, locked it down and waited for storms.
Wind - low profile, handles gusts. The rain fly seems to never get tight though. This leads to some flapping.
Rain - fly does not come down enough to stop back splash into the tent. The footprint sticks out and collects rain under the bathtub floor. The vents are located mid body which leaves all the warm air in the upper dome. The vents do not stay open because the props are like wet crackers. All together, after owning many tents, this is the worst condensation on the floor I have ever seen. It just puddles during rain.
Design - vents are worthless, vestibules are not bad for shoes ( with out it raining ), pockets and loft are a nice touch, single pole is a good fast pitch, dual up and down zippers help during rain. Fly sheds water well ( 22 hours straight ), plenty of room as I am 6'4", and I think the tent really works the best for hot conditions. All mesh and you can aim it so the fly would tunnel the breeze.
Over all - great price with nice features, like the fly on teardown of the tent if it's raining. But, I always test my gear before hitting the trail. This tent will soak your down bag if it rains, because the vents are wrong, dont stay open and water pools under the tent as the footprint sticks out. Luckily I carry an ultralight shamy. So I could sop up the water every hour during the night. I will probably do a full length video on my YT channel. Had hope for this tent, but rain kills it.

product_name: ECO-WORTHY Automatic Submersible Boat Bilge Water Pump 12V 1100GPH Auto with Float Switch for Boat Caravan RV
review_text:
Using as temp mini sumps in basement.. My unfinished basement had a serious flooding problem when we bought the house. We knew about it and got the house for a song. Over the course of two years, I did a lot of exterior grading to move most of the water away and that worked very well. However, when we get several days of hards rains, then we still get water intrusion into the basement. I've been using a large wet vac to keep it clear and that was ok, but a hell of a lot of work. I'm old. So on my last foray into vacuuming 100 gallons of water over a straight 24 hour span, I realized I was always pulling from the same two spots in the center floor seam. Pulled out the jackhammer and popped out two 1 sq ft holes about 8 " deep. Bought 2 of these (actually 3, one as a backup). Put them inside a screen enclosure and discharge into 1" drain lines to my main sump. These work brilliantly! Pretty quiet, run for about 4 seconds every minute on automatic. Yippee, I get to sleep when it rains hard. Yes, this is temp and in the spring I'm going to bite the bullet and cut in inside perimeter drains, but for now, THEY WORK GREAT!!! and cheap. I got the automatic ones.

UPDATE - Well, these little guys just keep on working, perfectly! I have a small, SLA battery next to each pump. The pumps draw so little power that after several days of intermittent operation, I really did not need to charge the batteries. I am not so sure I want to chop up my basement perimeter for a permanent drain, as well as these guys are working. I'll see over the course of this year if I hit a rainy period when they can't keep up or fail. For now - PERFECT!

product_name: CamelBak Kickbak Tumbler, Stainless Pfb, 30 oz
review_text:
Leaks like a sieve. I purchased both the 20 oz and 30 oz varieties of the Camelbak Kickback Tumbler to replace an older Camelbak Forge (16 oz) for which I'd lost the lid. Both the 20 oz and 30 oz models do an excellent job of keeping hot liquids hot. I can pour a fresh cup of tea, put the lid on, and then promptly forget it on the counter when I leave, and it's still hot enough to burn the tongue a couple hours later when I return. Even without the lid, it loses heat slowly enough that I can nurse a 30 oz cup of tea for most of the morning. The problem is the lid. It simply doesn't seal. It doesn't merely drip or dribble a bit; it streams. If I fill the cup, put the lid on, and then tip it with the larger of the two lid openings pointing downward, liquid will pour from that opening. Upon inspection, I discovered that this is because the gap when it "closes" is large enough to be visible. This opening is about 1 3/4" wide on the 30 oz model; slightly smaller on the 20 oz version. The visible gap, when the flip top is in the closed position, is nearly 1/16" running the entire length of the opening. As you might imagine, quite a bit of liquid can flow from an opening of that size pretty quickly, should you drop or tip over the mug. It will be a considerably smaller mess than if it had no lid at all, but a sizeable mess nonetheless. The fact that I have this issue with the lids from both sizes indicates this is not merely a case of having gotten a single defective lid. Rather, this would seem to be a design flaw and/or manufacturing issue. So, if you plan to use this around the house, or at your desk, or even while working around the yard, rest assured, it will keep your beverage hot for a long time. But if you knock it over, it WILL leak, so I wouldn't recommend using it near electronic equipment or precious heirlooms. And it is certainly NOT acceptable for carrying in a backpack or even on a belt holder, as any liquid that sloshes about from your movement WILL leak from the lid onto you, your clothes, your gear, etc. Use at your own risk.

Just one additional note. While I like the extra capacity of the 30 oz version, it can be a bit difficult to handle. I don't have especially large hands, but nor are they abnormally small. I find I have to grab the mug where it tapers toward the bottom, as the larger circumference at the middle - where I instinctively want to grab it - is just large enough that I can't always get a good grip on it; particularly if I'm outside, wearing gloves. This is not a design flaw, but rather just the nature of a mug of this capacity. But if you're considering a purchase and trying to decide between the 20 oz and 30 oz, it's something to think about.

review_text:
Revised review….It last less then 2 years!. Revised: The chair lasted less then two years.
Now it’s either repairable or a large brick. Nice while it lasted. I’ve had this chair for over 8 months. I did a lot of research before making this purchase on chairs in this price range. This chair comes in a large box. The foot rest is attached with a stationary pin and a pin that’s on a spring. You also connect two small air tubes and an electric connection. It took me less then 5 minutes to put together. ( it’s not difficult at all). Connect the remote and power cord and your ready to go.

This chair has a LSS track which means the rollers go all the under your butt checks! This feels incredible. There is rolling, tapping, kneading, and other motions. There are 5 auto modes and I love the “Extend” program as it compresses your calves and the foot rest raises and lowers to stretch out those muscles. The foot rollers are strong! I wear thick socks for the first few weeks, but I have gotten used to it. The heat is therapeutic, but you would definitely never get burned and it does not get as hot as a heating pad.

Some have said it does not do the neck and shoulder blades well. The auto programs don’t seem to hit those areas; just hit the Manuel button and up button and it will hit your neck and shoulder blades perfectly! I was also surprised by the Bluetooth speakers, they are pretty good to play relaxing music or a meditation beat.

If you have arthritis, neck or back problems, this is the chair for you. Sore after working out or doing yard work? This will take care of it and get you back up and running.

If you like your neck and shoulder blades rubbed hardier, just flip the pillow back and it will really go to town. This chair seems very well made and I’m hopeful it will last a long time! There are also air bags on your upper shoulders, places to skip both arms into, calf area airbags. If this is your budget for a chair I don’t think you can do any better. My neck pain is reduced and no more restless legs at night. You will sleep like a baby! Just do it!

review_text:
This is bigger than most folding umbrellas and has an attractive look.. For almost 30 years I carried a Brookstone brand umbrella. It was built like a tank but was light and folded to 18" in spite of having a 56 inch arc. Recently I backed my golf cart over it and, because Brookstone is a shell of itself, I couldn't replace the umbrella. After an incredible amount of searching, I found this umbrella. It is almost as big as my Brookstone and folds to under 16". It seems to be almost as sturdy as the Brookstone and it opens and closes at the push of a button. It is very nice-looking with its wooden handle and blue fabric. I tried it with wind gusts and it hasn't inverted and I like the water repellency. My old umbrella would soak up water like a sponge and take several hours to dry. This one is dry in less than an hour. I also like the double folding that makes it easier to hold above my car door to open and to close.

Pros:
- size, both open and closed
- attractive looking
- seeming to resist wind
- the cover is very nice with its zipper

Cons:
- The handle looks good but is too slippery (rubber would be better)
- It is a little heavier than the umbrella it replaced
- it is "fatter" than my last umbrella and much harder to strap closed

review_text:
Really nice starter bike for my daughter. My daughter has just gotten to the size range specified for this bike, and after going to a local shop and seeing the minorly insulting options for little girls, I decided we'd take the route of a higher quality bike instead.

This was easy to put together with my husband and took about a half hour, most of which was us trying to interpret instructions. The booklet showed how to install a few different bike models, so we had to keep checking we were doing it right. Everything was mostly straightforward once we discerned what the instructions would have us do.

The materials on this look great, everything is solidly built, nicely finished, and looks like it will last through multiple kids, if you have them.

It is not too heavy, and it is easy to get going on it. The scoot bike experience in our household surely helped.

We put a few Yoshi decals on to make the green extra fancy for my daughter. The green has a matte finish that took the decals well.

Overall we couldn't be happier with the quality level on this. Really lovely little bike for offroading in the back lawn, and a good first real bike for my daughter.

The only problem I've had with it is once in awhile when you pop open the  top water will spray out. and sometimes the straw makes a whistling sound but these are very minor things. product_name: Hover-1 Alpha Electric Scooter | 18MPH, 12M Range, 5HR Charge, LCD Display, 10 Inch High-Grip Tires, 264LB Max Weight, Cert. & Tested - Safe for Kids, Teens & Adults
review_text:
Comparison with Ninebot ES4. I have a Ninebot ES4, the one with the upgraded battery, which weighs ~30 pounds, goes 18-19 mph at max speed on flat ground, and has a range of 28 miles. I'm a petite adult woman (5'4", 110 lb), and I use a scooter as my daily commuter in an urban area that has some minor changes in elevation (nothing like San Francisco, but not flat like Florida).

In comparing this Hover-1 Alpha scooter to my Ninebot ES4, the Hover:

- has a louder motor
- has a slightly lower max speed (17 mph)
- has a shorter total range (12 miles)
- has pneumatic (air-filled) tires, which are a MILLION times better and provide a way smoother ride than the Ninebot's solid rubber tires (awful, my main complaint with the Ninebot)
- has disc brakes, which I like better than the Ninebot's electric hand brake
- doesn't fold up as flat as the Ninebot and is thus more awkward to carry
- has a wider and grippier deck
- has higher handlebars, which was weird at first but then I got used to it
- has a weird location for the charging port (really low, at the height of the deck)

Both have:
- a foot brake on the rear wheel
- fun lights under the deck
- about the same total weight (~30 lb)

I still like the total range on my Ninebot ES4 (28 miles), but this Hover-1 Alpha scooter is an excellent contender for someone who doesn't need that kind of range but who still wants fairly high speeds, much better than the ~14 mph top speeds you get with most single-battery folding scooters right now. If this scooter had been available when I was originally in the market for mine, I probably would have opted for this one instead of the Ninebot ES4 because this one is literally half the price. I would just bring the charger with me to ensure I never ran out of juice/range.

Overall, really fun and highly recommended.

review_text:
Decent in very low-light conditions. A compact little visibility light, quite useful if you are running at night and want something to tell drivers that you are around. Superior to a simple reflective vest, especially with a blinking pattern. Not so useful at dusk though - the light simply isn't bright enough to draw a lot of attention when the ambient light is still high. This isn't a significant issue, just don't expect it to do something too substantial.

The interface is pretty good - a long press ensures that it will almost never be activated accidentally, it is easy to switch between modes, and the light remembers the last mode you were on. The blinking patterns are variegated and should draw notice from drivers. The clip is perfect for non-intrusive mounting to a belt, arm band, or pack strap.

I would recommend this for night runners, so long as it compliments a reflective vest and reflective wrist/ankle bands. I use it as a a rear pack light when hiking, since the pack hides my reflective vest. The lithium battery and long lifespan make this an ideal light to tuck away in your hiking pack just in case you end up on the road at night.

review_text:
Seems OK, if it were not for the fact that mine came sewn incorrectly. This product seems to be a decent quality, although like so many nylon harnesses, it can have sharp edges. I think they melt the edges to prevent fraying, and this can result in hard, sharp pieces of plastic sticking out. The sharp parts are very small, so probably not a problem for a dog with a thick coat.

But, mine came sewn incorrectly. When one side has the black buckle under the metal ring (as it should be, to be able to connect to a leash), the other side has the block buckle over the metal ring. The whole thing has to be twisted 180 degrees to make it work.

So, I can't really recommend this product. In general, I would not recommend any nylon harness unless you are sure small sharp parts won't bother your dog. Get another material like cotton or hemp that doesn't have sharp edges. And of course, hopefully yours will be sewn correctly :)

product_name: Hidrate Spark 3 Smart Water Bottle, Tracks Water Intake and Glows to Remind You to Stay Hydrated, BPA Free, 20 oz, Coral
review_text:
Great but could be perfect. Updating my initial review now that I have had this a few months. I am adding another start because once you have up up and running and using it, the bottle is pretty amazing. It appears to track water intake pretty accurately. Also, I was concerned about the battery life but I am still using the initial battery that it came with and so it has been working for about 90 days now which is a lot longer than I expected. I probably prefer having a replaceable battery now versus a rechargeable one that I requested in my review below. I highly recommend it! Just wish I could sink it with my Fitbit and WeightWatcher App.
******************************************************************************************************
I was excited to find this product when I was in the Apple store. I have been looking for something that would both remind me to drink water plus track my water intake and this sounded like exactly what I needed. I previously tried using a hydration watch which vibrates to remind you to drink but your brain gets used to the vibration and ignores it after a while. Well at least my brain did. So I bought this wand while I like it, it really could be so much better if they made some slight improvements.
1) The instructions are not that great. They don't really explain much about the product.
2) Downloading and connecting to the App was super easy. Maybe one of the easiest products I've ever had to sync to an app via bluetooth.
3) Assebly. I removed the bottom of the bottle to do the initial clean-up and when I did the rubber seal fell out. Again the instructions don't explain how it should be assembled properly so I kept reassembling it how I thought and it kept leaking on me. Finally on my third attempt throughout the day and using a spoon to ensure the seal was pressed into the base properly it stopped leaking. Luckily I won't have to remove the base everyday but just periodically to clean it.
4) Battery. While they make it sound like the replaceable battery is a positive thing with not having to recharge it, I would prefer a rechargeable battery. I have no issues with placing something on a charger every night before I go to bed. I hate the idea of having to continually purchase replacement batteries. Plus they claim this is a proprietary battery which in my minds means I can't buy it at my local store and it is going to be expensive to replace. I have no idea yet what replacement costs are. Again, their instructions never mention anything about battery life.
5) Reminders: This is my biggest disappointment. While you can go into the App and adjust the glow reminders the options they give you are limiting. I was hoping you could tell it to remind you to take a drink every 15 minutes if you wanted that but instead you program the hours that you are awake during the day and can tell it to remind you up to 10 times during that window. I want more flexibility and control please. Also I do it see it glowing a few times a day but I've not seen it glow 10 times as I have it programmed. I would expect it to glow every hour since my hydration window is 10 hours long but it doesn't seem to do that. I am wondering if I am continually drinking from the bottle that it doesn't then remind you to hydrate since you have within the past hour? Again the instructions don't explain how the reminders work at all.
4) I want to be able to quickly and easily turn on and off the reminders. If I am in a meeting with the CEO I don't want my water bottle to suddenly start glowing on the table haha.
5) I want to be able to control how long the glow lasts. You can. You can control the brightness which is nice and if it should fade in and out or blink but now how long it stays lit. I wish it would stay lit until you take a drink because your eyes are not on the bottle all the time so you often miss the reminders.
6) Make it vibrate, again you don't always have the bottle in plain sight so it would be nice if you could turn on a vibrate mode to give you an audible alert as well.
7) Water intake tracking - This is probably the best feature of the bottle and seems to work pretty well. My only issue is that so far every morning after it has reset from the previous day and I open the app up before i have drank any water it has already registered some amount of water intake that has ranged anywhere from 3oz to 9oz. However this is not a big concern of mine as long as directionally I know how much water I am consuming throughout the day. It doesn't have to be 100% accurate in my mind.
8) I really like the feel of the water bottle. It is a nice design. However the plastic lid and base do feel like a pretty cheap plastic. For the price you would think they could have splurged for a better quality.
9) It does not seem insulated at all and they don't claim that it is but surprisingly it does seem to keep cold water cool longer than I expected.
10) Rather than make the whole bottle glow which can be a little distracting and embarrassing when you are using it at the office it would be nice to have just a more subtle ring at the base glow and as mentioned earlier stay lit until you pick it up to take a drink.

It sounds like they've made several improvements int he 3.0 versus the previous model. This is a good product, I just wish it was a great product. Hopefully some of their future versions will incorporate some of the things mentioned above. Enjoy!

product_name: BELL Stratus MIPS Adult Road Bike Helmet
review_text:
Fine mid-level helmet with caveats. I certainly wouldn't pay too much for this helmet and didn't. I got it via Amazon on some type of sale, for about 60. It does not seem to be a $100 or $120 helmet.

Pros: comfortable, fits my head (just like for motorcycle helmets, the first priority is fit, and only secondary/tertiary do stylistic or other features come into play), the Bell sweat guard does the job on the brow (until it doesn't, but gives a rider plenty of time to either look down/press their forehead to it/press the helmet to their forehead to drain it - and it will be an impressive stream of sweat).

Cons: yes, it allows air in, which is what we want, but perhaps it either allows more air in than other super-vented helmets, or it just isn't a correct design, but I feel this helmet is less aerodynamic than my last Giro. But the helmet certainly seems a little wider/mushroom-topped than the Giro.

Neutral: there is a little tab, pictured and highlighted, that is a 'keyed' tab - mine somehow came undone, and despite trying to snap it back together it just wouldn't. It wasn't until I was analyzing it today that I saw it was a keyed tab. So it didn't break, but it did come apart at some point. I feel that some less aware may either not notice this, or never figure out how to put it back together. I'll call it a better design than a snap since it floats its range freely and probably has less of a chance of breaking.

Verdict: A great mid range (not upper mid-range) helmet for casual cyclists. A little less aero than we roadies who hope, and do, maintain higher speeds should expect. I'm keeping it for gravel riding, and just bought a different brand to try for my road helmet.

review_text:
Too thick for new Trek Checkpoint SL5. I really want to like this but I just can't make it work on my gravel bike. There is not enough clearance anywhere. My bike has the standard Shimano 105 crankset. The gap between the crank arm and the rear of the frame is very narrow and can't accommodate this device. I'm honestly not sure how this would work on any modern high end bike. I've tried facing the sensor on the outside of the crank arm, and that works great as long as I don't clip my shoes into the pedals. As soon as I clip in, my shoes rub against the sensor.

Someone suggested taping the sensor to the outside surface of the crankset (on the chain side.) I did this in hopes that it would work. It does not. The problem is that it's too close to the center and doesn't get enough momentum to to accurately register anything. (Think of it moving in a small circle versus a big circle...the device doesn't appear to move fast enough in each revolution to work.) I've even tried attaching it to my shoe and that doesn't work.

Bottom line: If you have enough clearance or if you don't clip your shoes in, this is a great device for this price. If you have a newer high-end bike or want to clip in, look at the gap between your crank arm and frame very closely before you decide.

Second time ordering. My golf life involves playing 3-5 times a week.
I used Lamkin grips for a long time and then ran across these Karma grips. I've had the Karma mid-size grips on my irons/wedges (4-60 degree) for about a year now. Changed a few that were getting worn but stayed with the Karma brand. I like the grips. No complaints at all. Wildly inaccurate golf shots are on me, not a grip.
INSTALL: I found these Karma grips to install easier than the Lamkin grips. Getting the inside tape off the shaft is not easier, but once the shaft is ready, the Karma grips go on quickly.
VALUE: These Karma grips look like a Lamkin grip, wear like a Lamkin grip and cost a lot less.

review_text:
Not the Best Bag. Here’s Proof:. (Watch my included Video Review for demonstrations about all of this stuff I list. The owner keeps trying to “downvote” or remove my review for some reason instead of emailing me about this one-on-one.)

PROS:

-Bag is made very, very durable. It’s pretty cool how attentive they were with attention to detail.
-The handles are great too. My gripe with other major brands of sand bags is that their handles are just flimsy pieces of cloth. This company is great because they’re legit plastic handles with finger grooves - great for those brutal soul crushing workouts when you can’t grip any longer.

CONS:

-NOT 50lbs. Video review is attached of the sand bag filled full and also sitting on a (new) Rephno Scale. Max weight for this bag is roughly 30lbs, if you fill the bag to the factory-recommended “Max Fill Lines”.
-Colors are a little wack. Not a big fan of all-red everything, but i suppose that doesn’t matter too much. Color scheme is most definitely where this company is hurting compared to its big brand competitor that essentially allows you to customize your sandbag online with different colors or patterns.
-It’s pretty small compared to its competitors. This bag is just BARELY over 2 feet long, while most competitors have bags that are 3-4ft long. I’m a bigger dude (6’2” at 240 lbs) so having a tiny bag is a little annoying, but the handles make up for it, allowing better grip and stability during workouts for how small it is in size. For shorter or smaller individuals the bag will be just the right size, i’m sure. For bigger dudes, I wouldn’t recommend this bag based on size alone, but to each their own. Perhaps the stability provided by the great handles will change my mind down the road.

I’m sure I could over-fill the bag past the factory recommended limit and it would hit 50lbs, but then I risk having sand leak out obviously, and with this national quarantine I’m doing workouts in my apartment living room, so that’s a no-go for me. Not worth the risk.

Overall, for $60, this isn’t a bad deal. Their competitors- with arguably much better products - list their bags for well over $120 for the cheapest options, so I would say this: If you’re trying to save money and don’t mind the bright red color, sure go for this bag. It’s not too bad. Just know you have to over-fill it a bit to hit that 50lb weight. If you would like a bag that you can essentially customize with colors, or prefer bags a little bigger (3 to 4 feet long) then do NOT buy this bag. Spend the extra money and go with the big name competitor (rhymes with "Fruit Borce").

Just my two cents as a tall and super active fitness dude looking for a sandbag for daily workouts and training.

Essentially these are microfiber tubes that go over your head and around your neck like a cowl - but these aren't tight around your neck. If you're a sewer and have some stretchy fabric, I'll bet you could do the same thing, but I can't sew so these are great.

review_text:
Great, light-weight Saddle - 5 stars. This review will only be for the saddle, not any other accessories.

I've had this saddle since the summer of 2016, so I've been using it for four years. For most of that time, I typically have ridden 2-3 times a month easy trail riding. Nothing complicated or rough. For the past 3 months, I've been riding 3-4 days out of each week.

With that said, I really like this saddle. For a couple hundred dollars, it suits me just fine.

Pros:
. Very light weight and easy to handle. I can throw it on my 15hh palomino with ease. I'm 5'11" tall.
. Durable for my style and amount of riding. As mentioned above, I'm not a roper or rodeo guy. Just a person with a horse and some acres. Easy, fun riding for recreation.
. Pretty much maintenance free. I don't even clean it. I just get it out, use it, and put it away.
. I also have saddle bags attached to the rear and the equipment attachment points are holding up well.
. After four years, I have absolutely no plans to replace it. It's holding up great and should give me many more years of enjoyment riding my four-hoof friend.

Cons:
. The "leather" on the horn is showing signs of getting tired and frayed around the edges as my hands and reins rub on it. It has a few tiny threads sticking out and the number of threads showing seems to be increasing. Though, it does NOT look or seem worn out. Just fraying a little.
. The stirrups are a bit tight around my boots. I wear fairly narrow western boots and I still found it helpful to remove the material covering the stirrups and spray paint them black so my boots slide in and out easier and more quickly.
. The buckles on the inside of the fenders that you use to adjust the height of the stirrups has sort of "sharp" corners. I have them wrapped with a couple layers of heavy duct tape so they don't rub against my horse's side.

The rest of the tack is just so-so. I've never attached the breast collar, but it would serve as decorative, but probably not practical or functional as it is only held on with dog leash type clips. And the bridle is OK, but nothing more.

I would recommend buying that equipment separate and getting better quality components.

All in all, a great saddle, not just for the price, but in spite of the low price.

I would recommend it to a friend.

review_text:
Block sound but has horrible buttons. These check the box of blocking sound. Good for kids and they are just the adult version but with a smaller head piece. I tried them on as an adult male and I can technically wear them at their largest size but they are pulling up on my ears. My wife experienced the same but they fit our girls fine. First of all while you have big buttons the tactile feedback when using them is zero-zilch-nada. This could be overlooked because you could press them again if the volume didn't change but the other problem is that there seems to be a lag of a second or two in when it responds to the change. Lastly I can't seem to find a setting I like. There seems to be wow-this-amplifies-the-worm-crawling-50-ft-away at the top and as son as you turn it down enough it stops letting voices through. There are different levels just not where I think they should be.

If you find a setting you like these work fine. Loud sounds aren't let through and you can still hear people around you. Or the people on the other side of the shooting range for that matter. Wow do these things amplify. When you do get the battery cover off these are pretty plastic-y. I think they will hold up to the average persons use but they aren't Caldwell's top quality version.

review_text:
Wonderful Invention. My 83 yo mother has had several falls in the house. I have MS and am not strong enough to lift her off the floor. Therefore, we have to call EMS each time and feel guilty about using them for something so simple as lifting her into a chair. Of course, they are always most professional and kind to help us when this happens but I kept thinking there had to be a better way.
The ELK has saved the day! My mother had a fall two days ago and we tested it out on her for the first time. It worked exactly as specified and she was up off the floor in no time. As others have mentioned, it's topsy-turvy while inflating so you have to hold on to your person to keep them safe...or have them hold on to a chair for support. It's worse on Level 1 and 2..the bottom cushions. Once you get to the top two cushions, it becomes much more stable. Like others have said, keep the unit plugged in all the time. The battery goes flat pretty quickly if not plugged in. The unit is very mobile and easy to set up. Instruction booklet is excellent too.

review_text:
The Holster Sucks. I kinda regret buying this. It's very adjustable size wise and fits great, but there are a few things I really don't like about it.

First is the holster, sure it will hold a full size heavy pistol, but if you move or lean forward the velcro holding the holster starts to un-stick, especially at the top of the holster, which ends up leaving the top sticking out and hanging away from your chest. This could be easily ripped off. There are two straps attached to the holster which would prevent it from just falling to the ground, but they are not very adjustable so you can't really get them to hold the holster tight to your chest like you would want to.

Second I don't like the rigid tube they put in the right shoulder. It can interfere with sholdering a rifle and should just be removed.

I'll probably just end up buying a better molle vest and buy the attachments I want for it. Lesson learned again, you get what you pay for, buy once and cry once. This should be relegated to airsoft and not any real use.

Other than that the vest feels good when you put it on after getting it adjusted, and there is a lot of included storage so in that aspect you are getting a lot of storage for your money, just really wish the holster system was improved and this would actually be useable.

product_name: Mitchell 300 Spinning Fishing Reel
review_text:
REVISED OPINION. My first spinning real was the original Mitchell 300, a hand-me-down from my dad -- about 1959 or 1960. I thought I would give up fishing, so gave all my gear to a boys' club. I thought that I was old enough to be "fished out". Well, I am now 76 and at my wife's urging (read: nagging) I am going to get out her hair by taking up the rod again.

This real is a great improvement over an already great reel. It is so smooth and tight. I look forward to putting it to use this summer.

UPDATE: After two months of actual use I have severely changed my opinion of this real. First, it's innards are more exposed than on my old real, susceptible to all kinds of crud. Second, the bale is different and it is difficult to set the line with out it snagging on the bale, sending your lure into the mud or brush at your feet. Third, it gets both mild and severe backlashes -- I had more in one day than in all my previous life. Fourth, The line easily wraps around the handle or back of the real; the line then gets nicked, resulting in strange line breaks, sometimes 15 feet from the lure!

I wish I had my old version back again.

I was also surprised how well these tires clear mud.
There are 2 versions of the Trail King, one is hand made in Germany and the other in China which costs about $10 less than the German made tire. I've tried both and the performance is the same. No punctures so far even though I ride through dry vegetation, rocks, exposed tree roots, dry creek beds and rough central Texas terrain. Trail King grip is excellent and rivals Maxxis Minion tires.

review_text:
A very good rain poncho/tarp for most uses. Covers quite a bit and keeps you both dry and ventilated. Good ventilation and coverage is why I prefer a poncho over a rain jacket. However, high winds and driving rains will make you hunker down until the blow passes.

The material is pretty durable, and with the grommets this makes a good light duty shade and rain tarp (you have to make sure you close off the hood). But it isn't sufficient as a general duty camping tarp.

I carry this on hikes and day hikes. Sometimes I will also bring an ultralight hammock on a day hike. I can use this to keep either sun, wind, or sprinkles from getting to me. But again, it is the "have it if you need it" item rather than the everyday use item.

Something for the EDC "get home now" or "bugout" bag. I suppose. I don't really know. But for those of you relying on the 99 cent plastic poncho...DON'T. This would be MUCH better.

Not only that, but the only-1-battery (vs 2 for the old model) really doesn't gain much because these fade so much more quickly than the old models. They are OK, but I have searched and stocked up on the old 'sulphur spring' color model and will hope they last until Nathan realizes that their not-so-new lights just aren't as good.

I'm a little torn over these. I've been using the "sulfur green" color from the previous gen and really like them. However, one just failed and I thought I'd try these, and in almost every way they are better:
1) They are much brighter with 3 "big" looking lights vs the 4 smaller ones.
2) They only take one battery vs the old ones using 2, and if they last for a similar time this is great in terms of minimizing disposable battery usage.
3) They have 4 rather than 3 patterns so there's more choice.

So what's not to like:
1) None of the patterns acts quite like the old 'strobe' and I don't think they're as eye-catching.
2) I am used to having to hold down the button for a few seconds to turn them on and off, but it sure feels longer and annoying to do it.

I maybe should give these 5 stars because I'm going to immediately switch to using them because of the additional brightness.

review_text:
Great value!. I included lots of photos to show examples of what I was speaking of.

The material is nice. The inside of the material seems to have like a rubberized silver reflective quality to it. The floor is thin so I would reccomend a tarp or some kind of footprint if you are placing on a rough surface. The screen material is a soft mesh material that is tightly woven. No bugs are getting in other than when you open the door. The tent was delivered today. I opened in my front yard right away without looking at the directions. It went up in less than 2 minutes. Now that I know how to do it, it may only take a minute to have ready to use without stakes. I sat inside the tent for roughly 20 minutes. I didnt notice any odor that you might get from a product that was wrapped in plastic. The seams of the lower half of the tent on the inside has what looks like a heat tape sealing. That gives me a bit of reassurance that no water will get through those seams. There is a nice sized mesh pocket and a lantern hook inside the tent. The screen does hinder some of the air flow because it is tight woven but that can really be a benefit. I was very comfortable moving around in the tent.
Taking the tent back down did take me a bit to do. I have weak hands but I did manage to get it done. I dont feel that would keep me from using this style tent. I feel like it would hold up well in a windy situation. It does come with four wind cords and 8 stakes.
Unfortunately there were a couple of small holes in the tent material. I contacted Hewolf Outdoors through Amazon. They responded same day, very quickly to resolve the issue. I will not tell the details of the resolve but I will say they are amazing. I am definitely going to be shopping for more items for my camping and backpacking supplies.

I reccomend this tent and this company!!

product_name: CAP Barbell Exercise Machine Attachments, Black
review_text:
It gets the job done. During The Great Gym Exodus of early 2020 (during the pandemic), I was lucky enough to have my own power rack at home. I had 45's 25's 10's, hella 5's, Olympic bar, a reliable folding bench and a LOT of time.

2 of the big 3 were fine:
bench press - the rack handled it
Squat / legs - the rack handled it

Back was lacking however, I can only do so many deadlift variations and pullups. Originally I had intended to fashion my own pulley system from home depot to hit back, but that was a lot of work. A landmine was the perfect choice.

I had screw-locked this onto the bottom of my power rack and so-

Negatives:
-The bar it comes with is flimsy, I was just careful with it, kept movements controlled. It feels like this part of the "package" was slapped on just so they could charge a little extra. If I could do it over I'd buy a separate one.
-The landmine itself is a bit loose, wiggles here and there when its altogether.
-There was an extra bit of formed metal on the bottom of cup where you would place the bar, this snagged on the ground whenever I lifted the bar to a 65 degree angle.

Positives
-Although the landmine itself is loose, the separate pieces held just fine. I check it after every session and the bolts stay in place. Just have to deal with a little side-side play which is not noticeable when I lift.
-screw clamp/lock kept it in place.
-Although there was a piece of metal hanging from under the cup, the slight snag is easily pushed over. You'll notice it at first but after that its easy to push over and you'll forget its there.
-It literally gets the job done exactly how it should.

In summation it works perfectly fine for any landmine-type motions. It isn't a slickly built, well oiled device, but it does everything I want it to without problems.

Worth it, try to get without the bar.

product_name: Cascade Mountain Tech Lightweight Aircraft-Grade Aluminum Trekking Poles with Extended Down Grip Plus Tip Kit
review_text:
Bought For One-Day Local Trail Hikes. Chose aluminum over carbon fiber because I read if a trekking pole is going to break (like, if it gets stuck in a crevice or something and you slip), carbon fiber will snap, but aluminum may only bend, and bend at a slow enough rate you might be able to save the pole. Or even, would be able to bend it back. Compared the weight difference with carbon fiber version, and these were not all that much heavier. But, I am only using them for local day hikes, so shock/vibration isn't too much of an issue, though I did choose cork handles because it is supposed to dampen shock/vibration. Also, I've used handles that are EVA foam, and when they get wet, I found it very gross as they absorb sweat and water.

The quick locks work well. I first locked one at the desired height, and leaned on it really hard. It sank a little, so I unlocked it, twisted the thumb screw about half a turn, then locked it again. Tested it again, and it held up nicely. Did the same for the second quick lock on the same pole, then of course, did the second pole. Didn't want to twist the thumb screw more than I needed to. May need to in the future though, the more I use them, so less is better in the beginning.

The included instructions describe an anti-shock feature, but this is not a part of their quick lock trekking poles. The instructions aren't very good. The trekking poles came with snow caps, mud/sand caps, and boot tips and rubber tips for hard surfaces. The boot tips and rubber tips just pull on and off, the snow caps and mud/sand caps screw on. As for adjusting the wrist strap, I pulled it as short as it could go, but wanted the strap to support my wrist, so pulling the one end of the strap as directed didn't allow it to be small enough. So I pulled both ends of the strap, and simply tied a basic knot with the two ends, to get them small enough. One end of the strap has a wedge attached that is supposed to lock into a hole, but, since I could not get it small enough, this end is hanging out of the hole with my knot.

review_text:
Claude Monet tires: they look great from a distance, but upon closer inspection, not so good. TL;DR - Terrible quality control. One tire is holding up great, the other is a puncture/tear magnet. Classic Claude Monet tires: look good from a distance, but upon closer inspection, not so good. The center tread is thin and does not hold up well.

Bought a set to go on some longer distance rides over pavement and bike paths. Set them up for a dry fit then tubeless with sealant and went for a test ride around the neighborhood to make sure everything was good. Let the tires sit overnight and the pressure dropped a little bit, which is normal. First ride, I put a little air in and went on my way. Rode from LA to SB on some smooth bike paths and roads and the rear tire must've picked something up and starting spewing out sealant. No worries. Normally, I would just use a plug, but I pulled over, patched what I could with a tire boot and put a tube in because I still had a ways to go and most of the sealant had spewed out. Further up the road, a different spot in the center tread tore and the tube was a goner. Luckily, I brought two tubes because I'm an overachiever like that. Swapped it out, and made it to SB before the turnaround. On the way down, guess what? Another flat in a DIFFERENT spot on the same tire. At this point, I patched what I could on the tube and made it back as far as I could before calling for a ride. 1 wrecked tire, 2 holey tubes, 3 empty CO2 canisters, and a terribly ride experience later, I'm looking for something else now.

review_text: Wonderful Hydration System. This "Mobihome" hydration backpack is wonderful! In the past, we had bought one for our youngest son, and he raved about his. So...I ordered this hydration backpack for myself. I go hiking in the Wyoming hills with my BFF occasionally and it seems I always run out of water before we get return. This backpack holds 2 liters of water so I have plenty for a day hike. Also there's these little rubber ice cubes you can put in the freezer the night before and have cold water all day. Just make sure the rubber ice cubes have no sharp edges. The bite value you pull up to open and push down to close. The water bag inside the backpack has a harder plastic handle that you slide off to expose the water bladder to fill it up or drain/clean. Make sure this water bladder is completely drained and dry before you close it again or you could have mold next time. There are additional zipper pockets for cell phones, bandages, anti-bacterial cream, bug repellent, an extra pair of clean socks and shorts/pants, and your breakfast and/or lunch. Perfect for a day hike. The main storage area at first was difficult for me to find as it sits inside an oval shaped fabric trim. Plenty of room in their for clothing and/or lunch, beef jerky, and any snacks you bring along with you. There's also braided elastic bungee cords on the back that you could use to hold a small blanket or an extra pair of shoes and even a small tent. It does unhook so you can tie your item down. Each side has mesh pockets. I usually put canned/bottled pop in mine but others like to take along a can/bottle of beer. There's a yellow rainproof cover to keep everything dry. The shoulder straps are nice and large with an orange snap closure. And there's a black snap closure strap for around your waist. This lightweight backpack fits snug to your body and if it wasn't for the weight of the water, you'd probably not even notice you had it on. I hope to get more hikes in this summer. However, it's already getting pretty hot even in the mornings. So next time we'll need to find a place to hike that has lots of tree's for shade. This hydration backpack is holding up very well.

review_text:
Uncomfortable (sadly) + PVC?. I'm so bummed this pack isn't going to work for me. I purchased the Luminous Green color, to use on walks. It is SO cool-looking, I think the pictures represent it well but it's still exciting to experience it in person. I actually scrapped the bladder idea and tried it on with two full 24 and 27 oz water bottles in it. By some magic I couldn't feel their weight! I can only compare it to one other pack I've tried, but it's a night and day difference with that one.

So... the problems are: the shoulder strap buckles hit me right in the soft area by my armpits. It hurts. And given that this bag is made of some kind of vinyl or something, the straps themselves are stiff and that also causes discomfort. Now, the description says the BLADDER is PVC-free, but I think the pack might be made of PVC. It does off-gas, and since I was planning to use it to walk in the summer sun, that would make it worse. I could even smell it faintly hanging on the chair 10 feet away from my bed. Smell or not, if you're concerned about toxins, you might want to pass on this.

Finally, the sternum strap is too short if you're an above-average-chested woman. I was willing to replace it, but I was already over-budget on this bag by like $20, just cuz it really did look so much cooler than all the other ones
on Amazon and once I saw it, I didn't want to settle for less!

Dang it!

review_text: Lifesavers during the first trimester. My wife and I are pregnant with our first child. During the first trimester, she struggled with morning sickness (honestly sickness all throughout the day) quite a bit. Especially when she would wake up. But also when she would see one of her food aversions, smell something that made her queasy, or sometimes just while sitting on the couch for no reason at all. These little lifesavers were awesome! She kept a couple in her purse, and in her pockets when she didn't have the purse and would pop one in at the first sign of nausea. They really lessened the severity of most of her episodes, if not staved them off completely on several occasions. The ginger flavor was evident, but not as strong as she was expecting and more than tolerable. She actually doesn't like ginger flavored things, but the creamy texture and natural flavoring toned it down plenty. I would highly recommend these to any woman that is considering trying them for nausea related to pregnancy just based on my wife's praises of them.

review_text: I would recommend this bike rack. What I like about this bike rack is that it can handle wider handlebars than almost all of the other racks. I also like its clean design and simplicity. It also seems sufficiently sturdy. How could it improve? Two ways: 1. Its mounting bracket assumes you put three screws into the side of a 2x4 stud, which requires perfect alignment - easier said than done when the stud is hidden behind drywall and you need almost 2" of wood. But as most people know, a "2X4" isn't really 2" wide, it's more like 1 and 3/4th" wide, so its very likely that not all 3 screws will find good wood in the side of one hidden 2X4. Also, the rubber cushions for the bike frame have sort of multiple fingers, I assume so as to work with a multiple of frame widths. Sounds good in theory, but I found them problematic when trying to lift and properly place a bike onto the frame, since the fingers kind of get in the way and challenge your ideal placement. I think a simpler U shaped rubber cushion design would work better. All that said, after researching this rack and several competing products, I still think this is the best one, especially for wider bikes. I bought 2 of them and would not hesitate to buy another should I ever add a 3rd bike.

product_name: Volt Saddle
review_text:
Saddle Up & Ride!. I’ve now had a little over a month to ride w/the WTB Volt Narrow Steel Black Saddle (W065-0584). I decided to upgrade my 12 year old stock Bontrager saddle. I decided to go w/the steel because of price & have never purchased or ride w/any WTB saddle. I went to the WTB website & used there tool to enter my physical information to determine which size saddle best fit me.

My first impression when I received the saddle was that it looked great & well made. The all black microfiber cover looks sharp, especially w/the subtle imposed logo. There were no issues w/stitching or construction.

While riding, I immediately noticed I was more stable in the saddle, especially when putting down power. When I hit the steeper hills & really started power spinning up it, I was much more comfortable in the Volt than I was in my old saddle. So far I have not had any issues w/a sore butt or any discomfort due to the saddle. I’ve ridden on rides as long as 2+ hours, on double, single & downhill.

Overall I’m very happy w/the WTB Volt. As long as it holds up, I’d have no issues w/spending more on one of the more expensive saddles made w/the lighter rails (cromoly or titanium, prob not carbon for $200+).

Thank you for taking the time to read my review, I hope you found it helpful.

review_text:
Too large with no adjustment. I have a number of boonie hats but liked the concept of the BUILTCOOL Adult Bucket Cap with Neck Shade – Boonie Hat, One Size. I really wanted to love this one. The material is soft and it looks great. However, the hat is just too big. All of the other hats I have fit great so I believe I have farily regular-sized head. This hat slides down over my ears with room to spare. Other reviewers pointed this out but I assumed it would be okay. I was wrong. All of my other boonie hats have an elastic drawcord above the brim that allow you to adjust the size if needed. Ironically, I never need it on those hats. Not having an adjust cord is a a major design flaw for this hat. If it did have one, I would rate this a 5 instead of a 1. As it stands, the hat is largely unwearable and I assume the company will eventually fix this flawed hat. I would wait until a new version is out.

UPDATE: I reached out to the seller and it seems they are aware the fit is not good and actually confirmed they are working on a new version. Their quote - "We are working with our design team and we anticipate adding a new smaller size to this product for 2021."

It is dissapointing they are still selling this version.

review_text:
the best of two. I have a 1.75 cobra belt with a V-ring. It's big and clunky. The velcro hooks on it has flaked off over time so the excess no longer holds. Here's a photo of my 1.75 cobra belt for comparison.
I have one these 1.5 belts with the same quick clamp buckle. Though it is missing the V-ring. This belt is a combo of those two.

This one is not as as wide and is much more relaxed than the stiff 1.75. It also relies on a clamp style buckle instead of a ladder lock buckle. And it uses an elastic loop instead of the hook pile velcro to secure the excess.
Its much easier to get on. Unfortunately, the loop for the excess is loose. It slides every where. It might be good to sew it in place. I just took it off all together. I had a few inches of excess that I trimmed and burned.

The V-ring is smaller on the 1.5 and will actually slide through a belt loop. So centering the buckle is possible with this belt versus the 1.75 where that larger V-ring made it impossible.
That beings said, I would NOT use this V-Ring for rigging. The belt material is looped back one inch behind the ring and sewn with a single box X stitch. Whereas my heavy duty cobra belt was double backed the entire length of the belt. Which also account for the stiffness. That belt could stand up all by itself.

Overall, a nice light duty belt. I've made it my every day wear belt and have put the other two in storage. I'll wear the 1.75 for out in the boonies and this 1.5 for the rear.

product_name: MSR Zoic 1-Person Lightweight Mesh Backpacking Tent with Rainfly
review_text:
Nice tent, but questions about waterproof. Edit on 10 August, 2020. I seam sealed this tent after my June section hike, then took it on a 41-mile hike on the Appalachian Trail in The Smoky Mountains. On night one, I again encountered heavy rain. This time, droplets only appeared at the top of the rain fly, which I noticed because they dripped on the netting at the door of the main body tent. I did not notice any other moisture. It appears the seam seal helped, which I learned how to do by following a video provided on the MSR website. I still like this tent, and will maybe pursue other sealing improvements on the rain fly. But I'm not going to upgrade it to 4 stars or higher until MSR contacts me.

Edit on 14 July, 2020. I took this tent on a two-night section hike on the Appalachian Trail, at the end of June. Droplets are still forming on the inside during rain, and fairly quickly. Further, when there was a particularly hard downpour during a rainstorm I encountered, I could feel mist on my face. I have emailed the company twice and I await a response. If MSR is reading this, my case number is 00049517. I really don't want to return this tent. I'd rather have advice on how to seal the rain fly. I intend to seem seal it soon, as I plan a long section in the Smokies in less than two weeks.

Original Review

I've taken this tent on two trips. I like this tent. Easy to setup, and lightweight as advertised. It has some nice things inside; pockets, and places to hang a light. Even two gear storages up top.

I want to give it five stars, but I need to resolve a water issue.

The second trip we base camped for three nights (6/15/2020 to 6/18/2020). I just returned. On day two it rained all day; one of those soaking rains. I was not in the tent the whole day. When I returned there was a good amount of moisture inside the rainfly.

This is what I just wrote to MSR. I am hoping for a response:

"I just used my Zoic 1 backpacking tent for three nights. We were base camping at the Mt. Rogers National Recreation area the past few days, and it rained a lot. On the 2nd day, when we had experienced a particularly soaking rain, I came back to notice a few water droplets inside the rainfly. There was maybe 3 or 4 water smears on the netting of the main tent.

I gingerly wiped those off, and I remained dry that night and the next day. So no major issues. I'm mostly wondering if this is normal. I mean, I was NOT in the tent, so my body heat did not produce moisture inside. It appeared as if the water was slightly seeping through the rainfly. I can tell you that the vestibule was very wet on this inside.
Thoughts?"

Though I have backpacked a lot, I am no expert on tents. So maybe what I experienced is normal. After all, I did not get wet.

review_text:
My neti pot is going to be gathering dust. Generally speaking, I've been happy with my neti pot, but it's not something I can take with me when we travel or camp. This looked as if it might be a good alternative, and I believe that it is. Being plastic, it's not going to break. I didn't realize that I was going to love that I can close the nasal applicator tip and shake it up to make sure I dissolve the salt, but I do. Having used a neti pot for a very long time, I was also surprised by how much easier and more comfortable it is not to have to lean way over in order to have the solution flow through my nasal passages – I'd just gotten used to doing it. Being able to squeeze the bottle also allows for changing how fast it flows in. Being able to see how much is still in the bottle, so that I can stop halfway, and switch sides is also extremely helpful! The only thing it doesn't have, which I wish it did, is a stand to hold the bottle upside down when drying it.

The salt packets are hard to empty, as the slit for opening them is badly placed: lengthwise, and in the middle, so they just tear down the middle, leaving a pocket on both sides which is hard to empty by pouring (as a nurse, I'm not going to stick it in the bottle and shake it, for sanitary reasons).

This is definitely a keeper!

review_text:
Decent Resistance Bands With a Couple Issues. For the most part these are good. I followed the recommended workout on the pamphlet. It was 3 rounds of 6 exercises 40 sec. work, 20 sec rest (I did 4 rounds). No problem going through the first 4 in the recommended time. However, I would need another anchor and set of handles to be able to get through the workout uninterrupted. 4 of the exercises (squat, overhead press, calf raise, squat again) I used my feet to anchor the bands - no problem.

To avoid switching bands, I just left two of them connected and switched back and forth. 2 exercises (triceps and ab rotation) used the door anchor. However, they use different positions on the door. So having 20 seconds to move the anchor, reattach the band, and then connect the handles was not enough time. I would probably do this routine in the future as rep count vs. timed exercise to allow the appropriate time for transitions. On the overhead press I also noticed the bands rubbed a lot on my upper arms. Not a big deal, I'd probably just wear a longer sleeve shirt the next time.

I also noticed the directions below and the graphics do not match. See photo and you will notice the discrepancy.

Ultimately there are many options for resistance bands. The biggest thing to look out for is quality. Lower quality bands and accessories can lead to some injury for sure. These seem to be of good quality, so there's enough there to recommend these.

It's definitely like a 'hugging' feeling but in a comfortable way. On to my first wear: I am 5'11 160lbs (not super thick in any particular way, but the height was a worry for me)... I bought size Large in both the top and bottom & fits pretty exact to me. Just as a side note, I usually am between M-L and L was a way better option for me. I wore the suit with a sports bra, a waist trimmer underneath, and was comfortable until about 10 min when I felt a type of 'tickle' after doing a brisk walk/run around my neighborhood. It was the sweat dripping out of the suit... seriously. I don't think I've ever sweat so fast or so much by simply combining a walk/run together for 10 min. I continued this alternating walk/run and within 30 min my sleeves were dripping on my hands (sweat), and my leg openings- the same thing.
Thoughts: if it does nothing else, I promise you- wear it for 10-15 min walking/moving/running/whatever, and you'll start feeling the sweat. What I'm unsure about? The care of the item once worn is kind of tricky- it says to wash separately and for only a minimal period of time, etc. I inside-out my outfit and hung to dry. Most likely will wear 2x a week before washing, then hang to dry- Overall, after one use, I see what they mean by 'sauna suit' and I can definitely see how this would make anyone sweat more, faster, and lose more weight. If you have $45-50 bux, go up a size and give it a try!

product_name: Walker's Razor Slim
review_text:
Early Review: First Impressions. The things I was curious about before buying these:
A) How they sound.
B) How they feel.
C) Compared to Howard Leights by Honeywell as well as the BT edition of the Walker Razor.

I have not tested the Noise Cancellation yet but provided it works as it should I wanted to get out my review in case anyone wondered what I did. My hand's on impressions have been fully positive.
If you get these and wonder how to open the package: I just bent the package in half. This caused the cardboard to split open and the plastic clamshell is not sealed - it is 2 parts and the headphones came out super simple.

How do they sound? (I own Sennheiser HD600 compared to those:)
A)Surprisingly good. Not audiophile but not bad.
B)Bass is light. Not much bass from these. Bass seems purposely reserved, truth be told probably neutral.
C)Slight emphasis on mid-range. But not annoying in any frequency.
D)Highs are present but not pristine.
E)Overall, they sound good for a $43 set of headphones that do so much more. I am pleased with it. I can listen without irritation.

How do they feel?
A) A little tight on my medium-sized head but the muffs are plushy and do a good job of distributing the clamp pressure.
B) I can't imagine wearing these for much more than an hour at a time but it might be ok for longer but probably no one will actually want to.
C) Headband doesn't rub my scalp.
D) No hair pulling or "pinchy parts".
E) The hinges that hold the muffs look thin but they work (so far). Durability could be a concern.
F) The hinges are adjustable. I collapsed then down about 2/5ths of the way so they could possibly fit larger heads but wider heads may have more clamp pressure?
G) Again, the clamp pressure is pretty tight. I am surprised how tight they are. But they stay on the head when moving my head which is good. It is a good thing they are tight but it could cause them to fatigue your head after a while. Be aware they are pretty tight on the head but I don't believe it will be a deal-breaker.

How is the enhanced hearing:
A) Fairly natural. I can rather accurately distinguish sounds.
B) I never knew what a bee flying sounded like other than Bumblebees right in my ear. I heard the bee and I will learn that sound but I wouldn't have known what it was had I not seen the bee and heard the sound.
C) You will discover new sounds you haven't heard before.
D) Unfortunately, the sound is mono-sounding like everyone has said. Determining the origin or placement of noises does not work out so well.
E) I questioned whether to get these or the Howard Leight by Honeywell. I decided to try these first after listening to YouTube videos. I have read reviews that say the "Howard's" better determine which direction noises come from but some videos said they do not do it better enough to choose them over these.
F) These are supposedly more comfortable than the Howard Leights.
G) They are cheaper and look better IMO than the Howard Leights.
H) I might buy the Howard Leights just to see if the sound placement is better because I think that would be a big deal but from what I have read and heard the hype may or may not be all it is cracked up to be. The reviewers mostly chose these over the Howard Leight.

Overall, I am impressed that these are only $43.
Be sure to get a 3.5mm to 3.5mm male to male wire to use them for music.
I wanted to get the Bluetooth version but after reading how much problems people were having with the BT dropping or not working, I decided to get the wired version.
The BT version has 4 mics which, on paper, seems would give better awareness of surroundings but from things I heard it didn't quite work as well in RL as it seems it would.
