review_text:
Large, well thought out. I picked this one over others because it is lightweight so better for summer and because you can unzip it from both sides. I'm claustraphobic and the temperature affects my sleep a lot so I didn't want a sleeping bag that was too hot since my husband gives off a lot of body heat, and our dog will probably sleep in it too especially if I'm cold. I'll bring a lightweight blanket too in case I get too hot. It's big and we're using it for short backpacking camping but instead of buying small individual things we bought couple things, so it doesn't really matter that it takes up my entire pack. That's what I tell myself anyways ;) I was considering buying a heavier couples bag for colder weather also but I read they take up a lot more space and I don't have more space. I'll update after I use it a few times.

Update:
I've used it twice and it's pretty good for my purposes and the price. I wasn't sure if my husband would like camping so we bought cheap things at first which were very heavy. We slept in it in a very cold night in the mountains in the summer, I think it might have gotten below 30 and I had on warm clothes and a small blanket and I was perfect. We used it again at a lower place in the mountains with the dog and that night I was too hot with my husband and dog in the bed. We also bought a normal air mattress and that with the tent and this sleeping bag made our packs a little too heavy. This year I am going to buy expensive light weight blow up pads to reduce our weight but we are going to keep this sleeping bag instead of replacing it with a lighter one because we are going to be moving somewhere warmer and it doesn't really make a lot of sense to invest in a warmer sleeping bag and we don't have many backpacking adventures planned to where it makes sense to invest in a more backpacking friendly sleeping bag. My husband said he is happy to shoulder the extra 3 lbs to save money so. So for us this is definitely a 5 star bag at this price point. I do dream of a nicer fancier less heavy sleeping bag but they are really expensive.

Good strap, weights aren't too hard to insert, absorbs sweat. I have a 6 1/2" wrist. I have fibro, osteoporosis, and body wide neuropathy so exercise is challenging. With the pool closed from Covid-19, I needed some way to exercise. My physical therapist suggested adjustable (1 - 2 lbs) wrist and ankle weights to wear around the house. These will work great. I have to have one weight inserted to be able to get the velcro through the D ring (it's covered up by the other end of the wrap). Since the wrap doesn't have any extra weight to it, I need a weight in it anyway. The velcro doesn't rub on my skin and the material soaks up any sweat.

The weights aren't very hard to put back in. I put the middle ones in first only because it appears to give me more room for my hands to get the rest of the weights in. It does take some pushing and jiggling to get them in their pouch but it isn't too hard.

Since they barely fit my wrists, these are a standard product so they get an average amount of stars.

I looked around at a lot of YouTube breakdowns of drivers, researched a lot of online pga pros, and read what I could find for about 2 months and all of that led me straight to this driver.

This driver out of the box has a great feel I was coming from a box set driver that had a stiff shaft and huge face that was adequate but really made golf not so fun when I just sliced into the woods most holes.

I have tested this thing out and I can say it may be the lighter helium HST 50 shaft suits my swing speed (slower) than the driver I used previously, but this thing feels great! Sound is on par with any driver you’ll find. The milled face intrigued me as it was unique to any products I had researched. This may have been an impulse buy but I can see myself using this for 10 years easily. Golf tech is relatively the same so getting a driver like this at the price gives a weekend hack the tool he needs to get the job done and enjoy it in style. I love the style too. A lot of golf purists don’t like the yellow but I like the freshness of it.

You get in this package:

Weights (attached already) , leather cobra head cover , adjustment tool to change weights and degrees, and driver of course. Also there is a sensor that tracks your drives through an app called ARCCOS (cobra connect) that is built in to the top of the club which if you are trying to stat. track could be a plus as it is a free service and is already attached to the club upon delivery. I am so happy I decided to finally buy this club.

I only heard one quarrel about this club from a guy at the range who said the carbon material on the club face around it’s edges CAN SOMETIMES chip if you hit it just right but this is MERELY COSMETIC as a flaw and does not effect performance according to a PGA guy he inquired with.

review_text:
Frame rusting and net sagging after a month, misleading customer service. First, the good: my daughter loves the net, we've had a lot of fun playing badminton and volleyball as a family. The portability of the net is great as well for when you want to take on the road with you, to a friends house or even the beach.

The bad:

1. Frame rusting: As seen in the pictures, the frame is already rusting at its connection points. We do not leave the frame and net outside in the rain or when the sprinklers are on. I'm going to have to wire brush and rustoleum spray each connection point now.

2. Net sagging: The net is already beginning to sag. I'm not sure if it's the elastic in the net itself or the bungie cord that runs through the frame. Either way, I'm not sure how upright this net is going to be next summer.

3. Customer Service: The shipping and delivery date for my first attempt at ordering the net came and went. Boulder's customer service people told me that they were having trouble processing my credit card and that was the reason for the delay. I've been a Prime member forever and have never had a credit card issue, in fact the other two items I ordered from another vendor when I purchased the net (a volleyball and badminton racket set) came, so something was off. I double checked with my credit card company and they didn't see any attempt at a charge, nor did Amazon.

Just to try, I cancelled my original order and placed a new order under a new credit card, but now the net was backordered (ugh). I checked back a few days later and noticed that Boulder was accepting orders again which meant the item was back in stock. For a second time, my shipping and delivery date came and went. I reached out to Boulder again, and again was told that they were having trouble with my credit card. The next day, I received a shipping confirmation from Amazon, however according to Boulder, they were still having trouble processing my card. The net ended up coming, however Boulder had no idea apparently.

My take on this is that Boulder was likely overwhelmed with orders due and manufacturing delays due to covid and they were blaming my credit card. I get it, I live in NY and understand how crazy things were a couple of months ago, but just be honest, people are reasonable and understanding, it's just a net. I just didn't appreciate the confusing messages from their customer service team.

The cot seems well built and is wonderfully light weight. So it would be good for smaller people. product_name: Volt Saddle
review_text:
Relatively comfortable. I guess that the Volt is sort of a modernized replacement for the Rocket V, which has been my favorite for years.

I'm using the narrowest Volt on a track stand bicycle, for riding Zwift. It's more narrow than the WTB web site tool recommended. It is a little different from the Rocket -- thinner, with more modern styling. The Volt with metal rails is a good value, since at this writing the lighter rail options have marginal reductions in weight.

Comfort depends a great deal on how your hip bones are shaped and how long you'll be in the saddle. All I can suggest is what I did: buy the cheap one and try it out. If you think you might be sending it back, put one wrap of plastic tape around where you'll attach it to the clamp, and cover the seat temporarily with a plastic bag. That should preserve its like-new condition.

I still have an older, relatively heavy Rocket V on the bike I ride outdoors. It's probably more comfortable on longer rides.

product_name: Yogitoes Manduka Yoga Towel for Mat, Non-Slip and Quick Dry for Hot Yoga with Rubber Bottom Grip Dots, 68 Inch Long, Thin and Lightweight
review_text:
Works ok, overpriced. This is the gold-standard for hot yoga towels, thanks to the silicone grips. I've seen this used in multiple studios across the country.
I'll start with the pros:
- It grips the mat better than other towels I've tried, and the towel stays put most of the time. You will still be readjusting and straightening it throughout class, though. Probably 4-6 times in a 75-minute class.
- DURABLE. It's machine washable and very durable. At my studio, we have towels that have been used and washed up to 3 times per day for years and they're still not showing any sign of wear.

Cons/Critiques:
- It's definitely overpriced for what you're getting.
- It's very skinny and barely reaches the edges of a regular-sized matt, let alone a wide mat.
- It will hold a decent amount of sweat, and it does actually get grippier the wetter it gets, but only up to a point. For me, usually 40 minutes into a hot class, it's gotten so wet it loses the grip and I just put a regular hand towel on top to help me stay in down-dog.

Tips:
- definitely spritz down the mat before you lay your matt down, then the top of the towel before practicing. A little moisture actually improves the grip.
- Avoid putting it in the dryer. Sometimes our studio towels do end up going through the dryer and they're still fine, but this probably degrades the towel over time.

Overall, it's decent and performs better than any mat on its own (I've tried every "hot yoga" mat there is, and none of them stay grippy throughout a hot class, so I think a towel is just required). However, it's not stellar. But I don't know if there is anything better out there, so this seems to be the best for now.

3.5 stars

It managed to eeek out enough lift to be useful, but I had to do the rest of the lifting. The battery display should give me an idea if the battery is low. Also, the charger should be powerful enough to either fast-charge the unit, or power the system while running, so that, in a pinch, the user can plug it in and get full performance.

On my tracker, none of these are or do. Heartbeat will finally settle down to a good measurement, after reopening the screen several times but it takes far too long. It's all over the place at first. Forget the sleep time; it is so far off as to be laughable. (No I don't sleep 14 hours a day! LOL I'm usually only in bed about 7 hours and it takes me a while to fall asleep. No naps at all.) The Alexa function is so unreliable as to be almost useless. Who wants to try six times to get it to finally do the simplest thing?

I'm hoping future firmware updates will fix these problems, so I'm not going to take the trouble to return it. I have an ancient Fitbit Charge HR that is still much more reliable and accurate, but of course it has limited functions compared to the newer ones.. I just bought a Fitbit Inspire HR but have only had it a day. Today I'm having problems getting it to sync with my iPhone and Fire tablet, but it synced fine yesterday. The measurements seem more accurate. I wore it and the Wyze tracker all night.

UPDATE RE FITBIT: After using it a few weeks, the Fitbit data seems accurate, BUT it is terrible at connecting via Bluetooth and at syncing. It will only sync when Fitbit decides it can, sometimes not even once a day. I've done all the suggested trouble-shooting steps without improvement. This is a common problem on the Fitbit website community. If Fitbit could learn Wyze's syncing method, and Wyze could learn Fitbit's sleep and HR accuracy, there would be two great trackers!

Yesterday I took a 20-minute walk wearing both of my new trackers, with the ancient FB Charge HR in my pocket. The old FB counted the most steps, the new FB the next, and the Wyze the fewest, but the difference from most to least was only 146 steps so that may be okay. The awful sleep counter is a deal breaker for me at present, though. This tracker must think anytime I'm still I'm asleep. The HR and Alexa functions are also frustrating, as they are important for me. Hoping for better performance in the future. Also, the screens in the Wyze phone app are very difficult to read as many have complained (some blue on blue tiny text, etc). The Fitbit phone app is much, much better--IF you can get it to sync.

If yours works better than mine you'll probably love it. It may be well worth a try at its low price. It is lightweight and comfortable; the tracker's screen is very nice and the battery life is good so far. I love the features (if they were accurate and/or worked consistently). The band allows it to fit wrists of many sizes including very small wrists. And it does reliably sync! Firmware updates could make an improvement in its accuracy later, hopefully.

review_text:
Not like conventional belts (!). Some people are dinging this belt in the reviews because they don't understand the correct method of using this belt (and I get it, as I didn't understand it either before I watched the manufacturer's how-to video). This belt is not like conventional belts. It is not, and is not intended to be, fastened and unfastened the same way you use a normal belt. With this belt, you fasten and unfasten it one way to open and close your pants and another, different way to move the belt from one pair of pants to another. To open and close your pants, you separate the two parts of the buckle with the quick release (which is this belt's entire advantage over conventional belts); to move the belt from one pair of pants to another, however, you leave the two parts of the buckle fastened together and flip open the *other* latch at the right end of the buckle assembly to pull the end of the belt out of the buckle assembly altogether, whereupon you wind up with the normal-style belt-with-a-buckle-at-one-end which you can thread through belt loops with no problem.

As mentioned above, I had a bit of a time grasping the correct method of using this belt at first too (because I hadn't watched the video or read any instructions), but when I found moving the belt from one pair of pants to another to be well-nigh impossible, I thought, "this *cannot* be how you're supposed to use this thing" and watched the instructional video...whereupon all was made clear and I've been a fan of this belt ever since. The quick-release used to open and close your pants is fantastic (though the process of moving the belt from one pair of pants to another could be somewhat streamlined...even if, like the manufacturer, I'm not sure exactly how that would be done).

The one nuisance about this belt's design is the elastic loop used to hold down the end of the belt after you've put it on. The loop is necessary (unless you tuck the end of the belt under the belt rather than folding it back over on top, but that's even more awkward than using the loop), but it's fairly small, it's a separate piece from the belt, it usually gets pulled off the belt by your belt loops when you remove the belt from a pair of pants, and if you forget about it at this time you could easily lose it (I have two of these belts, each a different color, and switching between these two belts allowed me to forget about the loop such that I unexpectedly found one on my bed about a day after I'd switched belts). So I wish there was a better solution to the issue of holding down the end of the belt.

But other than that, I like the belt a lot, and I appreciate it all over again every time I open or close my pants, which is what this belt makes so much easier than it is with a conventional belt.

review_text:
Team Cooler Does Its Job. Received this item as a review product.

Don't mind the Pat's logo. I believe you can select your own team, so having Pat's logo should not be a negative factor.

The cooler has canvas like texture outside with two exterior pockets. The cooler is a soft cooler, with perhaps 1/2 inch thick insulation. The cooler arrived partially folded, just to give you an idea of its softness.

The capacity does have room for 24 cans but the weight of 24 cans may potentially cause product to fail around the top handle area or where shoulder strap attaches to the cooler. But carrying a few cans and bottles of drink, should not be an issue.

To test how well the cooler works under a moderate heat environment, I partially filled the cooler with a large bottle of frozen water, three cans of refrigerated carbonated water, one smaller water bottle and an ice pack and left the cooler outside over night. The ambient temperature was between ~76F to 82F over night - it is summer in TX. In the morning, I checked the contents - the large water bottle still had a large ice core left and approximately 50% have melted. All the drinkers were cold. The ice pack was cold to touch but was completely melted. I can see this cooler being perfect for kids soccer or baseball games or day trip to nature.

Overall the cooler did what it is supposed to do - kept the contents cold/cool for a desired period of time.

Add me to the mold issue people. I bought 3 new caps last year to use across 2 bottles. I wash them frequently by hand and still need to drag qtips through the crevices. As noted by others, at times mold will develop on the seal in the flip top and it's nearly impossible to get out then. Nalgene recommends soaking in bleach for a few hours

I just bought one new one just now (because I didn't like the other colors available). The bright green is pretty muted in real life

Nalgene as told me they don't have a store on Amazon, so I wonder if these are counterfeits.

I am trying to find out if there should be a seal on the part that touches the bottle. Mine have never had seals and leak there often

My first cap WAS defective in that it was hard to open. The new ones were much better.

.....

July 2021: Slight update after a year. I still use this pretty exclusively for bike riding. I have not had mold issues like some others have. But I am buying another to replace the cap on my Camelbak Chute Mag which creates an incredible amount of mold quickly.

*****

I bought this to put on a 20oz Camelbak bottle for bike riding. I find it's difficult to thread on so that it doesn't leak, which I still need to test with the original Camelbak top to see if the bottle is the problem.

But what is definitely a cap problem is the fact that it's incredibly hard to push the button to open it and even harder to push it closed again. Not the one handed while on the move operation I was hoping for.

review_text:
When used correctly, it works well and lasts a long time.. The cooler holds up well when used properly. I've used it for many years. It has been on every vacation. I think plugging it in and out a lot is not good for the Peltier. I usually leave it plugged in for over a week at a time. It does get unplugged from the car when on vacation, but usually gets plugged in right away in a hotel. I've left it plugged into the car and left running for hours and the car started just fine.

I even used as a beer cooler continuously for over a year. It got too cold once and froze a bottle of beer. Maybe a 45 degree garage is too cold.

I live in a cool dry climate, but it still frosts up. It needs to be defrosted once in a while. This is easy. Just unplug overnight and wipe up the moisture in the morning.

The vent needs to have free airflow with no obstructions. If shoved up against a seat on a trip, don't expect it to work well.

It only cools to about 40 degrees less than ambient. Where I live, it rarely gets to 90, so it works well. Dont expect it to cool much outside in an area like Florida or the low desert in Arizona in the summer. Try moving it indoors to cool effectively in hot climates.

product_name: SUUNTO 3 Fitness Tracker Sports Watch
review_text:
Great fitness tracking app, especially as a kayaker. I have a 3rd generation Apple watch and have long been frustrated by its inability to track my kayak paddles. Enter the Suunto 3, it has a built in option for kayaking which is great. I was excited just to be able to track the distance of my kayak paddles without paying for a 3rd party iPhone app, but the data collected by the Suunto system absolutely blew me away.

Not only did it track distance, heartrate, and speed over time, but it also tracked my cadence which was very interesting to see. The free app works phenomenally and makes it very easy to review your data. My favorite part is that it will show me the path I followed overlaid on a map which is very nice to see for something like kayaking or hiking. Graphs alongside the map show things like heartrate/speed over time so you can see what your heartrate/speed was at each point along your path on the map. In the app, you can even add comments and photos you took so they are tied to the workout which I thought was super cool.

Additionally, I was able to set up a custom watch display specifically for kayaking workouts and could tailor the information displayed specifically to what I was interested. For me this was the icing on the cake; not only could I see in-depth information after my kayak paddle, but I could see nearly as much as I wanted in real time. I could see not only my elapsed time, heart rate, and distance traveled (which I would expect to be able to see) but I could also have it display my cadence, current speed, average speed.

As a fairly serious kayaker, the native tracking functions of this watch blew away any 3rd party cell phone app that I'd otherwise have to spend money on a yearly subscription with.

I only have a couple complaints with the watch and they are minor:
1. On one of my paddles, the detected heart rate for the first roughly 30 minutes was ~55bpm when in reality I was probably at least double that. The watch was on fairly snug so I'm not sure what the issue was, and that issue didn't occur regularly, but it was odd.
2. Learning which buttons do what was a bit of a task as they're not labeled at all. With time it is improving but it's not the most intuitive compared to some of the "dumb" watches I have used on the past for timing sprints/intervals.
3. My kayak paddles on flat water often seem to think I gained/lost upwards of 20 feet of elevation over the course of my paddle. I assume this is a product of the variation in my phone's GPS readings but it was still a bit odd to see such a drastic elevation plot for a flat kayak ride.

The battery lasts an impressively long time, much better than most smart watches I've used. The day-to-day tracking (steps, calories, etc) was comparable to my Apple Watch 3 for the few days where I wore both. The numbers weren't identical (and I wouldn't expect them to be) but they were within the ballpark of each other which is what I would have hoped for.

All-in-all, I'd recommend this watch if you're looking for fitness tracking. The tracking is good and the mobile app is amazing.

product_name: Rain Fly by NoCry 10x10 Lightweight Survival Camping Tarp; 100% Waterproof; Makes a Great Backpacking Tarp or Hammock Shelter; Comes in Multiple Colors, Survival Bracelet Included; Black
review_text:
UPDATED AFTER USING. And a mention about customer service. HERE IS MY UPDATED REVIEW:

I really wanted to love this tarp. And I did on one sunny camping trip. The color is nice, it didnt stretch at all during the night. It is lighter than my other tarp by a couple ounces. While longer it doesnt actually give more coverage though because of the way it is cut. I am planning an AT hike soon and felt I needed to rain test this. So tonight we got a nice heavy rain coming it so I set it up in the backyard. After 4 hours I went outside and it leaks. A LOT! There was some leakage from the middle seam but most of it was just coming through the fabric! Some water was running down the tarp and some was collecting and dripping down to where I would be sleeping. See photos. I had a couple plastic lawn chairs under the tarp, in case we just wanted to hang out and they both were splattered with quite a bit of water. Good thing I tested it first! Unfortunately I cant get my money back as its been too long. HOWEVER, I did email the seller about the tarp leaking and they emailed back within a day! About 10 days later I had a replacement tarp! Customer service is OUTSTANDING! As for the replacement tarp, I will rain test it as soon as I get a chance and will update.

UPDATED AFTER RAIN TEST:
I tested the replacement tarp in 2 thunderstorms. While it did not leak as much as the first one, some water did come in. A light misty rain may be ok for this tarp, but in a heavy downpour you MAY get wet.
Sorry guys, really wanted to love it, but a few drops will still soak your gear given enough time. Just cannot trust this tarp to keep me dry.

ORIGINAL REVIEW FOLLOWS:
I really wanted one of those $200 tarps. But I just cant afford it. So a friend said that if you shop wisely you can get a $50 tarp and turn it into a $200 tarp. I have done this with some other tarps but they were all advertised as 10x10 and when you get them they are really 9.5x9.5. When I decided I wanted a 12 foot tarp I bought this one.

Just a few things. It seems thin, but this isnt necessarily a bad thing. Since I havent used it I cannot attest to its durability. The sewing job seems nicely done, however a couple of the grommets were off center a little. The center seam IS taped on the inside. BUT...READ ON...

A couple things I want to point out, to the manufacturer as well, to make this a 5 start tarp:
1. Get rid of the grommets. It only adds weight and when rolled up in a backpack the movement of them rubbing on the tarp can cause holes over time. They also take away from the waterproof area as they let water in. Loops are WAY better.

2. Put waterproof tape on the upper side of the tarp. When taped on the inside, if you use a complete ridge line the rope rubbing on the tarp will rub off the "tape" over time. Better to have the tape on the top, or just connect the ridge line to each corner (from corner to tree on each end) rather than continuous line under the tarp.

3. The ridgeline corners need to be taped too (see photo). Where this has been sewn is 6 inches in, so that takes a full foot off your waterproofness under the tarp. So these need to be sealed too.

Just another point. The camo color isnt quite as shown. There is A LOT more tan patches on the tarp I got. Maybe that doesnt matter to some, but it did matter to me. I wanted more greenage.
Carabiners are cool but you are better of learning a couple quick tie and quick release knots. The survival bracelet is...ummm....well, the ferro rod wouldnt produce ANY spark, but the compass points north, most of the time. I may use the lines, but they seem pretty thin.

product_category: Cell Phones & Accessories | Activity & Fitness Trackers
review_text:
AMAZING watch!!!. I decided to try this watch because I'd had such bad luck with my Fitbit Versa. I bought the Versa when it first premiered, and over the last few years, the company had to replace it 2 times because it failed...and the second time they gave me a really hard time about it. I always take great care of my things, especially something as expensive as a Versa. But with this last failure, I decided to try this watch.

All I can say is AMAZING!! I would have never bought the Versa and wasted my money if I knew a watch this reasonably priced existed! It does absolutely everything the Versa does. In fact, I have an android phone, and the Versa would tell me my phone was ringing, but never who was calling. Guess what? This Blackview watch DOES tell me who's calling! So it actually does more than the Versa. The steps are even more accurate. I have a Nordictrack Incliner, and the Versa was always off by almost .5 miles. The Blackview is completely accurate and stays with the same step count and mileage as my Incliner. The watch is comfortable to wear and cleans easily. The sleep tracking is just as good as the Versa and it has an alarm just like the Versa. And one of the best parts...the battery life actually does last 12 days!!! I am truly disappointed with myself for wasting my money on the Versa. The app that goes with the Blackview is great. On a small occasion, the watch may lose it's connection and not receive text messages. This has only happened twice. The app has an easy place that you click to simply reboot the device and it works again like a charm! I mean, really, a device that last 12 days will have to be rebooted on occasion! The charging cord is great and it truly only takes 2 hours to fully charge. I have coworkers who have the expensive Apple watch, and this Blackview looks like a clone. One of my coworkers thought it was an Apple watch until I told them. They're now going to get one.
All I can say is you won't regret your purchase with this product!! Please give it a try. Thank you and happy stepping!

review_text:
Big but fast. I bought this scooter to get around due to impairment of my right leg as a result of back injury. It is very easy to get on and to learn to drive but a few things need to be adjusted first. The emergency brake is difficult to use but I finally got mine to work properly. You need this to work as there is no park feature as you find on other chairs

I also had to adjust the toe in to get it to drive safely. Before it was very difficult to drive as it darted uncontrollably as I picked up speed. Be sure to inflate all 4 tires as well, I set mine to the max of 40psi as there is no recommended tire pressure. All 4 tires were way off when I got it which contributed to the poor drivability.

The frame and body panels are well done and solid, I have most of the unit apart to inspect and to add a trailer hitch. They have attachment points both font and back which I assume are there for attaching accessories such as a Custom hitch or bumpers.

I love mine as it has 4 speeds, slow + 1-2-3, slow is about the same as walking speed, 3 gets you up to 24 kmph or about 15 mph. I drive mine on the road (keeping right) to go for coffee in town, it has a full automotive lighting pkg including signals. It is an attention getter, lol.

product_name: FINGER TEN Mens All Premium Soft Cabretta Leather Tour Fit Grip Left Hand Lh Right Hand Rh with Cadet Size Golf Gloves Value 3 Pack Size from Small to XXL
review_text:
for the money, a really nice glove! Note sizing though.. I bought these to use on the driving range in a hot humid climate to keep from damaging my good gloves and not worry if these get thrown away after several uses. I actually was shocked how well these performed.

Sizing: I wear a M/L in almost all gloves (Footjoy, Titleist, etc). This M/L fit really nice in the hand but was noticeably smaller circumference around the hand. It was a bit tight. So if you have a wide or thick hand I would definitely size up.

Use: I started out on the range and hit maybe 50 balls. Went to the course and walked 9 holes in hot humid conditions. Glove and myself were soaked after the round, but the glove actually held up well. No rips, tears or noticeable issues and surprised me much more than I thought. Leather feels good, breaths well and did not stretch hardly at all.

I bought a similar priced Callaway glove that was leather but it felt cheap, stretched a lot and didn't feel like leather.

Verdict: Is it of the quality of a $30 high end glove? No. There is a noticeable difference in feel, but the fact I can get 3 of these for the same price is amazing. I don't particularly like the logo and I think a more subtle professional design would make the glove look more expensive. Will I wear this on weekend rounds of golf? Probably not. I prefer the softer feeling leather and like the Titleist and Footjoy logos much better. That being said, I would buy these again! Well worth the money.

review_text:
pros and cons. This is an interesting supplement that I've been taking on and off for a couple years. The thing is, it's the only thing I've tried that can calm down my heart palpitations; I'm prone to anxiety attacks and the palpitations cause me even more anxiety so as long as I can get rid of those I have an easier time calming myself down and the attack ending quick. So, for that reason this is a godsend for me. However, unfortunately it comes with some weird side effects for me. It affects me mentally to the point where I feel like I'm almost drunk (but not a good drunk), or sick, like everything is very slowed down and I almost feel like everything is going in slow motion. It's really strange. I'm not sure what this means or what I can do about it, I've experimented with different dosages, added sea salt to the water like the box says but I can't get rid of that unusual symptom. I am really sensitive to supplements in general so I generally try to avoid them and have paradoxical reactions to a lot of things (other magnesium supplements I've tried have actually made my palpitations worse, or brought on palpitations even when I was feeling fine, so maybe my body just has a weird sensitivity to this), so it probably won't apply to you, but just putting it out there.

To the people complaining about the taste, I really don't get it...it just tastes like slightly mineralized/salted water. You're supposed to dilute it in a big glass of water so you really shouldn't have a strong taste at all. I actually like the taste, but it's very subtle.

product_category: Tools & Home Improvement | Sports Water Bottles
review_text:
I drink so much more water now.. I'm a hobbyist photographer in my spare time and I do some very light hiking around for landscape photos. On those small trips I always carry ice water to stay hydrated. I've been carrying a vacuum insulated aluminum water bottle by Zojirushi for a few years and it's worked well, but I had a MAJOR problem with it. As dumb as it sounds, every single time I drank from the Zojirushi bottle I would get a stomach ache about 30 minutes later. Since the Zojirushi bottle is made of aluminum it has to be coated on the inside (like an aluminum can) to prevent metals from leaching into your drink. I'm pretty sure my coating was defective or scratched or something. I threw it away when I bought this Iron Flask. I have no such problems with the Iron Flask.

I like the size, weight, durability, portability and the performance. I honestly can't say a bad thing about it other than I put a small dent in it almost immediately. But it's a tool and tools get used. I got the 18oz variety in gray. I can fit about 6 "regular sized" ice cubes in it and it will keep ice for hours in a hot car and will stay chilly for almost an entire day. I like this thing so much that it's my regular water glass around the house. I tend to drink more when my drinks are easily portable and the included screw-down-flip-top lid has a nice handle built in. It fits in my car's cup holder and it slides into the side pouch of my camera bag (a Peak Design Everyday Backpack, if you care). The wide mouth is easy to get ice into and easy to clean. I like that it comes with a variety of lids so you can choose what works best for you instead of being relegated to a particular "style" of lid. Although admittedly I've stuck one lid on and use it exclusively. I haven't put any hot drinks in it but I can't imagine why it wouldn't do just as good of a job keeping things warm as it does keeping things cold.

It's a really nice stainless steel bottle. I guess my only complaint is that it isn't made in the USA. It's built well, but I really, really wish I could find more stuff made domestically. If I can, I'll pay a premium to buy a quality USA-built product. I don't think I'll be replacing this bottle unless a catastrophe happens or I lose it; in which case I'd probably just buy another one.

review_text:
Gunk in cap. For the most part, I love this bottle. It fits in the cup holder of my car (I measured before buying and compared it to the 32oz standard Nalgene. I had already removed the rubber insert to fit my Eddy bottle and the Chute Mag is at the limit for the drivers cup holder)

I have not filled it with ice, but considering I can put water from the fridge in it and leave it in the heat outside for hours and the water is still cold, it's wonderful. The Eddy always had that first bit in the straw that would be hot - not this one!

My complaint is the cleaning. I did read reviews on areas where mold can grow and have been careful while cleaning - though I do admit I will refill a few times before completely cleaning (I can drink 3+ of these daily in the summer).

Last night I took a q-tip to the inside of the big part of the cap and wouldn't you know, I pulled out some gunk. I'll give the cap a good soak with those cleaning tablets but it really shouldn't be so hard.

I hand wash everything. Not sure the dishwasher would make a different for the cap - I used to put my Eddy caps in the dishwasher and they still got mold badly.

product_name: Walker's Razor Slim
review_text:
Hmm.. Jury is still out for me on the noise cancelling of these ear muffs.

First, I do LOVE the speaker part and being I already have hearing issues even as a 38 yr old woman I found it super helpful to me to hear my husband or any instructors next to me clearly and could hear conversations way off in distance at our outdoor shooting range.

But I didn’t really notice unless I don’t understand how it works, it cancelling the noise so much when shots go off. It seemed to do fine enough to keep the shots from ringing my ears but didn’t notice the shots being any more or less with the mic on or off. Seemed the same to my ears either way. But the mic helped me to hear folks voices. But I thought the mic was supposed to help deafen the gun shots more than when it isn’t on and I couldn’t tell a difference. I noticed though it canceled My husband’s voice when he was talking to me when others were shooting loudly and close by then I had to have him repeat but it didn’t seem to cancel the gunshots like I assumed it would. Maybe I am misunderstanding the concept?

But all in all they are comfortable muffs, they did help with ear protection and dampening the noise. They fold up very compactly as well.

review_text:
Beware of hidden mold. I purchased this brush at WFM and only used it several times before cleaning it and putting it away, forgotten, under the sink.

The bristles weren't stiff enough to wash root vegetables and I found the ring design a bit awkward to use. The narrow design of the bristles also meant a smaller contact space which meant scrubbing something wide like potatoes takes longer. Scrubbing and preparing potatoes already takes a significant amount of time, last thing I need is to double the scrubbing time, lol!

I went back to my plastic Oxo with its short, firm bristles and wide profile that fits nicely in the palm of my hand. (I have no connection to that product.)

I came across this brush again in my gadget tub and pulled it out, hoping I'd like it better this time. I used it occasionally for some lighter scrubbing for a couple weeks. I like to clean my brushes and upon a closer inspection I noticed black mold at the base of the holes where the bristles are anchored into the bamboo. Our climate is very dry here and my Oxo, which was quite a bit older, was fine. I think the wood base verses the plastic base in the Oxo creates an environment for mold growth. I normally try to avoid plastic, but mold as the alternative is a deal breaker.

I have several natural bristle bottle brushes that have never molded so it's not a problem with the bristles, it's a problem with water not being able to air dry properly in the tight spaces where they are anchored into the bamboo. Cleaning vegetables with a moldy brush is not safe, even when the mold isn't obvious. Spores are microscopic and it doesn't take much to contaminate food, your hands, or the air. This is especially important for anyone sensitive to mycotoxins.

product_name: YETI Tundra 45 Cooler
review_text:
It's a YETI - Sizing will be the main dilemma when choosing one of these.... The first thing to note is that YETI marketing is misleading. So the number in the product name DOES NOT indicate actual capacity. For example, I have the YETI 45 and it does not hold 45L. It's less. But I'm guessing this is due to the space needed to make this a bad a** cooler that can keep ice for days. If you're new to YETI, a first time buyer, you may be at a dilemma on which size to get. You can't look at outside dimensions and compare it to a non-YETI cooler that you may be using and say it's the same. Because it's probably not in terms of capacity. At the same time, the physical dimension of the YETI is still something to consider if you have space constraints and are looking for a drop in, same size replacement. For me, I was attempting to replace an igloo MaxCool and I had a space constraint to work with. I was "hoping" to get the mighty YETI cooling power AND have the same capacity/footprint as my Igloo. But that's not possible. I was deciding between the YETI 35, 45, Haul, and 65. The sizing for YETI seems intentionally offset to other brands so I felt the size I needed was in between the 45 and 65, ex. if they had a 55 that would have been perfect. The 35 is essentially a drink only cooler for day trips like the traditional old school hand carry igloos. It's small. The Haul is actually larger than the 65, I think, which is HUGE. The 65 would have been the one I should have went with for capacity but it wouldn't meet the footprint I needed to meet. So I went with the 45. When it showed up it was a bit disappointing as it's more of a bigger cooler for mainly drinks like beach parties or maybe day trip. I was hoping to use it for multi-day camping trips for food and drinks. HAHAH... dreaming. There isn't a whole lot of space and I'm guessing best case it's enough for a 2-day camping trip for a family of 4. Maybe for 1 person you can do drinks/food for multi-day camping. But again I think it's more for drinks. It does come with a YETI basket, which is nice but something I'm likely not going to use. Space is too much of a premium to use a basket. All of this was made up for by the amazing cold retention of the cooler. We had ice for days (3+ days) and food cold with some drinks. I ended up using both my igloo for drinks and the YETI for food for camping. It worked out very well.

The 45 is heavy but not too heavy for a strong person to carry, even fully loaded. I do think if I got the 65 and it was fully loaded, there's no way one person can carry it. My igloo comes with wheels but the YETI didn't. This was one reason why I was considering the YETI HAUL. Wheels are nice when you need to transport or move from the parking space to where you need to go. I did find out that you can buy 3rd party, after market wheels for the YETI 45. They are expensive but may be worth it.

Overall, it's a YETI and it delivered on what it's known for. Just realize you're getting less in capacity for the same physical size.

review_text:
I included how to measure the ball. It's a great ball. I also have the TheraBand Pro series and this one is no different, for a fraction of the price. Nice sturdy material. It comes with a pump, and it takes a bit to inflate it to however firm you want, so it might be easier to use a bicycle pump. I found it no trouble to inflate with the pump it came with. The pump has two sizes of tip, they give you three plugs in case you lose one, and two plug remover tongs. Those are nice extras because I've lost the plug on my old ball before and had to scramble around trying to find it because I didn't have another one. Exercise balls are a wonderful thing to have. I used them years ago when I was a personal trainer but when I had an accident and ended up in physical therapy for a long time they gave me the ball and a weight bar and exercises to do for my spine. I still do all of them today because it keeps my spine in limber condition. Some people were talking about how long it took to get it but I ordered it through Prime and got it two days later.
There's a trick to measuring the ball to get the size you need. The chart indicates diameter (the distance straight from one side of the sphere to the opposite side, passing through the center), NOT CIRCUMFERENCE so use the centimeters in the chart and multiply by pi to get the actual size of the ball (in centimeters).
For example, if the chart says 55cm, you multiply 55cm x pi (3.14) = 172cm. That's how big around the ball is. Get out a tape measure at home and see if that size will work for you. 55cm is how high the ball is from the ground up. It should come up to about the back of your knee. I found that I was able to fill this ball very firm. They are made not to burst. It's better to buy a slightly smaller ball and fill it as firm as you can, then to buy a bigger ball and have to inflate it less and then it will be too soft to be challenging. Or if you inflate it fully, it'll be too big for you.

product_name: Takeya Originals Vacuum Insulated, 18 Ounce, Navy Stainless Steel Water Bottle, 18 oz
review_text:
Uh-mazing!. While I will strongly disagree with their claims of how long liquids will stay cold, I do concede I live in an area where temperatures are above 100 for over 12 hours a day in the summer. Having the contents being even cool is extremely welcomed and the body of the flask doesn’t burn your body! Nor does it get slick or pick up dirt and mud by sweating.
I have had coffee stay steaming warm almost 12 hours. It could be that everything else is also steaming here. This winter, we get to maybe 30 as a low and low 40s to the 50s at most, I’ll see how long it can keep things warm, hot etc.
the handle works well for holding, clipping into place or onto something well. The screw top for the main mouth holds well and doesn’t allow for spills when put on correct. The mouth spout allows for easy flow of fluid out as well as has a screw top that also prevents spills when closed correctly. I’ve even put in powder mixes to my water and shook it in the bottle with 0 spills.
I’ve had liquid in the bottle over night and even for two days, on accident, and no rust spots or weird smells after washing. To wash I just use a baby bottle brush, a tablespoon of baking soda and dawn. Nothing special. No mildew or mold, even under the lids and the gaskets or the grooves of the screw parts. I’m VERY allergic to molds and mildews so this is very important to me. No smells of past liquids, but if you put something funky in, or it turns funky, I’m pretty sure you’ll have to expect funky after. That’s just common sense. That and washing them correctly!
No flaking from the paint, no burns from the flask from being in the 115 direct sun, and liquids, as mentioned, will remain at least cool, after 4+ hours out in the sun and heat.
Takeya, if you read these, I know some trail runners and myself that are more than happy to help test more of your products out in the Arizona trials all year round! Prove me wrong and show me you guys can keep liquids ice cold for longer! We all love how rugged, easy to use, long lasting your products are!

product_name: OXYVAN Bike Seat Most Comfortable Universal Replacement Bicycle Seat Cushion Dual Shock Absorbing Ball Wide Bicycle Saddle for Men Women
review_text:
8 Comfort Style Seats Compared by Older Riders. This review is for seat #2 in the attached images. Comparative review below.

I see many reviews comparing these comfort saddles to the very hard stock saddles on some bikes. Any saddle in the comfort class is better than most stock seats I’ve seen, so I decided to compare comfort saddles against a higher standard – ranked within the comfort seat category.

My wife and I compared 8 different bike saddles for comfort. In the attached two images, they are numbered 1 – 8. (1-5 and 6–8) Most were street ridden for over 6 miles of testing. Both my wife are I are 59 years old, and saddle comfort is much more important to us now than it was 4 or 5 years ago. I am 6’ 210 lbs., she 5’6”135 lbs.

Despite all the discussion about measuring your sit bone width and aligning to the “right” saddle flatness width, I found that to be less applicable for the comfort seat category, as both my wife and I, with over 1 inch difference in sit bone width between us (5.5 in. vs. 4 in.), ranked these comfort seats almost identically. Most are simply too narrow to provide great weight distribution comfort, and some lose their shape/support on the sides when under pressure, hence less flat area to support your sit bones, and that also begins to make them feel less stable.

All but one tested were too short to allow for any forward or backward shift in saddle riding position. Remember also that too wide a saddle impedes your pedaling motion. Too narrow (not wide enough to support your sit bone width) and you feel the full weight of your upper body on a smaller area, thus ride pain and even numbness.

Rankings - Amazon Seller is in ( )

Best - 5 Stars
#1 –GRM Comfort -B (GRM Store)
Build and material quality is also excellent, and waterproof. After 24 miles of riding for both of us, this GRM wins easily for comfort. It is slightly wider and longer than all other saddles tested. The added length provided forward and backward sit position shifting, though it was not needed for comfort. The width worked well for both of us, and it’s cushiony yet firm in holding its form, so excellent weight distribution.

Good – 4 Stars
#2- OXYVAN Bike Seat (Deerlux)
A little soft overall, not holding its form on the sides, some sit instability, but generally comfortable.

#6- Comfortable Bicycle Seat (SFDGVS)
Also a little soft overall, and not holding its shape as well under pressure. You tend to feel less stable in the saddle, but generally comfortable.

Decent - 3 Stars
#4- Schwinn Women’s Stock Seat – 7 yrs old
#3- Schwinn Men’s Stock Seat– 8 yrs old
Both our stock Schwinns were surprisingly as comfortable as the marketed “comfort” saddles below. Although not as wide, they still provided decent comfort with their firm structure. They are soft, but not so soft that they lost their form and support, but neither is as wide as the new seats we tested.

#7- NUOBESTY Comfortable (Sellshopus)
We were not impressed with the material quality as it was somewhat stiff compared to the 4 and 5 star rated seats, but it holds its form well under pressure.

#8 Comfort Bike Seat (Luscian)
Plastic stiff feel to material, Holds form well under pressure.

#5- “Most Comfortable Bike Seat”(Hutigertech)
Very stiff plastic feel, and certainly not an accurate name for this seat. Holds its form under pressure.

review_text:
Completely inaccurate and useless gauge, but gets the job done as a pump. Pros:
Compatible with both presta and schrader valves
Comes with adapters that can be used on soccer balls, basketballs, etc.
Comes with case for adapters that attaches to the body
Notches in the top of the pump body to hold the pump tube when not in use
Wide pedals to stand on while pedaling that look nice and stabilize the pump during use
Coloring on the latch makes it easy to know when it’s engaged with the valve (I personally get this mixed up from time to time and it’s helped me remember)

Cons:
The gauge is COMPLETELY INACCURATE
The pedals to stand on feel like a cheap attachment

This pump gets the job done. My biggest issue is with the gauge, considering I would have never bought the pump in the first place if I had known the gauge would be useless.

TL;DR: opt for a nicer pump that has a working gauge, or get a cheaper one with no gauge at all. I’d personally recommend doing the latter and getting a handheld gauge if you care about your tire pressure, since this means you can carry it with you during rides as well just in case.

review_text:
Works but needed help to apply. These pain tapes, impregnated with lidocaine as the active ingredient, do work on various kinds of pain to provide some relief. The tape format, though, was a bit of a challenge for me to use. My pain is shoulder joint pain (caused by either osteoarthritis, carpal tunnel or both). Because the pain is deep within the joint and the area of my shoulder is relatively thick, perhaps application of the tape doesn't work as well as on other areas of the body. I think it would work great for knees, backs, ankles and lower arms but not quite as well for shoulders.

Application is easy on most of the body, but for shoulders, you really need to have someone else apply the tape for you. Doing it with one hand is just about impossible in that area.

product_category: Sports & Outdoors | Sports Water Bottle Accessories
review_text: Great Water Bottle Holder, but Color Transfers. First, the positives... This is a GREAT holder for my large, 32 ounce, water bottle (I ordered the larger option of the holder/sling).  My large water bottle fits perfectly in this holder, and it's plenty deep, so there's no risk of the bottle tipping out over the top.  The outside extra pocket is great for my larger phone (iPhone 7Plus).  I wish the outside pocket was a tad deeper, but when the water bottle is in place, there's enough tension that the phone sits in the pocket snugly.  The extension strap allows you to use this holder on your shoulder, or cross-body, which is what I do.  Next, the things you need to know (neither positive nor negative)... I initially adjusted the strap length so the water bottle would sit at about hip height.  On my first outing I noticed two things.  First, with the weight of the filled bottle, the strap will stretch out, so adjust the strap for a lesser length than you want, knowing it will stretch.  Next, if the water bottle sits anywhere around your hip area, you will get significant "bounce" of the holder as you walk.  I don't mean bounce up and down; I mean bounce back and forth off your hip.  I found this distracting, but didn't want to have to keep one hand on the holder to reduce the motion.  To make this more comfortable for me, I adjusted the strap quite a bit shorter, so the water bottle sits above my waist, alongside my torso.  There's still some bounce, but it is greatly reduced and I can comfortably walk hands-free. Lastly, the negative... I ordered this holder/sling in color black, expecting it would show less dirt and would be a more neutral color for various users in the family.  The problem is the black dye from the strap, which I have positioned as a crossbody, transfers to your clothing (see my pic).  I don't know if this happens with other colors, but it's definitely an issue with the black.  I'm going to try washing it to see if that will reduce the dye transfer, otherwise I'll only be using it with black tops.  I really like the function; just bummed  about the color transfer.

review_text:
High Quality, but heavy and limited capacity. 20 quart Capacity:

I was hoping for mobile cooler that would be good for holding a decent amount of food or drinks. The cooler is very durable and robust. It is sturdy enough for someone to stand on without even deflecting the lid. The seal between the top of the cooler and the main compartment is tight. The hinges are molded out of the rotomolded plastic. It also has rubber feet. This reminds me of the type of cooler that would be used to transport organs by a hospital - very high quality with no doubt that it will keep the products inside cool for a long period of time.

Unfortunately, it did not satisfy my needs. I didn't realize how small the interior capacity would be. The exterior dimensions of the cooler are 12 inch deep x 19-1/2 inches and the inside dimensions are 8 inches x 14--1/2. That means the cooler is 4-5 inches thick at some locations, which is obvious by the heavy weight of the cooler. With nothing inside, the cooler weighs around 17 pounds, which doesn't sound like much, but it is relatively heavy for what you would expect for a cooler of this size and capacity.

The other thing that I don't love is the big 'amazon commercial' yellow sticker on the front that sticks out like a sore thumb. Of course, they need to market their product, but they could have added branding in a more subtle way.

45 quart Capacity:
The 45 quart capacity has all the same features and attributes as the 20 quart, but just a little larger and heavier. I think this one is versatile and functional.
Exterior Dimensions: 27 inches x 15-1/4 inch

It's got a smooth, soft texture, but it's not slippery. It comes in a really great selection of colors, too. It's easy to clean - they recommend water with a drop or two of bleach to make sure it's clean, and I like that bit of advice. I've never seen it on any other bottle I've ever used. It comes with cute, and possibly helpful, motivational statements at hourly intervals, if that's of use to you, and it's offered in a wide variety of attractive colors. And yes, I'm buying another one today. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED. Don't waste your time and money on inferior versions.

review_text:
If you have 40c to 45c tires, this is the tube for you.. I own a 2020 Trek Verve 1, with 700x45c tires. These are the 700c equivalent of beach cruiser tires (lol), they are wide and hold a nice volume of air. Tire psi is recommended at 60-80psi max. I usually pump to 65. I have one original tube in back, and had to replace the front tube from a thorn flat.

I went through about 4 tubes in a month that all looked like your typical 700c tube. They are no good, they cannot withstand even up to 40psi because of the amount of room in a 45c tire, the tube can physically expand too much, and will always fail.

These Sunlite tubes are different. When you take them out of the box, you see the difference immediately. These are thick, heavy duty tubes that are darn near as thick as the sidewalls of my tire. Very heavy duty, not like a typical 35c tube at all. I mounted this one and pumped to 65psi no problem, took it on a 2hr bike ride over our rough roads where I live, without a single issue.

Pretty good, but I like the equivalent razor scooter a bit better.. I have both this and the "Razor A5 LUX Kick Scooter" and I like the Razor a little bit better for two reasons, and give that one 5 stars and this one 3 stars. This "New Bounce Kick Scooter" is ok, but there are several things that drive me to like the Razor one better.

First, the razor scooter's center of gravity is a little lower, as the base is lower to the ground. This makes it more stable and (in my opinion) a little easier to ride.

Second, the Razor also appears to be engineered a little tighter. This creates significant impact to the steering, as unless you manually tighten your "Bounce Kick" scooter with tools you may find that you can turn the steering wheel a little to the left and a little to the right with no wheel movement whatsoever. This is really scary when you are trying to make tight turns because you may oversteer since the first mild steering actions do not do what you expected.

I was able to switch between scooters on a daily basis over the course of weeks and I still find the Razor scooter to be a little easier to handle, and, after crashing once, I came to really love the tighter steering.

Now, this is not to say that the Bounce Kick scooter is bad -it is not. It has a very grippy base (like sandpaper) and the color scheme (black) looks pretty nice. It also folds up just as easily as the Razor, and has the same type of kickstand. It even has one thing that the Razor does not, which is a cushioning suspension for the front wheel. Honestly, though, after putting on a lot of weight on this scooter and going over a bunch of bumps, I really have to say that this advantage doesn't tilt the scales either way, and might actually lessen the steering control a tiny bit.

Overall, if I only had this scooter I'd give it 4 stars, but since I have the other as well, and compare the two, I give it 3 stars.

product_name: Sun Will Battery Heated Beanie Hat,Electric Rechargeable Warm Winter Heated Fleece Cap
review_text:
Heated Stretch Beanie w/Rechargeable LiPo 2200mAh Battery, Wall Charger - 3 Heat Levels. I received this product in exchange for my honest review as part of the Amazon Vine Program. Seller the Sun Will Store lists this as "Sun Will Battery Heated Beanie Hat,Electric Rechargeable Warm Winter Heated Fleece Cap". On cold days I like warm ears. The hat lining is a comfy fleece material and the outer knit is a cotton/polyester blend with elastane. This heated stocking cap has 2 built in panels that warm up over the ears using "far infrared heat panels" which are powered by a rechargeable lithium polymer (LiPo) 2200 mAh Battery. LiPo batteries have a better discharge/recharge life cycle than standard lithium rechargeables so are best for a product like this.

What I received is in Picture 1 boxed; the few instructions are on the 2 double sided tags in Picture 2. Picture 3 shows the battery pocket inside the hat with the wire connector for the battery. Picture 4 shows the battery out of the hat, the dedicated wall charger that will only work for this type LiPo 7.4V Battery, and a tiny cover to seal the end of the hat wire connector if no battery is in use. A small velcro type closure keeps the battery in its pocket inside the hat.

This hat was a tight fit with not enough stretch for my head size. The battery sits at the back of the head with the control button near front center. A long press turns it on giving a red color and cycling through white and blue with repeated presses to Off changes the heating level. (see Picture 5). It keeps my ears very warm. The red is conspicuous when lighted.

I worry that the instructions are so scant. Is this safe to wear in the rain? Could it short circuit and cause a burn? Are there additional safety precautions? I wish the instruction set was not so brief and limited.

Still, this is a good value and works well. The battery even on high will last 2.5 hours per the seller. I did have to turn down the heat after awhile, and the tight fit made the battery bulge uncomfortable. For anyone with a smaller head that might be less of an issue. My big ears definitely got warm quick on high heat.

This is a great idea for cold days to keep one's ears and head warm. Additional batteries can be purchased. The hat can be carefully hand washed and dried with no battery installed and the wire cap on. I liked it despite that it could be a bigger and stretchier and have better detailed instructions. Recommended.

product_name: Sun Will Battery Heated Beanie Hat,Electric Rechargeable Warm Winter Heated Fleece Cap
review_text:
A little tight, but warms up fast. This is a neat idea for people who get cold easily. It's a stylish looking beanie (no 'closure' like the listing says) that would look just as good on men as women. The battery is removed from the hat to charge and to wash the hat. The battery reminds me of a house phone battery in size and shape. The charger has a red LED indicator that is on when charging and off when it's done. The battery plugs in and tucks into a small pocket at the back inside of the hat. I thought it would feel bulky and press into my head, but you really don't notice it.....though I imagine if you wore a helmet over it that came down to the base of your skull you might feel it.

You turn it on by pressing the stylized S logo on the front. Not just a quick press, hold it for a few seconds. When it lights up red, it's on. The directions insert says that with repeated presses, it goes from 3 bars lit up to two, and one to indicate charge level. That must be the old model. This one goes from red-high, to white-medium, to blue-low. And one more press to turn it off - the logo is no longer lit up. It warms up quite quickly, and I may use this as a mini-heating pad for a sprained wrist!

It comes in a high end looking gift box, with the hat on one side and the battery and charger in a box on the other side. The only drawback is that it's a bit tight and not too stretchy on the inside layer. Great for teens or kids or smaller people; but for people with normal to larger heads or a lot of hair, this is going to feel tight. You might be able to get it wet and stretch it, but I'd worry about breaking the wires then.

review_text:
I really like these chairs.. I got a couple of these because I thought they were replacements for 2 other chairs I used to have and really love. I tried to find them again thinking they were Tommy Bahama.
These are nice and lightweight but they are wider than my old chairs. This is good for some of my guests.
I like the backpack part. These are very easy to fold up unlike some other Backpack Tommy Bahama chairs we got a couple of years ago. The plastic part was amazingly hard to get to fold up and I didn't like it at all. These are a breeze so I don't know if there was a redesign or what.
I love the wood armrests on these better than the all plastic ones. They get less hot and don't burn your forearms as easily.
I don't love the back pouches quite so much, but I do think the cooler part could be useful for some people. What I don't like is that there is not one big compartment like the chairs I was trying to replace. It turns out those were Rio backpack chairs. They were lighter slightly, narrower, had wood armrests and the big compartment accomodated a ton of stuff meaning sometimes I could get away with not taking an extra backpack of things to the beach with us.

Anyhow these are great chairs, nice and wide for larger people, so far they have made it through one season and I hope they will last many more seasons (some people have complained they don't hold up).
These are not quite as comfortable to carry as the Rio backpack chairs I got.
But they do have the ability to lay completely flat which is a nice bonus.

I would still get the Rio chairs for my specific way of using them, but these chairs are a close second as a choice.

review_text:
Edible but not enjoyable. I remember the cabbage rolls my grandmother made. Tender cabbage surrounding meat that was spiced just right and covered in sauce that was so good that any drop remaining would get mopped up with some bread. Absolutely delightful.

These don't taste anything like that.

The best description I can offer is that they are in fact edible, but it helps if you're really, really hungry. The cabbage is limp and tasteless, the filling is oddly flavored to the point where it has an aftertaste, and the thin sauce is has a metallic-like taste to it.

But it does serve a purpose. The container is shelf stable and has almost a 2 year shelf life (the ones I received in Oct 2020 have a best by date of July 2024). It can be reheated in the microwave, in boiling water or a hot plate. It's emergency food and, if there is an emergency, chances are you'll be happy with a hot meal regardless of the taste.

If I were to rate this on the basis of taste, it would be a 1 star at best. But considering the shelf-stable nature and the variety of prep methods, I'll give it 3 stars. It's not a meal you'd actually want to eat, but it's edible if you're in a situation where you have to eat it.

review_text:
Barely functions just as a watch. After my Samsung Gear S2 suddenly died, I needed to find a replacement without spending hundreds of dollars. This is one of three cheaper smart watches/fitness bands I bought in the hopes to find something usable (I have an online geek store, so I’m also doing product research). While I knew that none of them could possibly live up to my $160 smart watch, I figured I'd give them a try, hoping one would be sufficient for a watch with notifications. I was (not surprisingly) disappointed.

The main thing I needed out of a watch is just that: a watch. Yes, this does keep time, but it's a huge pain to get it to display. The idea is that you lift your wrist to look at the band and it wakes up. That happens maybe two percent of the time. The rest of the time I have to tap it multiple times to just wake it up. Hardly useful.

The notifications are also a joke. For some reason, I get three notifications for just one event. It doesn't always display them either, so I have to tap the band three or four times to wake it and then go into notifications. Honestly, by then it's just easier to pull my phone out of my pocket.

The Alexa feature is nice and is the main reason why I chose this one over the other options. It also has a good battery life, but since it hardly functions, it isn’t worth the tradeoff. The band does have a nice fit and is very lightweight. I wasn’t a fan of having the app running on my phone at all times as I was concerned about my battery. Fortunately, I didn’t notice much difference in my battery drain, or at least not enough to cause concern that my phone wouldn’t last the day.

Perhaps if they would put more into it, it could actually be a decent basic smart watch rather than a cheap fitness band that barely works. Even as a fitness band, the step counter is far from accurate—it said I had over 300 steps in one day when I had maybe 20 because I was still putting on my shoes. It still ranks above the $20 one I had shipped from China. That one is totally useless. Still, even at its $30 price, I would pass on this and go with something that is going to function better for a little more money.

As for me, my new Samsung will be delivered tomorrow. I should have just done that from the beginning and saved myself the time and money wasted on this cheap junk. I was curious, and now I know. No more generic ones for me, and not one of them will ever find their way into my online store’s inventory.

review_text:
cant complain! but i willllll. i picked up a sougilyang spinner reel for $20, comes w spare spool and overall feels great. felt more like a $40-50 reel. i have a few kastking reels i nabbed for $50 and felt like $80... even one that had issues outta the box cuz incorrect assembly was still awesome after i fixed it.

the plussino reel however did not get that same emotion.

at first glance, its a gorgeous reel. definitely looks like a $80 reel. my buddy’s cheapo $15 reel? definitely looked cheapo with plastic parts falling off. so the plussino has that, along with a smooth retrieve.

its biggest issue was the drag and some really sharp edges... and its heavy!

the drag was a mess. i had to take apart the drag completely and found metal shavings in the felt. there were also some imperfections and cross threading happening here and there. even with it cleaned out, drag was still super rough. wasnt till i added some drag grease that it gotten smoother.

then the sharp edges. the machining on the spool looks “sharp!” haha puns - the slotting in the spool is literally sharp. i had to go across it a few times with some ceramic rods to clean and smooth it out.

its also a pretty heavy reel for its size - wished i paid attention to that. whereas other reels of this size are in the 8-10 oz range, this feels much heavier.

am i happy with it? meh. its what i paid for so i cant complain (but i just did complain! lol) - it’ll suit its purpose as a backup reel. its just, i was hoping for the same fit/finish and waulity reel vs some of their other competitors which ive had good luck eith.

it doeeesss look sexy tho on the plussino rod.

review_text:
Heavy duty, long battery life, easy and so fun!. I love this thing, it is so fun. We don't have kids, I got this for me! I have used one before and this one is just as easy and smooth to ride. This thing is heavy, it's really high quality and supports my weight and my husband's, easily. It really zips along and I use it mostly in the house. Its only downside is it not being able to go up a little lip where our flooring changes, it doesn't like our thick carpet (with our weight on it at least), and if you run over a little rock or bump you may fall off because its tires can't handle it and you lose balance. The other one I used didn't seem to have any trouble with this. It does great on flat, clear surfaces. Can't do hills of course. For what I wanted it for though, it's great. Super fast and very sensitive to your slightest movements. You don't have to move much for it to know what you want it to do.
It runs with an app where you can control the audio and some of the lights. I wish you could turn off all the lights but that's not an option. You can only change the colors. The bluetooth speaker is unnecessary but good and easy to connect to. It's loud enough for the rider to be able to hear clearly.
In the house it's plenty loud. It's nothing special but I guess an added bonus.
The battery is impressive! I don't take it for long runs, but riding it around the house for long periods the battery level doesn't even drop. It holds the charge well too. It's ready to go every time I turn it on.
I think this is really well made, great quality and so fun and easy to use. Depending on what you're looking for, this is something I would recommend and an excellent gift for kids or adults!

review_text: Convex, not a flat mirror - listing should be clear. Two reviewers called this a flat mirror.  Perhaps Hafny changed it, but the one I received is convex.  I need a flat mirror.  Photo shows a tennis-racquet-shaped bug zapper reflected in several bar-end mount cycling mirrors.  Three of these five  mirrors were supposed to be flat, one was sold as convex, and one did not say.  Here are the five you are looking at:  1:00 position in the photo: Blackburn Bike Multi-Mirror (ASIN B0855G36NQ), 3:00: “ZoeDul Cycling” mirror (ASIN B089ST6PHJ, this is the only flat, bar-end mount mirror I have found on Amazon), 6:00: Mirrycle MTB mirror (ASIN B0009R96YK, sold as “convex”--best mount of the bunch), 8:00: MEACHOW bar-end bike mirror (ASIN B07DW3N2GZ), 11:00: This Hafny New Bar End FR04 (ASIN B07SG1CKXW). Note that the tennis racquet looks huge in the ZeoDul flat mirror and shrunken in the other four, which demonstrates the various amounts of convex curvature.  Unfortunately, the ZeoDul mirror’s mount is flimsy and shakes whenever the bike is moving, so it is a non-starter. This is a beautiful glove. This is a beautiful, well-made, quality constructed mitt (but what do you expect from Rawlings?).

While I haven't had a chance to play with it yet (it's November, after all) fit and a few catches inside make me think I'm really going to like playing with this glove. While I don't readily agree with the comment on the product card attached to it that the glove doesn't really need broken in it's not as stiff as some other gloves I've bought in the past. My girls both found it to be usable right out of the package as well, so that's a plus.

There isn't a lot of extra fluff in the glove's build -- not adjustment points, no finger slot or other crazy features you find on some gloves. This is a basic fielder's mitt, exactly what I was looking for.

The pocket isn't over-sized, either, a problem I have (again small-ish hands) with my current glove and many others I've tried or used over the years.

There could be a touch more padding in the palm, but I'm not a big fan of super-padded mitts as you lose the feel for ball contact with too much. Game conditions might make me re-think this as a possible negative, but probably not.

If I get it broken in properly and have negative experiences with it in actual game play, I'll come back and post. I'm not anticipating any, however.

review_text:
I LOVE this "pod". First, in order to legally attend church, we must do so in the parking lot, masked, sitting a minimum of 6 feet away. Here in "sunny California," we have had serious fires, wind, overcast weather, and right now (November 2020), we are running between 30-65 degrees. I am not immune to the cold. In fact, INSIDE buildings, I bring a blanket or a throw to put across my knees. So I have been freezing to attend church.

We got this on a Saturday night, practiced setting it up that evening, got to our church parking lot early and raised it without a hitch. Since we were enclosed, we did not wear masks, but had them at the ready. MANY of the church-goers came up to as afterwards and said this was a great idea!

Be aware that my husband, who is 6'1", and I, who am 5'1", fit comfortably inside this tent. We talked about the video on the seller's page showing two women and two children. It must be a snug fit. We found that the walls did not stretch out the way we would like. I am also concerned for the floor, pitching this on asphalt: I don't know how well it will last if we pitch it on top of a rock. We are buying a large tarp to put underneath, for added protection. I also just purchased on Amazon a blanket that can be used as a throw rug, the dimensions are larger than the floor, but it will provide extra protection against a chair's legs poking through the waterproof floor. I will probably get a tarp to put UNDERNEATH, as well.

As for the sides, they seemed to be bowing inward, but we have also purchased on Amazon (yet to arrive) some weights to hold the legs out further and pull the tent more taut.

Finally, we are very pleased with this tent. it prevented wind from chilling, but allowed to great visual to see our friends and view the service. I was especially pleased that the windproofing windows on three sides could be zipped down for extra ventilation, should that need arise. My husband, a scoutmaster, was impressed with the visual ability, but even more with the ease with which the tent went up.

The tent was lightweight, so I don't think it will withstand a heavy storm; but then, outdoor church would definitely be canceled in that event.

This is a purchase we would make again, and we will recommend it to others. In fact, we already have!
