review_text: Is there an ideal lidocaine patch out there?. I have pain and muscular dysfunction due to a shoulder injury that has affected my neck, in which I have a pinched nerve, and radiates down in between my scapula. Being that is a very dynamic area of movement, most lidocaine patches do not stick sufficiently to substantially relieve pain. It doesn't matter what I do, many that I've tried don't stay on or work. As far as these thin, flexible patches go, I've tried these patches and a similar product called Re-Lieved. The Re-Lieved patches work best, but the adhesive irritates my skin. I wear them during the day and have to use prescription steroid cream overnight. I always wash the area I'm applying the patch to and dry the area very well before applying the patch. These patches stick very well, maybe too well, because I have a irritated spot on my neck from wearing one today and even getting in the shower did not make them easier to remove. It was like ripping a giant band-aid off and a ton of adhesive remained stuck to my skin. I feel that I got some benefit out of the patch today, but not much more above lidocaine cream which needs to be reapplied. They do not work as well as Re-Lieved, but I did not have a reaction to the adhesive even though it was stuck to my skin. The patches are thin, light, stretchy, easy to apply, and comfortable. However, I don't think these work any better than the plain Salonpas menthol-type patches. Those smell terrible, but they stick and work. These might work for you if you don't have to worry about getting the adhesive off the middle of your back.

product_name: SUNGAIT Ultra Lightweight Rectangular Polarized Sunglasses UV400 Protection
review_text:
Incredible for the price and pack with features. - This is as good as any brand name sunglasses, only at a fraction of the cost. It has a considerable value for the price and packs a bunch of features!
- The pair comes with a cleaning cloth, a storage bag, a glare testing piece, and a tiny screwdriver.
- The new gray gunmetal frame looks sporty and quite fashionable. The weight feels good when wearing, not heavy despite being quite sturdy.
- UV400! It's a rating that blocks up to 400 wavelength nanometers. It will block out nearly 100% of any UV light, which is fantastic because you want that when you're out in the sun.
UV protection doesn't protect your eyes from glare, however. But it does protect from UV exposure, and it can be very beneficial in the long run, specifically to prevent cataracts when you get older.
- Polarized lenses, aka the ones that reduce glare. As you can see from their test piece, it's day and night with/without the glasses. That's when you look at water surfaces or metal objects under the sun; you squint your eyes because things seem to be much brighter than usual. This feature reduces reflective surfaces and increases the contrast a little. It's great for outdoor activities like fishing, boat riding, or going to the beach, for instance. Some lenses will say they are polarized, but they're just colored lenses; these are polarized! Because if you wear the glasses while watching your LCD TV, it's super dark. That's the real test, in my opinion.
- I love the nose pad too. The silicone is very soft, and doesn't hurt my nose when wearing it all afternoon. It's even softer than the pad on my prescription glasses, and perhaps it's due to it being silicone. *shrug*
- I haven't found any con yet. But I can't vow for the shatterproof feature at this price. Lol.
- I'm happy I went with this purchase. I bought it at first, use it for a few weeks. I really like the glasses, but I decided to relinquish them to my dad because he has cataracts. Along with taking his medicine and wearing these sunglasses, he reports that tearing red spots in his eyes has reduced quite a bit. I hope he wouldn't have to go through cataract surgery. These glasses aren't going to help with that, but they protect one's eyes from terrible sun rays. I aim to grab a few pairs for gifts next year. Cheers.

Setting it up is real easy. It took maybe 2 minutes from start to finish. As typical with tents, the included stakes are cheap and bend easily but I didn't use them. I use other stakes i already had.
Taking it down took a little longer but still quick. Bending the legs backwards to get it to fold felt like I would break the legs but it held up.
Size is good for 2 adults. Maybe 2 adults and 1 kid if you're not putting anything else in. I pack my supplies in a footlocker and was able to hold me and my footlocker with a little extra room. I am 6.5 feet tall so it was a little tight for length. Stretched out I was pretty much wall to wall.
I have only used it once on a 5 day trip but it held up well. I didn't have any rain but there was tons of dew and none of it made it in the tent. I also did not notice any condensation from my breath inside so ventilation is sufficient.
For a quick setup tent for 1 person, maybe 2, this is perfect. It will definitely see a lot more use from me.

product_category: Cell Phones & Accessories | Activity & Fitness Trackers
review_text:
Can anyone suggest a steel or leather replacement strap for Band 5? YES!!!. I love my Amazfit Band 5, but I'm apparently allergic to the band. So, upfront, I want to beg for a replacement band suggestion or hack. Has anyone had any luck?

UPDATE: I ordered ASIN B08DFP2PL3 as a replacement band, even though it's specified as only for the Mi Band 5 and one reviewer said it did not fit their tracker. When it came, indeed, it did not fit my Amazfit Band 5, but I was so desperate to keep using my tracker and my arm is so broken out and itchy from apparently silicone allergy that I took a fine ceramic nail file to the bottom plastic edge of my tracker and very carefully shaved off just enough plastic so the band fit into the strap with a firm push. The casing of the leather replacement band is metal, so there is no give in it as there is with the silicone strap that comes with the Amazfit Band 5. Just wanted to put this out there because the Amazfit Band 5 is an awesome tracker. I'm increasing my review of it to five stars. One other discovery is that you can overlay your heartrate over your sleep data, and you can see if there's anything weird going on with your heart, like sudden spikes higher or lower than your normal rate. I've discovered I do have some issues I need to discuss with my doctor.

But I love it. I'm especially pleased with the oxygen saturation reading, because of covid. I like the constant heart rate tracking and the ability to indicate type of exercise I'm engaging in. I find the PAI readings really motivating. I was pretty surprised the band perceives me as stressed out, though, because I feel less stressed out than I used to. I'm not sure the steps while tracking treadmill use are accurate, but I'm less concerned with that than I am the other indicators. The steps do seem accurate when I'm just walking around, and I like the goals tracking feature.

I wish the Zepp app integrated with My Fitness Pal, allowing for automatic syncing of exercise stats, but I don't expect the world at this price point.

I was skeptical but wanted to decrease my opioid prescription ASAP. I felt better after a few hours but it wasn’t until 24 hours that I felt I could attribute it to more than wishful thinking. Fifteen days postop I am now adequately controlled with acetaminophen w/one dose of opioid at night and before PT.
I liked this product because it is lighter-weight, adheres better, is thinner so more flexible, comes in a child-proof container, and is good for 12 hours, not just 8, so more convenient for morning and evening application. I use 2 at a time, one on each side of my patella where the most common TKR pain is. Be aware that in one can there are 10 strips, meaning using 4/24 hour day means one can lasts only 2 1/2 days, so plan accordingly.

product_name: OCOOPA Fast-Charging Hand Warmers, 10000mAh Handwarmer with PD & QC 3.0 Rechargeable Hand Warmer Supercar Design Heating time 15 Hrs Perfect for Outdoor Activities Brilliant Winter Gift
review_text:
Overall Great Hand Warmer for the Price. Lots of things to like about this hand warmer, although it is not perfect. 10000mAh battery is great. Last winter I used a Human Creations Energy Flux G3 warmer (https://www.amazon.com/Human-Creations-EnergyFlux-Rechargeable-Warmer/dp/B07GV87ZLD/ref=cm_cr_arp_d_product_top?ie=UTF8) that was 5200mAh and felt like I had to charge it every day. This one's battery seems to have much more life to it. It also gets substantially warmer even on settings one and two - sometimes it honestly feels *too* warm even on the first setting.

That said, it's not perfect. The only areas that heat up on these are the colored ones - in this case, the yellow area. The black plastic ring around the edges do not radiate heat, which is a bit of a shame. I figured the entire thing would get warm all the way around like my Energy Flux one did, so some areas of the OCOOPA one are hot and others are not. It's not a dealbreaker, but it is noticeable.

Another issue I have noticed is that the warmth seems to fluctuate a bit once its warmed up, all while on the same setting. It almost seems like it kicks into overdrive for the first 10m of usage and then it backs it down a bit once its warmed up. Every time I have used it I noticed that after a short initial period period it starts feeling cooler to my hand and I have to bump it up to the next level to maintain that same level of heat.

I also have a bit of an issue with the two different charging ports, too. It's nice that it supports both USB-C and Micro-USB charging but there is no easy way to tell which is which without looking very closely at the port every single time before you plug it in. Again, not a dealbreaker by any means but it does make this warmer a bit less usable IMO.

Lastly, I bought the yellow warmer because I really liked how it looked in the photos but the color in person is much brighter than it looks here. In the photos, it almost appears to be an orangey, "Amazon" yellow. In person its a bright, lemon orange. Not the end of the world but it was a marked difference when I first got it.

All that said, this is an excellent hand warmer, especially for the price. I ordered mine when it had a $6 off coupon, so for $31 its hard to go wrong with this. I liked the price, reviews and design so much I bought 3 more as gifts for this holiday season.

I go for long walks every single day, hot, cold, rain or shine and having one of these in my pockets makes dealing with cold Chicago weather all winter long infinitely easier.

product_name: Lafagiet Waterproof Arc Lighter, Outdoor Dual Plasma Arc Lighter, USB Rechargeable Flameless Electric Lighters for Camping, Hiking, Survival Tactical (F13-Orange)
review_text:
New, High Tech Igniter for Starting Campfires. For a Backpacker or Hiker having a source of ignition for fire starters is critical... Even a long distance Through Hiker should have some source of ignition for an emergency fire, despite the small added weight.
The Go-To igniter is the BIC or Mini BiIC due to it's reliability, small size and weight, and long-lasting life (a BIC has about an hour of fuel over maybe 3000 "lights", a Mini about 1/3 of that) - but a breeze and freezing temperatures are the enemy of the BIC.
The UCO Incendiary Storm-proof match beats the wind, rain, and cold, but using them is fiddly, requires practice, and the condition of the striker is critical, too.
The Ferrocerium Rod or Flint Sparker are great, simple sources of hot sparks that can ignite highly flammable materials, but their use takes practiced skill and good conditions - more an always-with-you just-in-case source of ignition.
Enter the Plasma Arc lighter. Wind is no problem. Actuating it is a button press. The Arc is hot enough to ignite any fire starter - my cotton-vaseline starters, my waxed jute cord "long match", my "Baddest Bee" starters, my Pyro Putty, even a thinned Fatwood stick all ignite in an instant with a brief second of Arc. (Then the starters are used to ignite the tinder in the fire lay, which in turn ignites the kindling, and soon you have a blazing campfire).
Now there are two electrode designs, and I prefer this "exposed electrode" design to ignite the starters rather than the "opposed electrode" design, which seems more for smokers. There are multiple lighter styles, too. I hope that this "all-weather lighter" style has a larger battery than other, fancier designs. I worry, too, that those with embedded flashlights might too easily turn on or drain the battery in use - an igniter is critical for the duration of your outing. Of course, if you carry a recharger for your cell phone, you can simply recharge the Arc Lighter "in the field".
While these are rechargeable, and it only takes a second to ignite a fire starter, how many ignitions one has is unproven, but said to be perhaps a few hundred... enough for most backpacking trips. And there is a limit on how many times these can be recharged, too... said a few hundred cycles. Let's say that means a life of 100,000 ignitions... that's equivalent to about 30 BIC's, so from a "Green" standpoint, the Arc Lighter is much less "bulk waste", but a Lithium cell is involved.
Cost-wise and effectiveness-wise, too, the Arc is superior to the BIC as well.
DOWNSIDES: The Arc Lighter is twice the bulk of a BIC. The Arc Lighter is clearly more complex, so "quality in manufacturing" can compromise its life. The "power" of the Arc is less than that of the larger flame produced by the BIC, limiting the use of the Arc to igniting fire starters rather than a piece of tinder, for example. The Arc is powered by a Lithium rechargeable cell which is degraded by low temperature, so similar to the BIC, the Arc lighter needs to be kept warm, kept next to your body.
RECOMMENDATION: There are so many sellers of this style Arc Lighter, likely they are all made in the same factory. I'd recommend these even with my limited experience so far - just buy from a seller with highest ratings. These are "Greener", should last adequately long for most outings (especially if you have a USB recharger along), do an excellent job igniting your choice of fire starters, and are inexpensive.

Great work-from-home stability chair!. So far I am satisfied with this purchase. The amount of air you add to the ball adjusts the stability for your intended use. I have it filled pretty full because I use it as a balancing chair for my at-home desk.

It also seems extremely durable. The material is thick, but flexible enough to adapt to more or less air fill. It does not smell of fumes, which was a concern of mine. I did not want my bedroom to smell like a pool toy.

The one area in which I struggled was filling the ball. The product does come with a manual pump, but it did take time and a bit of physical exertion to fill the ball. If you have a power operated pump such as one for an air mattress I recommend using that instead.

Also, while the product does come with a tool to remove the plastic plug when the ball has been filled, the plastic plug is still quite difficult to remove if you need to adjust the amount of air within the ball. I recommend partially inserting the plastic plug while you test out the firmness of the ball before completely inserting the plug in that valve.

Last, I love that the product comes with a chart of various exercises that can be done using the ball. Bonus! The guidance is appreciated!

product_name: ZEROFIRE Heated Ski Gloves for Men & Women, Waterproof Electric Winter Gloves with 2500mah batteries,3M Thinsulate,Touchscreen for Cold Winter Running Riding Hiking Climbing Hunting Snowboarding Motorcycle
review_text:
Fingers run a little short, but hand is correct size. Warms quickly.. I got these a size up from what I usually wear, and they actually *sort of* fit better than my usual size. The finger length is just right. I don't have extra fabric at the tips of my fingers. But the hand and wrist are true to an XL. Which is actually okay - I can better tuck my sleeves into the cuff this way. I do have to tighten up the velcro strap across the wrist quite a bit; I'd have to try it with a coat tucked in to see if it's worth cutting the extra off though. They are quite comfortable and soft inside.

On the pair I got, the zipper for the battery compartment on the left glove didn't quite go all the way to the end of the opening. (see photo) But if I lay the zipper pull the other direction and tuck it under the cover, it covers the opening, so it's probably fine and covered enough to keep dry. I like that these gloves have a rubbery placket to better keep water out. The battery is larger and flatter than the one in the listing photo. The faux suede palm and inner thumb make gripping things easy. The sleeve cuff on these is longer than on other gloves and is more likely to keep snow out of the glove. You can cinch the end of the cuff up snug as well.

These come in a nice looking, giftable box with a charger with two plugs so it can charge both batteries at once, and the batteries and gloves. There is no carry/storage bag. After they are charged, plug them into the built in cords in the zipper pockets of the cuffs. To turn it on, press the power button on the back of the cuff. To change the heat intensity, just press again. It cycles through the settings - high, medium, low, off, with each press, and the number of bars lit will show you what setting you are on. They heat up quickly. In about 30 seconds, you feel it warming, and after a minute or so, it's at full strength. And it's directional. Feeling the outside of the glove, I couldn't tell that it was heated at all, but from inside it was nice and warm. These heat the backs of your fingers and thumb as well as the entire back of your hand. Feels nice just to sooth sore, arthritic hands, too.

The straps tend to loosen after a while so you need to check on how tight but remember not to tight for once you go in the water and  take in air the suction will tighten on the mask.  The major problems are not enough cushions  in certain area and the snorkel angel and length all wrong. I would be willing to pay extra for the extension and U shape putting the snorkel higher in the water rather than just an inch maybe a bit more if you move your head down and cuts off your air. review_text:
Beautiful Piece of Equipment, But.... I have to say, this really is a beautiful, well made, well thought out piece of equipment. However, it did not come with instructions on how to work the non-traditional locking levers. It took a bit to figure those out, but we finally did (**instructions will be at the end of this review). And, *it should come with stipulations on user physical size limitations. In addition, it DID NOT come with and sanitary disposable covers, though it lists those as a selling feature. I purchased this for a friend who had detached retina surgery. Unfortunately, this device will not work for someone who is on the shorter side with a pudgy middle section. She is about 5'3" and maybe 250 pounds. She was not able to bend at the middle section enough to be able to lay her head in the post surgery required head position. It just would not work. We did set it up under the mattress as a trial, so she would be able to lay flat on her abdomen with her face in the cushion to sleep. That worked well. It was easy to set-up. We also finally grabbed an adjustable height table, so that she could lower it enough to be able to bend over at her mid-section (without the provided chest cushion as her weight prevented use of that), to be able to place her head bent over and flat in the face cushion. But, that required that she had to sit on the very edge of a chair, not back and comfortable. A position she could never maintain for 5 minutes, much less, 7 to 14 days as was required post surgery.
*Synopsis: for the person with an average size body, this is a very nice, well thought out, very usable post retina surgery piece of equipment. For shorter people who are overweight, this will not work.
**Lever Instructions: Twist the levers in the direction that loosens them. Once loose enough (not too loose) they can be bent over completely flat against the device into the locking position. Also, in our not getting the covers or any directions, it makes me feel though sold as new, someone may have purchased this before me and returned it. Too many things missing.

review_text:
Very nice jacket, not traditional "fleece". I've had lots of fleece jackets over the years and this one is a bit different material than what I'm used to, but it works really well and looks good too!

The material of this jacket is very soft and dense, the overall thickness feels slightly less than traditional fleece jackets but I would argue that the density of the material makes it warmer than traditional fleece jackets. The material is quite stretchy which helps with fitting it over other layers or for people who have a range of body proportions.

My only real complaint about the jacket is that waist rides up a bit during active activities. I think if the jacket was just a bit longer it would solve this problem. With that said, the bottom of the jacket does have a bit of elastic which keeps it snug to the body and prevents any riding-up from letting cold air in. It's a minor thing that hasn't been an issue from a warmth standpoint but I have noticed myself pulling the bottom of the jacket down on occasion.

All-in-all, I would definitely recommend this jacket.

We will have to sew them back on ourselves, which is disappointing for a brand new product, especially from Santa. But we’ll deal with it.

Pros:
Wide and long--plenty of surface area
Lots of studs -- 12 on each side
Fairly light weight
Standard 15mm flanges, old pedals off, new ones on, just the one open-end wrench.
Feet feel locked to the pedals -- I was sliding off stock pedals.
Bearings (so far) are super-smooth!

Cons:
A bit heavier than I hoped, but still acceptably light...my alloy pedals on my road bike are definitely lighter, even with toe-clips and straps.
No pedal reflectors. Not a surprise, I knew it when I bought them, but I wish they had them.

Otherwise, looking forward to my next ride.

review_text:
Great quality and fit, but a little warm. I ran across the meo lite mask and needed to try it because to my knowledge it’s the only mask that uses wool as it’s filter, which just sounds awesome. Also this mask is supposed to do a great job filtering coronavirus, basically as well as an n95 or kn95, but is reusable to save costs if you’re just using it to run to the market every so often.

A little background on me: I currently live in an area that is hard hit with coronavirus. I usually only use homemade masks because I have a pronounced nose and wear glasses and store bought masks really have not fit well. I’ve been looking for a better filtering reusable mask since kn95s also do not fit me well.

The meo lite mask feels well built. There are simple adjustments on the ear loops and the fabric is thick, soft, and well sewn. The filters themselves are also think and replaceable. They feel a lot more substantial than most reusable filters I’ve used, and the pocket where you place the filter is secure, much better than Velcro I’ve seen other reusable masks use.

Wearing the mask is a little warm probably due to the wool, since it’s winter it hasn’t bothered me. It doesn’t feel like wool, and you don’t actually have the filter against your face so if wool itches you that shouldn’t be a problem. The mask is easy to breath through as well and for me it formed a solid seal around my face without fogging my glasses.

The one downside I found is the medium mask does not cover under my chin. I personally prefer masks to hug the bottom of my chin because just feels more secure to me. I weigh 190 and am 6’ so usually I would buy a larger mask, but Amazon doesn’t carry this mask in large. My wife is much smaller than me and the mask fits her perfectly though.

I personally am super impressed with the meo lite mask and have recommended it to my friends. I might try to hunt down a large size to see if it fits a little better than the medium.

review_text:
Good for smaller pain. I have a reoccurring shoulder pain and this was pretty helpful. I put it on at the beginning of the day when it was starting to twinge a bit and within a half hour I was feeling pretty good. I don’t know if it would be helpful for really severe pain but for this everyday muscle fatigue (that I’m also trying to heal with regular PT) it did the trick. It didn’t feel especially warm to me but these type of patches never do so I think that’s just me.

I like the way the patches roll out and are easy to remove. They were the perfect size for me but for larger areas you might want to double up. There was a strong lidocaine-like smell when you opened the tube but I was pleasantly surprised that it was pretty mild once you put the individual patch on. It stayed in place all day and I didn’t have any real problems with it.

My only nitpicky thing is that the plastic tube the patches come in is a little too big for the product and feels a little wasteful, but I’m sure I’ll find some other use for it once I’ve used up the rest of my patches.

I was given this product complementary, but I’d still consider repurchasing on my own in the future.

review_text:
Fingers Crossed. I really have my fingers crossed with this one. It's a new product, and I hope very much that it's going to work flawlessly for a long time. It's a lot of money for a water bottle if it stops working right after the warranty is up, which is when most devices decide to call it quits. The battery is non-replaceable, so it's a concern as to how long the battery will last.
But for now, I'm in germaphobe heaven.
The first photo shows how nice looking the unit is. The second shows the top and the charger, the third is the unit fully charging with a slow blinking green light. It's fully charged when the light is a constant green.
It's a magnetic charger, and it must be somewhere where it's not going to be disturbed. It doesn't take much for the charger to disengage.
My experience with this product is that the cap must be fully screwed on in order for the disinfecting process to begin. That's a great safety feature since this type of light can permanently damage your eyes or skin. This is serious equipment.
Press the button on the top, and a blue light will start flashing to indicate that the UV light is on and sanitizing the contents. It's recommended to shake the bottle gently to further assist the efficiency.
To stop the cycle depress until a purple light appears, otherwise it periodically turns itself on to continue sanitizing.
And that's basically it.

You're going to have to learn to baby it a little bit. If you tend to leave the cup in the car during soaring temperatures, or during freezing winter months, you'll have to get over that. The cap can't be exposed to temperatures below freezing or above 140°. And while the carafe portion is dishwasher safe, as expected, you have to be careful washing the cap.
Small price to pay for purity.
Besides sanitizing water, my favorite feature is that it also sanitizes the bottle itself. No more smelly carafe.
I'll definitely be updating this review as I continue to cherish this, my new best friend in my germaphobe world.
In the future, will Philips offer a replacement cap for purchase if necessary, or will this bottle be discontinued? More colors and sizes? How long will this battery last? And, as forgetful as I am, what's going to happen when I inevitably leave it in the car too long when it's either too hot or cold? I'll keep you posted, and until then...
Fingers crossed!

review_text:
Good texture, helpful to track intake, minor issues. See pictures.

I love the texture of this bottle! It's very soft, can't really compare it to something haha. The measurements on the side are a bit confusing, it seems to have lines that are hortizal with a time on one side of the line and another time on the other side of the same line. Usually you don't measure how much you drink hortizally but vertically. Not sure why it has this like this.

The straw seems to fit well to the mouth piece. So far haven't noticed any leaking, but haven't tested it really. The mouth piece however does stain easily. Although I bought 7 of these for the family to get more water intake, the kids use flavoring packets for water, and it stained the mouth piece. It has no sugar I'm them so I'm not sure how it stained like it did.

It is easy to drink from overall. Only issues are when you get down to about the last line, it's more difficult to get solid suction of water, and you get a bit of air. The straw doesn't move of course so you have to angle your bottle. The air hurts me, so I just pour more water in it at that point. I'm not going to pour it out because I buy 5 gal jugs of water haha.

One other issue is when I leave water in it over night, because I often need a sip in the night or first thing in morning for dry mouth, the water tastes a bit odd. Maybe a plastic kind of taste, can't describe it. But it's not real powerful. I don't have this with cups of water.
The whole thing is not easy to clean. I have to put a soapy rag with water inside of the bottle and close the lid and shake it. Can't get inside the rubber mouth piece due to its shape, or the other part of the straw. I wring the soapy rag over it and rinse a lot.

It seems to be helpful to get everyone to drink more water. Now they can see how much they drink and don't feel the need to gulp water down fast, making it harder for them to want to drink more water.

product_name: Electronic Foot File (Silver Gray)
review_text:
No more holes in sheets and socks from dry hard cracked heels.. Not powerful and stops? No
I’ve seen reviews that say it stops when it’s pushed down to hard, this can be misleading. Several other units I’ve bought over the years are literally just a motor spinning some piece of sandpaper. This one is geared down; meaning that it spins slowly but with more power. If you do press too hard then it will stop; but I haven’t found a reason to press it that hard.

Size: Great
The size is perfect for not only doing your heel, but it’s small size let’s you do the bottom of your foot too.

Adhesive on Sandpaper:
Is strong and great, It hasn’t slipped or felt like it’s going to come off. After sanding both my feet the sandpaper still feels new. Although it white from dead skin it still works like it’s new.

Handle: The handle is small and easy to maneuver it is smooth which gives it a professional feel, but a rubber sleeve over the middle would of given me a better grip. But I’m just being picky it’s fine.

The only thing better but not as convenient is a small wood detailing orbital sander; However being designed for wood it can take too much off if you’re not attentive; So I don’t recommend that.

If your foot is really really bad then get a new rasp type sander and use that to get it under control then use this to keep it soft and normal. I don’t know how this wood work on “concrete hard” heels since I used a new rasp first. Btw: Rasps don’t last forever and eventually get dull; I just threw several away.

Following up with a good Urea type Creme should help maintain you new baby soft feet.

I’m going to buy another one just in case, because I don’t ever want to be without one.

review_text:
Excellent masks with a few disposable extras. These are very well-made masks, though the cloth is quite impermeable. They come packaged with some disposable extras, a laundry bag and a storage bag, which are okay but not high-quality, and each mask is enclosed in a ziploc package printed with hilariously poorly-translated Engrish instructions about cleaning and use.

The fit is excellent, with a well-made curved form, adjustable ear loops, and an excellent, long, flexible nose wire that makes it easy to achieve a tight fit around the nose (though the fit in the chin is still a little tight so that a wide yawn can pull the mask out of position). The nose wire is the best I've used on any cloth mask so far, and actually gives me a better fit around the nose than many N95s — though the mask obviously doesn't seal nearly as well on the rest of the face, and your inhalation and exhalation goes around the sides of the fabric more than it actually goes through, the nose wire still prevents glasses fogging very well, directing exhaled air down and to the sides instead of up toward your eyes. The outer fabric is very dense and impermeable, so there is still some clamminess when wearing it for a long time, but I find these masks quite comfortable.

review_text: Easy to learn and use. I have never snowshoed before and needed a winter activity to stay active outdoors. I did some research and found these were recommended for novices on general rolling terrain (that is, not for alpine climbing nor for deep powder). I ordered the large size which are rated 150# to 300# (68kg to 136kg) and can will fit larger size boots (I wear a US size 15). If you have never snowshoed, it does require a bit of practice to learn to walk with your legs apart so you don't step on the edge of the other snowshoe and take a tumble. I have been out 6 times and done some 8k+ treks through trails as well as through woods and they work great. The bindings lock in your boot size so there is no need to adjust for each use as long as you use the same footwear. The ankle straps release well for easy off and the ratchet tightening allows you to get a snug and secure fit, and the crampons keep you from slipping on icy spots on the trail. If you have not used snowshoes before I suggest you try them out somewhere easy until you get comfortable using them. Out on the trail you will want at least a good walking stick and ideally good poles to help with hiking and balance in uneven areas. Very happy with these!

review_text:
Don’t let this happen to your little one!. My 6-yr old is in her 2nd season of weekly ski lessons and she wiped out last night on a blue run- “a typical wipe out” described by my daughter’s ski instructor. My daughter explained later that it wasn’t a bad wipeout and that she didn’t cry (meaning she didn’t lose both skis) and was able to get back up and keep going.

So why does my daughter have such a cut on her face? How does the sharp inner edge of the goggles frame cause such a cut, you might wonder? Well, after feeling the foam lining along the bottom side of the inner frame, it was easy to feel and see that the way the foam was cut (or glued onto the inner frame) was very poorly done- foam was cut so narrow to hardly protect my daughter’s face from getting cut from the inter plastic edge of the frame. And the foam was glued too far downwards celm the frame in such a way that the frame easily touched the face of the wearer with just a little bit of pressure. Very atypical of the 25+ yrs of my skiing experience.

I was super excited by the great reviews, the look and features of these goggles, but because of this, I’m going back to buying a long-time reputable brand, Bollé. This is just unacceptable. I shouldn’t have to worry about my child’s face getting cut up by her ski goggles during a very common wipeout. I can’t imagine what would’ve happened on a worse fall!

Fyi- this photo was taken approx. 24 hrs after the actual incident. So this cut already had almost 24 hours of Neosporin and Band-Aid treatment. It definitely was worse upon picking her up from her ski lesson.

Well, it works, the light is bright, etc... I was surprised at how long it takes to charge the battery.. Maybe it is not an issue, but, it seems to charge at a very slow rate... So, now, the big fat question, would I buy another if I had to replace it? Yes! It has plenty of good stuff to make it a buy... One thing I like is the size!!! review_text:
Good Quality for the Price, But Has Issues That Other Reviewers Pointed Out. I bought the Me Galua kickboxing gloves. It's good not great. it runs a bit small for me though I believe I have thick hands for just measuring width doesn't provide good fit indication. Although, I still could fit based on sizing chart it was very snug. I believe a few/several reviewers said it was thin and didn't provide the protection they wanted and at least one said it chafed their knuckles. All of these comments are mostly correct. However, I like thinner gloves as it provides greater flexibility moving from one set of exercises to another. That being said, it will hurt a bit if you use a heavy punching bag and go all out. The wrist support is not great but I believe every MMA/Muay Thai style of gloves are going to have that issue so buy a size larger and get the inner wrap that look like bandages. Finally, it will chafe the knuckles and again, I believe any MMA/Muay Thai style of gloves will do that because the first and second knuckles are exposed. Since, your first knuckles are wrapped into your hands when you make a fist, it's only the second knuckles that are exposed. I believe only boxing gloves will guarantee no chafing to the second knuckles. However, you can try a couple of things: 1) Focus on hitting only with your protected knuckles doing your best not to make contact with bag and second knuckles - this is kind of hard to do but it will provide some protection as you won't make contact as often, not a great strategy 2) Use the inner wrap making sure you have a bit of coverage on the second knuckles. Both aren't great solution, best coverage wold again be boxing gloves.
Overall, for the price it's still worth it with issues and all. I've been using it daily for several days now and it's holding up really well, so again good for the price.
Quick Update: After I wrote review, the next day I used gloves again and noticed a tear in the seams. Hopefully, I can fix that. If I can fix it or get company to make it right, the rating still won't change. Just a bit disappointed that it would rip so quickly. I have a Go workout/weightlifting gloves I've used for over 6 years and it hasn't started to rip yet.
Update 2/19/2021:
I returned and received a new pair, so the company made it right. However, after just 3 uses they are again torn in same area - along the seam between the thumbs and index finger. I'm contemplating returning them and getting something else, but I think I may just sew them so I don't have to waste time and money driving to return this item again. However, I dropped my review another star down to 3.
Update 4/17/2021:
Well I did not sew the little tear and have been using it almost daily. The tear hasn't grown any, at least not that I can see with the naked eye. As I use it more and more and learn to better brace my wrist, I find the wrist support adequate though for someone new to punching it may be a big issue. Even now, my wrist buckles at a hard punch, partly due to my not bracing well enough and partly due to the minimal wrist support. The padding doesn't provide a ton a support but as I wrote earlier, I kind of prefer that but there are some punches where I can really feel the hard plastic neck of the Wavemaster. For me, it's fine for a new user, this may be an issue. Still, I like it, but not love it.

I really wanted to like these, but they seem useless. I highly recommend trying a different brand. Who cares if they stay on if they don’t numb anything?

review_text:
This thing is god awful.. This pole is not for anyone that is actually intending to fish. Once extended you only have flex in the last segment of the pole. And it has about as much action and sensitivity as a pool cue. I'm not sure what lure weight/line weight this is intended for, because the markings on the pole seem to be in a format that is not used in the U.S. I would not attempt to use a light line with this. This kit is so bad, I have my doubts as to whether the positive reviews are coming from actual customers.

The reel and included line/lures etc. are pure junk. The tiny spool of unmarked line appears to be about 2 lb. test monofilament that is way to light for a rod this stiff, and will not even adequately spool the reel that comes with it. The plastic reel does not look like it will hold up to much use. The retrieve rate is slow, the bail is rough and difficult to close (hallmark of a poor bail spring design), and the whole thing is poorly balanced for the long heavy pole. The lure box comes with some cheap plastic lures that you would never use, a few hooks and some weird sinkers.

The kicker is that this "compact" telescope combo is packaged in a zipper case that unnecessarily increases the size of the unit while adding no utility. review_text:
Fine Set of Heated Gloves. This is a review of Day Wolf Heated Gloves

What You Get (Figure-1)
1 pair heated gloves
2 rechargeable batteries
1 120vac recharger
1 storage bag
1 user’s guide

Charging the Batteries (Figure-2)
Before using the gloves for the first time, plug them into recharger, plug the other end into a 120vac socket, and charge until the light on the charging unit turns green.

Note: The green light on my recharger was so dim, I had to turn the lights down in the room, just to see it.

Assembly and Use (Figures 3, 4)
Once charged, unzip the battery pouch on the gloves, plug the batteries into the provided cords, and zip the pouch closed.

To turn the gloves on, simply press the large red button, located on the back of each glove.
First Press: Glove heating element set to high.
Second Press: Glove heating element set to medium.
Third Press: Glove heating element set to low.
Fourth Press: Gloves are turned off.

Note: When the batteries are getting low, the large red button will begin blinking. At your earliest convenience, remove the batteries and recharge.

Test
With fully-charged batteries, I checked for temperature and life of batteries.
The first test was inside at with an air temperature of 72f (22c)
• At high the battery lasted 1.9 hours, and the internal heat reached 168f (76c).
• At medium the battery lasted 3.5 hours, and the internal heat reached 124f (51c).
• At low the battery lasted 5.4 hours, and the internal heat reached 110f (43c).

The second test was performed outdoors with an air temperature of 38f (3c). The life of the batteries was the same as the first test, so I will just display the temperatures.
• At high the internal heat reached 127f (53c).
• At medium the internal heat reached 102f (38c).
• At low the internal heat reached 75f (24c).

It is to be noted that even with temperatures approaching the freezing mark, the low setting is typically higher than most people set the thermostats in their homes.

My final test was to take them for a little walk. The outside temp was right at the freezing mark with dark clouds and a bit of snow. I put my coat on, set the gloves to low, and took a 45-minute stroll in the snow. Even at the low setting, my hands were warm and comfortable.

Note: I used a professional thermo probe to measure the heat, and an electronic stopwatch to measure the length of time. I stopped measuring time when the large button began blinking.

I performed both tests twice with the same results.

Bottom Line
Well-constructed of sheep leather with a comfortable velvet liner. If you are looking for comfort, as well as warmth, these are a good choice.

review_text:
Damaged valves, defective product. Sea Eagle products are highly rated, which is why we went for Sea Eagle.

We've had 3 negative experiences with Sea Eagle so far, 2x on SE 330 and 1x on SE 370. Defects happen. The weight and size of product makes it cumbersome to return. I really do want a kayak, maybe I'll try the 370 again.

In this instance:
1- box was delivered in tatters. We kept it because it's painful to return and we were excited to finally get our kayak.
2- the valves were broken causing air leaks. The photos show that the valves are chipped. We did some troubleshooting and couldn't fix it, so we returned it. We have previously set up 2x SE 330s, so we're confident it wasn't user error.

I'll reiterate a caution I posted in my review on the SE 330 - the kayak is small. Great size for 1 adult or 1 adult + 1 kid. The product description describes it as a kayak for two adults, which is hard to defend.

I've messaged them directly about this and Sea Eagle "stands by its dimensions", which isn't quite the same as standing by the product claim that it fits two adults. In reality, the 330 can fit a combined height of about 10', far from two adults. My girlfriend and my combined height is closer to 11.5'. To both sit in the kayak our knees needed to be tucked halfway to our chest. (Uncomfortable + unable to paddle).

The 370 product description says it fits 3 people. The 370 can comfortably fit two adults, and maybe two adults and a small dog / child.

review_text:
You have to have faith. This bottle was delivered in no time. I guess it is working because the light on its cap is flashing in the way the manual describes. There are two things to bear in mind though:

1) it uses proprietary charging cable, meaning it will become an ordinary (nice looking) bottle if you lose the cable. They should have at least shipped a spare one or, like another brand I tried, to split the charging head from the cable so that users could change the cable when it breaks. Of course, using ordinary charging head such as USB C or at least mini USB will be way better. This is especially true that the cap isn't waterproof anyway.

2) except trusting the cap's light, you have no way to tell if the UVC light is actually on.

All things considered, it is a good purchase for me in light of the relatively cheap price and famous branding compared to competitors in this market. With the R&D capability of Philips, I expect that they will release a smart / pro version of this, allowing you to check in on the actual LED status or even detect the water quality.

product_name: Rawlings | Renegade Glove Series | Baseball/Slowpitch Softball | Multiple Styles
review_text:
Great glove for the price! (Updated review below). Second time I have purchased a Renegade, LHT 1st base glove for my 13yr old son. He lost his first one after having it for a little over a year. Loved it so much that we got the same exact glove. Broke in very quickly. That's usually a sign that the glove will not last many years but that's ok. This specific Renegade was a little different than his other in that this one has a small cutout where the palm hinge is. I personally dont like the way it makes the glove close however my son loves it. I took a star off for that hinge. Even though he loves it, that hinge is not for everyone. I dont like that a glove forces you to close it the way they design it and the hinge almost makes that happen. Again, you cant beat the price. I would have paid $100 for this glove.
He plays competitive travel ball and can easily take 70+ mph across the diamond and it doesnt hurt his hand so dont think this is only a little league glove.

Update Aug 2021.
We've had the glove for about a year and a half now and it has gotten extremely floppy. I had said that I was concerned with this "newer" model with the hinge in the corner and sure enough, this is a much different glove than the same model without the hinge. The hinge does make it easier to close however you are forced to close it a very specific way which some may not like. Now after 18 months, the glove has gotten too floppy to take some scoops and now you have to catch it in the pocket with very little room for error due to the floppy end. Again you get what you pay for. He is NOT an every day 1st baseman so with limited action, I definitely thought we would get more than 18 months before having to purchase a new glove. Still recommend for younger kids but not for 13+ who will use it a lot.

review_text:
an average, middle-of-the-road toothpaste when compared to name-brand sensitive toothpastes. Review of: Spotlight Oral Care Toothpaste for Sensitive Teeth

I’ve been using the Spotlight Oral Care Toothpaste for the last week or so and, so far at least, I’ve been pleased with the product.

I found that the taste of the toothpaste is actually pretty good, especially in comparison to other ‘fresh mint’ flavored toothpastes I’ve tried before that seem to have an off-taste or bitter after-taste them. The mint taste of the Spotlight is present but not overwhelming; which I like.

The foaming action of the toothpaste I consider to be about average; certainly, enough in my estimation to feel as if the toothpaste was getting to every corner of my mouth but not so much as to be annoying.

The active ingredients I also consider to be about average for a decent quality ‘sensitive’ toothpaste; Potassium Nitrate and Sodium Fluoride. And, after using the product a few times now, I consider the effectiveness (based on the potassium nitrate level of 5.0%) to be about the same as many other ‘sensitive’ toothpastes I’ve tried in the past.

After brushing, the Spotlight toothpaste does leave my teeth feeling clean and does leave my mouth with a nice, somewhat minty taste.

For me, while this toothpaste is noticeably better than some bargain-basement type sensitive toothpastes, it is roughly equal to many quality, name-brand or store-brand toothpastes.

The cost, however, for this 3.5 ounce tube of sensitive toothpaste is a concern for me as I consider it to be on the higher side; especially for what I rate as an average, middle-of-the-road toothpaste.

Does Not work on Android. The Android sleep app is not the one you need.. I bought this product in 2018 and enjoyed it for a few months before I stopped using it. I recently wanted to use it again and I don't have the same phone or the original log-in information. They emailed me log-in info but I couldn't get the app to work. After 2 messages with the seller I finally figured out what the problem is.

The app you need to use is called Sweetsleep, with no space between the words and is only found on the Apple App store for iPhone and iPad. So it worked on my old iPhone.

In the android Play store, there is an app called Sweet Sleep with a space between the words. It's not the same app and does not track your sleep patterns. It only plays music. So I can't use this with my Samsung S10.

I hope this helps people having the same issue.

product_name: WYZE Band Fitness Tracker with Alexa Built-in, Activity Tracker Watch with Heart Rate Monitor, Smart Fitness Band with Step Counter, Calorie Counter, Pedometer Water Resistant, Black
review_text:
Well, you get what you pay for.... Initially I was fascinated with the notion we now have decent fitness trackers with limited smartwatch capabilities for $25-$30. Well, that idea went into the trash almost immediately, as I became acquainted with what the Wyze band can and more importantly--cannot--do. The Wyze band is a lot of things, and great isn't one of them.

First, let me say, clearly, that for $25 or $30, this is a hard device to beat. If you keep your expectations (very) low, in line with the very low price of the unit, you will not be disappointed. The biggest frustration initially was with the lack of clear, helpful instructions. The instructions tell you it is charged out of the box, and that you should plug it in to charge to activate it. Um, okay. The home bar pulses when it is plugged in to the charger, leading you to think it is charging. Perplexingly, there is no charge indicator in the default display configuration while it is charging, so you just think it is still charging. In fact, pretty much everything in the default factory configuration is disabled, including Alexa, even once you set up your Alexa info in the app. Notifications are disabled by default, so nothing talks to the band. You have to turn on notifications, and then scroll through the entire list of all the apps on your phone to enable notifications for each specific app, including calendar reminders, messages, etc. Problem is, nowhere in the documentation (even online) does it tell you this step is necessary. People who are not comfortable messing around with their devices will be frustrated quickly. Nothing is intuitive, and there is no real guidance. It's fiddle-around time--geeks (like me) will be comfy with this. The average consumer will not be impressed at all, and may become quite frustrated.

However, set up frustrations aside, it's the things the Wayz band lacks which may disappoint the consumer. It's a long list, but again, remember this thing is dirt cheap. To begin with, the band has no external speaker. This means Alexa’s responses, when you can raise them (which is by no means assured), are in text on the screen in a *tiny* font. In fact, this tiny font is everywhere. If you wear glasses for reading, you will definitely need them to use this band. This means if you are out walking or running, and you're not wearing your glasses, the band is almost useless. This is where not having a speaker is a real detriment: Alexa cannot speak responses, and without my glasses I can't read them. This is due to the very small screen which is only 240 x 120 pixels. There simply isn't enough screen real estate for a larger font. This screen is *tiny*, and feels about half the size of the screen on an Apple watch. Another design issue worth noting, the band is the cheapest design I have ever seen, and it both looks and feels like it. The plastic clasp feels like it may break at any moment. Also, if you have large wrists like I do, you’re potentially out of luck. The Wayz band ships with only one band, and no larger band seems to be available.

You cannot really interact with this band much, which limits functionality. You can read your incoming text messages and notifications in that teeny tiny font, but you can't reply (or if you can, I've no idea how, as this is not covered anywhere and doesn't seem to be possible). You also cannot dismiss all notifications at once, and will have to scroll through all of them, dismissing them one at a time. A word to the wise: be conservative about which apps you allow to send notifications to the band. If you are all in, you are going to spend a LOT of time dismissing notifications. With the exception of talking to Alexa, which requires you to touch the screen, communication with this band is almost entirely one-sided--you cannot input anything on the band at all, and you must use the app on your phone to interact with it--which begs the question… why am I wearing this again?

Wyze have also not included the ability to control music playback (or anything else) from your phone. With the exception of the heartbeat monitor and sleep tracker, this device primarily functions as a tiny supplemental screen for your phone to give you alerts (and the haptic buzz is STRONG). From what I can tell, the sleep tracking, step counter, and heart rate monitoring are far from accurate, rendering this device mostly useless. Also, if your activity of choice is not walking, running, or jogging, you’re out of luck--it can’t track anything but steps and heart rate, and as it seems to consistently get those wrong, it really does sort of feel like a waste of $30. Perhaps more than anything else, the Wyze band serves as a great advertisement for other, superior fitness trackers, as all the shortcomings of this device just make me want to get a really good fitness tracker/smartwatch and toss this thing.

It should be noted there is also as serious issue with the way the band communicates with the phone. This really was not well-designed at all on the app side. In order for the band to interact with your phone, the WYZE app MUST be running on your phone at all times. This has several implications: 1) security (it can potentially capture everything you do on your phone), 2) it munches up phone battery, and 3) if you close the app, nothing will work, including Alexa. This is *really* uncool, and has contributed significantly to my decision to return it and spend a bit more on another, superior fitness tracker instead. It’s going back.

review_text:
Junk tubes.... A little background - my CX bike is more of a light trail bike, but gets ridden a lot. Original tires and tubes lasted for thousands of miles; when the tires were completely worn through, I decided to treat my bike to some new tubes.
That set of tubes lasted for thousands more.
This last winter I decided to set up my CX indoors on a trainer, and put on a new rear tire (my Kenda mild knobbies were ungodly loud on a trainer, as you might imagine). Said training tire was a bear to put on and take off; and when I removed it a few weeks ago I goofed and pinched the tube a bit with the tire levers (my normal Kendas can be installed and removed with a firm hand and no levers), and poked a tiny little hole in it.

In a hurry to get out on the trails, I ordered this two pack of tubes (and used my mountain bike in the meantime), even though I only needed one (I do like having spares on hand, though they normally last me years at a time).

Fast forward to delivery... open a tube, mount it to the rim, throw the Kenda back on. Pump it up, and set the bike to the side for the next day’s ride.

Next day - go to load my bike in the car... and the rear is flat.

I’ll censor my next few words. Pulled the tire and tube off; checked my rim, rim tape, and tire for anything that may have caused an issue. All clean and clear. Grab tube #2, mount it (no levers), air it up, and head out to the trail (this was a rails to trails - so nothing even close to trying for a tube).

15 miles in to the ride, things are feeling a bit spongy - look down and back - and sure enough, the tire is loosing pressure. Was fortunate enough to find a trail side pump (didn’t bring a mini or inflator; foolishly thought it was short enough of a ride and I am used to going years at a time on tubes) and pump it back up. Squeaked out 22 miles, and put the bike back in my car.

Unloaded it the next morning (while loading the mtb), and yeah - completely flat.

0/2. I’m perfectly willing to admit (and aware) when I goof up and ruin a tube - that didn’t happen here - these are just junk tubes. Complete waste of time and money; even if I had a 3rd sitting on the shelf I could never use it at this point, as I’d be worrying/waiting for it to fail if it was ever mounted.

review_text: The 3-year Warranty Means Nothing. These are fine kayaks unless you have a warranty claim. We bought one last summer that had a slow leak near the valve. It took me a while to figure out, and eventually I contacted VM Express about it. They passed me on to Sea Eagle, who provided a little troubleshooting that didn't fix the problem. By the time you've paid shipping you're in the cost of another kayak. You get stuck with a lot of useless plastic and they keep selling their product under the guise of a warranty that makes naïve buyers confident that they aren't wasting their money. Sea Eagle is complicit in this...they also advertise a 3-year warranty but with VM Express as their proxy, they have nothing to lose if an occasional buyer ends up wasting their money. Not the case with this Spotlight Oral Care Toothpaste, it has Potassium Nitrate and Sodium Fluoride instead. It works to calm tooth pain and still leaves my mouth fresh! review_text:
Warm, not overly hot. Just completed my first snowboard season testing these heated gloves out.

Here's my key thoughts:

1. They stay dry. Plenty of days of melting snow or even some misting rain and the waterproofing on the fingers held up well.

2. The heat in these gloves is not overwhelmingly hot. Hot Hands gets hotter than these gloves do. That said, there is definitely warmth provided by the electricity in the gloves, but don't think you're sticking your hands into a heater by any stretch. There were some bone cold days and these gloves just couldn't make a difference even on the highest setting.

3. The batteries are a little bulky and sit weird on my wrist. For me I don't like having these boxes sitting on my wrists. It's not obtrusive but it's completely noticeable.

4. These won't make it a full day on the slopes. We got out around 8AM on the first lift and by 2pm these things were dead. Charging takes too long so it's not something you can do over lunch. You'll either have to buy more batteries to swap out or go without the heat in the later day.

Would I buy these? I don't know. They're pretty pricey and I just wish they got hotter. For me they're a nice to have, but definitely not a must have.

review_text: Awesome gadget. When I first opened the dog grooming set, I was skeptical. Even thought everything was nicely packaged.  It came with three attachments and is battery operated. Doodles have more coarse hair then our Maltese.  I  am afraid to try to use the clippers to do a full shave because the last I want to do is burn out the clippers. Heavy duty clippers ( professional) should only be used for a full shave. I bought these with the intentions of cutting around their eyes, beards, and in between their toes. 176 The trimmers work perfect for these areas. Again, I am not a professional groomer, and I am not used to cutting or filing down our dogs nails. Luckily we have dogs who loved to be groomed and pampered, so our dogs will just sit on the couch with their paws on a towel in my lap while I filed their nails. Again the filing tool worked great for our little Maltese. As for the Doodles it seemed to take way longer and did not seem powerful enough. After filing my dog Thias nails for ten minutes on one paw, I really could not notice too much of a difference between the filed paw and not filed paw . I would personally recommend this product to anyone who has furry animals for maintaining their animals nails or for small trims.  The attachments are extremely easy to take off and put on. The package it small enough that it is great for traveling or compact storage.  The product is extremely easy to clean. 346 If you are afraid to file or trim your dogs nails because you are afraid of hurting them by filing the nails too short then the filing attachment will work perfectly for you. I personally would  start to feel nauseous while trying to file or trim our doggies nails but with this attachment it is impossible to file the nails too short. 409 The little grips on the side of the tool make it safer to trim without your hands slipping and then you end up with a chunk of fur missing. I do feel that the batteries worked way stronger then the charged system. The trimmers also were not as loud as other clippers that we have and have used in the past.  Our professional clippers are so loud that they scare our Maltese and we are not able to calm him down enough to even let the clippers get near him. The sound freaks him out so much. review_text:
Boom and bust ( the good, bad and ugly side of the Bowflex M8). BOOM - When I first received this product it was amazing! The Wife and I built our entire workout regiment around different programs on this machine. We were using it about 6 times a week total (her M,W,F. Myself - T,TH,S) the 14 minute programs are all you need to have a great and complete workout.

BUST - I have owned this max trainer 10 months and thus far it has only been operational for 6 of the 10 months. The first time they replaced the entire body because the handle sheered off mid workout (thank goodness it happened to me and not the wife) it took 6 weeks to replace the motor body. The second time happened two weeks ago and the machine doesn't register any movement when you step on it ( They are in the process of replacing it now) est. time to the replacement piece arrives is 6 weeks again.

UGLY - Additionally, they will only replace exactly what is wrong with the machine and not the entire machine itself. You have to do the additional labor to add the part back in. There is something clearly wrong with my machine but instead of replacing everything and giving me a new one they would rather send me the parts and walk me though how to fix it myself. Then I have to put back on the other parts for first machine. And what happens to the old body you asked? Nothing, I had to pay to dump the entire machine body at my city's landfill because they took no responsibility for the machine's break down. I feel as if I gave you $2,300 for a machine (that is not even a year old yet) you should a least cover the first repair with a professional or assist with the removal of the old machine ... Maybe I'm old fashioned?

Overall, If you get this machine it is capable of great things and you will reach allot of your fitness goals but be prepared to become a mechanic and garbage man. Also, please set aside an additional 3 hours per breakdown just to call them and help the person on the phone identify the problem with your machine then repair your own machine after it breaks down.

review_text:
Buyer, use caution. I recently purchased ReMag and have been using it for about a week. I was eager to buy it based off the reviews and what I read in The Magnesium Miracle. I did notice a difference in how I slept (I don't suffer from any sleep issues, but I noticed deeper sleep while taking it). I also feel a general sense of calm (I have had anxiety off and on, and I seem.to feel a bit better).

However, upon reading further reviews, someone mentioned that it may contain lead, to which I grew concerned. I don't remember the name of the reviewer, but it was one of the 1 star reviews on Amazon. Thry did not indicate what lab did the resting or how they came across the information, so I looked deeper into it.

I was able to find information on ConsumerLab.com, in which they independently tested multiple magnesium supplement brands. The information is copyright protected, so I won't share the details here, but you can pay for an account and receive the full report (and others).

Their findings did indicate there was lead contamination. I would recommend viewing the report so that you can judge for yourself as to whether or not you wish to continue taking the supplement.

I personally will not continue taking it as I would prefer to have a pure product with no contaminants (especially no lead).

I have found another that I will purchase instead – Nutricology Magnesium Chloride.

It sucks because I spent quite a lot of money on it, but there is no value on my health.

I give it 2 stars because it actually did seem to help, but I cannot give a full recommendation given the information I know now.

review_text: Overall good quality helmet.. As a disclaimer, I purchased this helmet as it did seem to check all of the boxes and then made the decision to buy it after finding it at a significant markdown combined with some credits from Amazon.  It was hard to pass up.  Overall I find it to be a good quality helmet.  As others have mentioned in reviews, the feel on the head is somewhat like the way a "hardhat" sits on the head- a little high center, which must have been the design.  Ventilation seems very good.  I went with size L as I am on borderline, between M and L.  But in past MTB helmet purchases,  the M felt too small.  This helmet I think I could have gone with an M and been okay.  In this case, I do wear a "bandana" or "do-rag" under the helmet.  Other reviewers commented about its weight, that it is heavier than most MTB helmets but after wearing it for rides lasting several hours, the weight of the helmet was never an issue or even a thought.  I suffered no headaches from the fit and tension of the helmet as reported by other reviewers.  Pos that stand out; 1.  it feels substantial as far as protection & MIPs, 2.  Simple design as far as headband tension system that worked well for me with the goal to be sunglass friendly.  3. comfortable.  4. Its basic design seems well made and simple (with KISS being the standard).  And so being a good basic design, it feels like it will do for which it was designed, very well.

review_text:
Gorgeous, stylish, holds the bottle perfectly. When I ordered this for my 20 ounce thermos-style bottle (Iron Flask), I hoped the carrier would be close to what the photo showed. (I ordered the blue-turquoise one with the dandelion-ish white design on the side.)

In real life, it's just as gorgeous - or more so - than the photo on the Amazon page. It holds my 20-ounce Iron Flask snugly enough that the thermos won't slip out, but perfectly so I can slide the thermos out easily, to refill or clean.

I've already washed this carrier once - in the washing machine, and then air-dried - and it came out as good as new. No shrinkage of the fabric or the stitching.

I did not wash the shoulder strap, and it's fairly firm. That is, it's adjustable, but - brand new, anyway - it feels a little stiff. That's probably a good thing, long-term, for durability.

I'm delighted with this carrier. I do wish this color/design came with a zipper pocket on the side, to serve as a wallet. That's the only negative, so far, because carrying a purse and this... it's kind of awkward.

But, for situations where I can put my driver's license (etc.) in a shirt or trousers pocket - like for hiking or a theme park visit - this carrier is ideal.

I may order more, in other colors and designs. The product is well-made and - in my opinion - a very good deal.

review_text:
So far, so good! Nice cushy, stable ride.. I've had 2 other GOTRAX scooters but sold and chose this one because it is rear wheel drive and has a very nice menu of other features, one of which is great lighting. i belong to the GOTRAX scooter owner's FB page and I am well aware that there is a possibility of flat tires and error messages that can come up in scooterville. And there are remedies to the error messages and tires can be repaired. Ya gotta just get creative and do your research if it happens to you. That said, none of my other scoots have pneumatic tires. But this Apex has it's charm, a smooth cushy stable ride, and so I roll. Supposedly the factory puts Slime in the tires to help with flat prevention but you can do that yourself or upgrade to honeycomb or solid tires. Many bike shops that sell electric bikes will swap out tires for you and how-to videos abound on YouTube. This scooter has a nice, wide rubber padded floorboard. It folds easily. The display is bright and you don't have to worry about using an app. The lighting is strong and features a tail light. I am getting the stated range and speed but I am a slow cruisin' kind of gal. You cannot beat the price. The only reason I am not riding a G4 instead of this one is the complicated locking gadget on the G4 that was a put off for me. No thanks. I have another brand scoot that will carry me 25 miles on a charge with no chance of flats. But I will keep and love my Apex. It is basic scooting on a cloud and I hope it keeps running. Would buy again over any of the lower priced GOTRAX models.

Oh, yeah, forgot to mention that it has an odometer which is really a plus and it is very easy to fold and carry to put in my car for trips to the park.

The tire was round and straight with no visible runout. It rolls smoothly on the street with no anomalies. I'm pleased, time will tell on wear. For my needs it looks to be a good fit. review_text: You're better off sitting on this than on the fence about buying it.. If you're in the market for an exercise ball, you already know why you need it. I can confirm that they are good for L5-S1 pain because you have to use good posture to sit on one and they do distribute your weight well in regards to the pain triggered by pressure on the tailbone, but that doesn't tell you why you should buy this one versus others. Of course not all exercise balls are created equal and you don't want to waste your time or money on one that feels like it is going to pop and drop you on your already sore backside, so I can tell you this one is hefty. It is the size advertised, so if it is too big or small for your needs, that's for you to figure out,  but I can say at 5'4" tall with a 26" inseam, I  definitely wouldn't go any bigger than the 65mm ball that I bought. The pump is small and slow but functional and most importantly included, as is a nice thick poster of exercises to go with the ball, base, and adjustable bands. The base doesn't fit the ball as snugly as you might expect, but it does keep it from rolling out from under you while still forcing you to stabilize yourself on it (which is kinda half the point for most users) so I don't consider it to be an issue. Yes it comes with a 2 year warranty but I doubt you'll need it based on how well made it is and mine came with a bonus offer for posting the most helpful Amazon review. All in all, aside from the cheesy little pump, which you'll probably only need to use use one time anyways which makes it not worth paying more to upgrade, this kit is a total win at $28+tax.

review_text:
NotSoHot. This is more of a heads up review. First, the items is not returnable, I missed that little detail on my purchase. Next, the listing ad has these words as the first words of the ad: Rapid Remover Vinyl Letter Remover. This sort of gave me the impression this product would remove my vinyl letters rapidly. The instructions on the non-returnable product says: step 1. Remove decal, use heat gun.... 2. Spray product.....

What I learned about the non-refundable bottle is it removes the glue and maybe not the Vinayl letters.

So since I can’t refund the bottle, I gave it a try. First, for my purpose, the heat gun was almost enough. However, for what glue was left behind, this product took care of it. Honestly though in a side by side, goof off worked as well with a more controllable application method. In fact, this product left streaks of discoloration or Re coloration as the case may be (my rig has yellowed a bit)

Overall for the price I would not see myself buying this product again. Glad I bought the small $32 bottle as it will last a life time.

review_text:
Great value great product. Light weight, applies pressure and grip at the right points a natural fit and flexible unlike most gloves. Finger tabs work good when pulling gloves off to keep them from turning inside out. My experience there are many popular gloves look good but are not a natural fit under compression. The materials are a soft cloth, nylon and a gel-type (on palm) no leather, leather in my experience always stiffens, deforms and can shrink over time not good.
My hands are large so I ordered extra large for good measure and this was a good move I suggest you order the next size up as they will also adjust down a size due to the nature of materials and construction. My hands are 'large' and the XL is a good fit.
There is a unique gel a serrated pad on the palm side that has four spaces or cut outs to allow flexibility when gripping in lieu of the typical solid thick pad this creates a much stronger compression for gripping the bar. I was not impressed with the flat box they came in although a nice box I didn't think the gloves would amount to much but once I got them out they came to life high quality! I enjoy using these gloves and will probably order another pair in a different color. All in all exceeded my expectations.

Battery Issues!. This is a sharp looking little light. The shape immediately put me in mind of the mid-60's Thunderbird. The gloss black and chrome really pop. The mounting system is very versatile. Some complain of the strap being too short, but that could easily be remedied with a zip tie. That's what I liked, but that's not the entire story. I ride 1 1/2 to 2 hours at a time 5 to 7 days a week. I set the light to daylight flash, but it cut out in the middle of my 3rd ride twice with enough charge left to come back on if the power button was pushed. This is not acceptable.

Another gripe I have is that this company's other lights flash blue. Hoping to be mistaken for a bicycle cop is disrespectful to both law enforcement and motorists besides being illegal in most places.

The B1 light would work for someone who takes short bike trips and doesn't mind frequent charging. It would look really nice on a cruiser bike.

The battery lasts about 10 days for me between charging. Synchronizing is easy.  For aprox $20, it is a decent watch/smart watch. review_text:
generic quality but functional. Modern lightweight bicycles use a lot of small bolts and you really need to pay attention to how much torque you use on these bolts to avoid damaging your bicycle. Torque settings are often printed on the components or you can often find the settings on the manufacturers' websites.

This is a generic-quality tool. It looks and functions just like a number of other bicycle torque wrenches sold on Amazon. It comes with 3 Torx bits (T10, T25, and T30) and 8 hex bits (2 to 10mm). That covers most bolts that you will find on modern road or mountain bikes. The smaller sized head and shorter length make this tool easier to use on a bicycle where working room is limited.

Build quality is very good for this price. The wrench is easy to use and feels solidly built. The micrometer-style mechanism makes setting your desired torque very easy. Torque accuracy is very good when the tool is new, but long-term accuracy is iffy for tools of this quality level. The Amazon product page says it has a lifetime warranty, but the literature that comes with the tool says to look at the company website for the warranty details and I could not find anything there.

Harbor Freight sells a cheaper bicycle torque wrench, but this one is better quality.

review_text:
5 Star for super fit smaller folks.. 1 star for way too small for bigger folks. I am leaving 1 star primarily because there is no information regarding size fit.. it appears to be a one size fits all. As a bigger guy who is a wee bit overweight (like 50lbs or so).. looking to add some extra workout to help me lose weight.. I assumed the one size fit all accounted for larger folks. The 5 star is the quality..it is indeed top notch, and for my 6' HS kid, this fits with room and he'll get use out of it. For me, I can't even come close to using the side straps to tighten it up. They are WAY WAY too short. It does fit over my neck fine, which is another reason for 1 star.. why would you offer such an otherwise quality product, with straps WAY too small to fit a size 48 chest. I will try to rig some sort of rope or something around it I guess to tighten it up with.. but I am really disappointed for this price, that they didn't make the straps longer to account for larger folks. I know some may think "larger folks" means very round.. I am not very round.. just a few extra pounds, no joke. But I am big boned, and have broad shoulders. I suspect I will need to drop 40 to 50 lbs and 3 or 4 coat sizes before I might be able to see the straps fit, if that.

So.. if you are smaller to mid sized, or even a bit larger but very low body fat.. this may work well for you. If you are a bit broader/larger.. looking to add another way to help lose some weight and get in shape.. just know that this is going to require some extra jerry rigging to be able to use properly. If you can live with that (which I can since my kid will use it too), and lose some weight/size, you may finally be able to use this as intended.

What they should do is put a max size.. which I suspect is like 6' or so, 220lbs tops, and if you are really well built and that large, this may still not work well.
