product_name: Pogo BPA-Free Tritan Plastic Water Bottle with Chug Lid, 18 Oz, Blue
review_text:
Don't brag unless you can back it up. There's 2 major things wrong with this bottle, both in the lid:

1) It leaks when turned upside down
2) The small drink opening means it takes forever to chug water if you're thirsty
One minor thing wrong:
3) It's really hard to unscrew the lid if you over tighten, which is very easy to do.

This is weird because the manufacturer goes to great lengths in their product description to brag about their "leak proof lid" and "wide mouth chug opening." If they had just kept their mouth shut, I might not have minded as much.

The bottle itself is pretty sturdy. I've dropped it while full and it hasn't cracked or broken. The flip lid works great, and hasn't loosened up or broken after a few months of hard use.

The lid only leaks when the bottle is completely inverted; it's very leak-proof in a car cupholder sloshing around or dangling from a belt loop. However, it can't be used as a shaker bottle for iced tea, protein powder, etc. (which is why I bought it) Water sprays everywhere as soon as you start to shake it.

Overall it's a pretty ok bottle. I'd bump from 2 stars to 3 if they hadn't specifically marketed it as leak-proof. But c'mon, it's 2021; how hard is it to make a plastic water bottle that doesn't leak? Just pay a few bucks extra and get a Nalgene, that's what I ended up doing.

review_text: ABSOLUTELY AMAZING!! NO-BRAINER PURCHASE!!. Bought this after reading a review elsewhere from a professional detailer. Figured it would be just like goo-gone and not work any better, but we were desperate. I tried goo-gone on the old decal glue on the truck and it did nothing whatsoever. Not even with a magic eraser. Opened this bottle of Rapid Remover and it smells just like goo-gone. Uh-oh! Well, I can assure you it is NOT goo-gone. Sprayed RAPID REMOVER on the old glue residue and in less than 5 minutes the truck door was as clean as a whistle. You'll definitely want a plastic razor to scrape the stuff. We bought one of those rubber wheels thinking we'd need to use that, too, but NOPE!! This stuff really is amazing. It took me longer to get the red rubber stopper out of the bottle than it did to remove 4 lines of decals on the side of one truck door!! Spray on, wait 1 to 1-1/2 minutes, scrape off (SLICK!!!), grab a rag and spray a little on the rag, wipe up any leftover residue, grab a spray bottle of water, rinse the door and you're done! Some spots we had to spray a little more on, probably didn't give it quite enough time to do it's thing. Seriously, though, this was a GREAT PURCHASE. On hindsight, I would have purchased a much, much smaller bottle. We probably didn't use even 2 ounces to do two truck doors!! Now that we've got it, it will be nice to have this stuff on hand when another tough decal or similar comes up! We're already trying to think of things to use it on, it's that much fun to see something work so well! Highly, highly recommend and I'll try to add before & after pics soon.

review_text:
Works as advertised, but isn't very useful. This fitness band works exactly as advertised. The battery life of 10 days? Darn close to reality - I get a 20% battery warning at 7 days, and I recharge it when I get that warning. The Alexa microphone works well - I can tell Alexa to turn on my lights or whatever, and it Just. works. Alexa notifications show up as text, because the band has no loudspeaker, but that's fine. The app (I'm an android user) works perfectly too, and does not seem to hurt my phone's battery life at all. The various features, like weather, "light", app notifications - they all work exactly as advertised, also. In fact the one complaint I could find about this band is that although it is waterproof, you really should not wear it into the bath or pool because the touchscreen doesn't know you're underwater, and it will keep lighting up and navigating randomly. Super minor quibble, but now you know.

So with all that said... It does exactly what the label says it should do - and that isn't enough. It really isn't very USEFUL because it isn't part of a bigger fitness ecosystem. Do you care what your heart rate was at 4:17am on Tuesday? If yes, then this device will answer that question. Are you trying to get fit and participate in an exercise regimen? If yes, then this device won't really help you in that goal.

Good hardware, reliable software, awesome price - exactly what I'd expect from Wyze - but it's missing some piece of secret sauce that would make it part of a bigger picture.

review_text:
Broke first time I used it. I'm going to list the cons first because there's a big one: it broke the first time I used it! The directions say not to worry if the pole joints are a little twisted when you open it, just untwist them and you're good. Nope. One of them broke while I was untwisting it, and I wasn't being rough. It snapped at the joint.
*The windows also kind of sucked. You can't zip them.

Now that that's out of the way, there were some pretty great pros as well.
*The size was perfect, big enough to be comfortable, but not excessively big.
*The black inside helped keep us cooler in 110 degree heat.
*Mostly easy to set up.
*Very lightweight.
*I like that you can zip it up to change in.

So, if you're willing to chance it, it could be a great product. But I will be returning.

UPDATE - The company reached out to me and sent a new tent to try. Lake days are over for us for the year but I look forward to trying it next summer. Hoping this one is better. Great customer service.

review_text:

The backpack leaves something to be desired, however. There are two pockets on the shoulders that close using stretchy elastics with slides. I took this pack hiking and within a few miles (and no pulling, yanking, or heavy weight in the pack) one of the cords came right off in my hand while I was sliding the little slider up it. That's pretty bad. It's also fairly difficult to sew back on, because it's attached within a fold of the pack where the seam is covered. My repair is ugly but functional. However, I try to buy these types of gear for the long haul and I really think that they shouldn't fall apart so easily.

review_text: Not as lightweight as advertised. For some reason my initial review was flagged for violating community guidelines, so I want to be clear why I have a problem with this hammock. For backpacking, weight is everything. I have been considering investing in a backpacking hammock as a lighter-weight alternative to my backpacking tent, which weighs just under 3 lbs. But I've never camped in a hammock before and I want to know that I enjoy it before spending $200+ on a setup from REI. When I saw this hammock, the price was great and the advertised weight was 1.8 lbs, so it seemed like the perfect option for what I'm looking for. When the hammock arrived, it felt heavier than I was expecting right out of the package, so I put it on a scale. Sure enough, it weighed in at 2.6 lbs, nearly as heavy as my backpacking tent. This is disappointing to me, and the seller should update the weight on the page to reflect the actual weight. In backpacking, a pound is a big deal. This is not what I signed up for. That said, for the price point I will probably hold onto this and take it on a one night backpacking trip to try out hammock camping, but at 2.6 lbs, this won't be a long term solution for me.

review_text:
*Updated review* Losing faith in Wise Owl!! Poor quality control.. *UPDATED REVIEW*: In my initial review I loved the towels and only docked a star because the colors were off slightly. I'm now down to 1 star and feeling disappointed for trying to support a lesser-known American brand. I should've just gone with a more affordable option like Walmart for a no-name towel....

At the time I received my towels I didn't notice they were two different styles, we didn't unpackage them and they came in identical carry sacks. I realized when we used them together this weekend they are different. His towel has rounded edges and a soft fabric tag. My towel set has a cheaper-feeling paper tag and square edges. Again, these aren't make-or-break issues for a camp towel but I literally bought two of the SAME THING at the SAME time - it's not like I bought one last year and a newer style replaced the old one. Why couldn't you just send me two of the same thing? And why do none of the photos show a rounded edged towel?

UGHHHH. I've come away feeling like this company is not all it's cracked up to be and the products are misrepresented. It's a shame!!! I repped Wise Owl hard and bragged to many of my climbing/outdoorsy friends that I found an affordable and cool start-up. I've purchased Wise Owl towels, a camp pillow, a camp blanket, and was gifted their hammock. I feel like I know the products well and I'm sad to say I won't recommend some of them.

ORIGINAL REVIEW: I'm an avid camper and climber. I found out about Wise Owl after receiving a hammock as a gift (it's awesome btw). I decided to try these towels to save some space in our packs (my partner and I have been lugging around standard bath towels). I purchased the Red set in XL and gifted him the Marine Blue set in XL. We are camping this weekend so I decided to take my towel out of the bag for a test run.

Pros - Comes in a carry sack that packs easily. ​Just as absorbent as my regular towel, soft, and large enough to dry me off completely including my hair. I could probably get by with the Large size if I wanted to save even more space. The snap loop will be nice to use to rig the towel up on a tree branch without getting tree bits all over the towel.

Cons - **IF COLOR IS IMPORTANT TO YOU: The Red is much more like the Orange listing. Easy to see in my orangey-coral bathroom. The Marine Blue is not Aqua either as the listing shows, but much more like the one listed as Royal Blue (no pics because my partner took his home with him). Both have the correct tags attached so I know I didn't get the wrong items. A little disappointing because I was attempting to color coordinate gear so I knocked a star off for that.

The Beats are Back!. I've used my Ion Tailgater a lot over the years, for picnics, events, even while working in the yard, and almost always on battery, so it was a great disappointment a few weeks ago when I turned it on and, after just a few minutes, got nothing but noises and distortion. Thankfully, it didn't take long to pin the problem down to a worn-out battery, and when I found the Unicell TL1245 F1 Replacement Battery on Amazon I ordered it immediately. In a few days - well ahead of the estimated delivery date - the new battery arrived; I installed it in a few minutes, plugged in the Tailgater to charge the new battery, and by that evening was rocking again.

The Unicell TL1245 F1 Replacement Battery is very slightly larger than the battery I took out; while the original came from the factory with strips of foam tape to keep it from rattling in the battery box, the Unicell replacement was a snug - but not too tight - fit and required no foam tape cushioning. Otherwise, the new battery seems to be a perfect replacement for the original, giving the same operating time and the same low-distortion volume levels. I had worried that a new battery might cost so much as to not be worth doing, but this was certainly not the case.

review_text:
Heavy and awkward. Wheel holders break.. The concept of a hitch mounted bicycle rack is nice. In practice, it's not so great.

1) This rack is heavy. It is very awkward to hold the rack steady while you align the main support with your trailer hitch so it will slide in. You'll likely be crouched over, straddling the rack, shuffling forward, trying to get it attached.

2) You must do this while not disturbing the nut insert that secures the rack. Bump that nut insert out of place and you'll be starting the process all over again.

3) With bikes on the rack, it may or may not be possible to open the rear hatch of your vehicle (even with the rack lowered).

4) There are three plastic ratcheting straps per bike. Loading bikes on and off this rack is not a quick procedure.

This rack also has lots of plastic parts. Wheel holders, frame holders, three ratcheting straps for each bike. No problem, if they break, they'll be covered by the Limited Warranty. Right.....?

Nope.

All of those plastic parts are SPECIFICALLY EXCLUDED from warranty coverage.

I used this for a full day of snorkeling in Maui. It worked as promised, however I was not a huge fan of the venting function. Breathing in works as normal, however when breathing out, your breath is vented through what I believe to be silicone or rubber plugs in the front of the mask. In theory this is a nice idea, especially if you are worried about carbon dioxide build up. However it also pushes a significant amount of bubbles out the front of the mask, which obscures your vision and may alert any wildlife you’re spying on.

While I have not experienced any issues with water leaking into the mask, the force of breathing out concerned me and I often found myself putting a hand on my mask to make sure it didn’t lift off of my face.

The same way I do for my scuba mask. The next time I wore them, I thought they had fogged in the water but it was a horrible white film that wouldn't come off even with rubbing alcohol. When I brought them home, I gave them a vinegar treatment and that removed the white film but now they fog the second I get in the water so they're basically useless until I add a secondary coating of RainX or baby shampoo or something. Very disappointed that the goggles didn't come with info saying they had a coating inside or with directions how to treat them. The fit is great, they don't leak at all, but if they fog they're useless to me. I'll update this review after I treat them and report on how well the treatments work to keep them from fogging. Just very bitter about it - the film should not have turned white the way it did after one use.

review_text:
Great mid level balance bike. I did a ton of research on balance bikes for my 3.5 year old. He was ready graduate off his tricycle and I wanted something sturdy but not a ridiculous price point.

So let me start by saying I often buy mid-level products. I don’t want a piece of cheap junk, but I also don’t want to waste money on high end products. Especially things that little kids use for maybe one or two seasons.

The Strider has been an excellent purchase. I looked at the Woom (which if you’re looking for high end bikes then that’s the one to get), and I just couldn’t justify the price point. I looked at cheaper bikes (like less than $50) and I was seriously concerned about quality and sturdiness.

Balance bikes cover a very short period of a child’s life. A couple of seasons is all you’re going to get out of them no matter what you buy.

Yes. The Strider has “plastic” (or rather foam core wheels) instead of real rubber or air tires and the treads have worn down significantly with very little use. However, my son has no problems with slipping or falling based on the wheel material.

No. The Strider does not have any hand brakes. But honestly: does it need them? My 3.5 year old is using his feet just fine. It’s not like we’re mountain biking with a balance bike. We will graduate him up to a bigger bike with brakes when it’s time.

The assembly was simple. They offer lots of colors (anyone with a preschooler knows how important THAT is). And the resting spot for his feet on the frame is perfect. It’s easy to adjust height and he can easily pick it up by himself since it’s so light.

My only major issue is that I’ve found the connection on the handlebar to be too lose. It has twisted several times for no reason at all and that’s a problem when you’re trying to learn to ride a bike. I also was kind of annoyed that within 48 hours of riding, the “tread” had already worn considerably on the wheels. It IS a bit expensive for that to be happening.

But overall, it’s not cheap junk and it’s not overpriced craziness. It’s a nice mid level balance bike for going around our neighborhood, driveway and back patio. He loves it and I’m very pleased.

review_text:
A lot of functionality at a low price. I thought that this was a decent watch for the money. I have never thought it fair to ding a product because it does not match the standard of a similar item that costs 100's more. It has a lot of functionality and was easy to set up. I found a fitbit on sale, and am using it instead. The primary reason was that the Amazfit Band 5 Fitness Tracker would not stay on my wrist. The band locks with a small plastic pin that goes through the holes in the band. It does not take much pressure at all for the pin to pop out of the band. Whether it was something as simple as folding clothes or more rigorous exercise, I frequently looked down to see it hanging off of my wrist. Luckily I never lost it. The second reason I replaced it was that I did not find it attractive at all.

In short, it is a low price fitness tracker that does the job it says it does. It may not sync with other popular weight loss apps, but if you do not care about this, I would recommend it. Negatives are that the watch pops open easily, and I did not its appearance.

product_name: Pflueger President Spinning Reel, Fishing Reel, Right/Left Handle Position, Graphite Body and Rotor, Corrosion-Resistant, Aluminum Spool, Front Drag System
review_text:
One of the best moderate priced reels. I have been using Pflueger President reels (of various models and versions) for close to 20 years. They've all held up well for me, required very little to no maintenance (other than keeping them clean and not left outside continuously exposed to the weather). At their LIST PRICE they are a bargain for what you get - a reliable, reasonable weighted reel, that perform well and does so consistently.

Obviously, at their price, they are NOT the best spinning reel one can buy. My Shimano Stratic's and Shimano Vanfords are certainly superior reels - but also cost three times as much! Whether they perform three times better than the Pfluege President model - the answer is a resounding NO, not three times better or even two times better.

For somebody just getting into fishing but who wants a reliable, decent quality reel that is going to last and not disappoint, I can recommend these most highly.

My only complaint with the reels is that they used to come with a spare spool - which was great as it allowed one to have 2 spools with different line on each, for fast and easy change-outs. My recommendation to Pflueger is to market spare spools (or of course, better yet to include a spare one in the box).

Secondly, I would like to see Pflueger indicate on the reel the size reel that it is, in an easy to see and visible location. Since I have multiples of these reels in many different sizes, this would be very helpful. Especially for fishing trips when rods/reels are broken down for transport - it helps to avoid putting the wrong sized reel onto a rod - only to realize this after getting on the water. Because the reels themselves, physically are not too different in physical size (at least at the 3000 and below size levels), this would be very helpful and appreciated (I am assuming by others as well).

But to end this, YES, I highly recommend these reels. They punch way above their LIST price point. If you find them on sale, by them in multiples!

review_text: Great design with a few flaws. I really like the design of this chair. It's low-slung and surprisingly comfortable with an aluminum frame and cotton seat so that you can set it close to a bonfire and not worry about sparks burning holes in your chair. But, there are a few downsides. First off, the pocket in the back is useless because the fabric stretches so tight when you sit in it that anything in that pocket gouges your back, including the extra foot supports that come in it (I just threw them in a drawer). Second, the cotton isn't treated, so you'll need waterproofing spray to avoid mold/mildew if it gets damp. Third, whoever put the "protective" plastic on the arms used the wrong kind... it's nearly impossible to take all the way off without damaging the aluminum underneath as you'll need a sharp implement to cut it. Finally, it's almost too low slung. I'm 5'10" tall and can lounge in it just fine but am unable to sit in any other position comfortably. If you're shorter it should be fine, but if you're any taller you'll likely find it disconcertingly low. So, if you're not too tall and looking for a chair specifically designed for lounging near a bonfire this is a very good choice. If you're looking for something more multifunctional that doesn't need much care I'd look for your chair elsewhere.

review_text: I absolutely LOVE this stove!. I have messed around with DIY rocket stoves with some success - my best was in using concrete blocks.  They work, but who wants to carry around 4 or 6 concrete blocks in their car?  It's not awful, but this rocket stove is lighter weight and works pretty much the same way.  One really good deal with this rocket stove is that it has the slide on grate pieces so that a pot/pan can be put on top to cook food, boil water for coffee or whatever.  It also gives off heat so when you are out camping, you can sit near it while cooking and not worry about the wind changing direction and open flames burning you as might happen with a regular fire.  Not just that, but with this rocket stove, you can gather small twigs that wouldn't keep a regular fire going and in a rocket stove, they burn well.  I think if I were to make any changes to this design, I'd change the legs.  I'm no engineer, but I think a folding mechanism could be used so the legs are permanently attached, but fold down so the rocket stove is as small as it is now (without the legs being removed and possibly lost).  The same with the slide on grate pieces.  Again, I am not an engineer so it may be that hinges that close to heat might be an issue, but if the grate pieces could be slightly curved so they rest against the stove pipe section, then the same would be accomplished with them as the legs. product_name: Kelty Tallboy Family Car Camping Tent, 4 or 6 Person Freestanding Shelter, Large Capacity, Stuff Sack Included. 2022
review_text:
Big tent.. I just got it today. I thought I had ordered the 4 man, but the bigger 6 man arrived. So I went into the side yard to give it a trial.
Stake the 4 corners. Then put poles together and slide them through the corner sleeves. This is a bit of an issue. The sleeves are continuous, that means there's no space from one side to the other to grab and push the poles through (my previous tents had spaces between pole sleeve sections). The fabric sleeves tend to bunch up and not allow the pole to smoothly slide across. I managed to get them placed in a few minutes. Then step into the door and lift up the center. This gives you just enough height to get the poles on 4 corners to bite into the ground. Then go around all corners and place them into the corner grommets. For a hot summer day/night, this is all you need! There's big walls of see through mesh on 3 sides, allowing total ventilation. Hang your battery powered fan inside! There's still privacy material at the bottom all around for a couple of feet from the base. Kelty should have provided a flyless photo that showed how much air is possible. So. Now the rainfly. A bit trickier for one person. I used the wind to help me float the rain fly over the tall top of the tent. Match up the blue staking strips so you have it aimed right (make sure "Kelty" shows on the outside). Buckle them in, pulling all of the corners as loose as they will go.
Now to install the "ridge pole" pull up the fly opposite the door from outside the tent and seat the ridge pole into the sleeve under the fly, it's a tight fit. Run it up under the fly over the top of the tent towards the door. Now go around to the door and stand inside so you can use the cloth finger loop attached to the pole sleeve to pull the fly away from you till you can pull down on pole and out on fly to get the other end of the pole seated in there. Yes, I had to reread the instructions and they didn't even mention using the loops to help you pull. Without them I couldn't do it.
You can still increase the ventilation under the fly by using the ties on the outside of the fly all around. Pull out the cord and stake it out from the tent. If you need the fly, it will probably be cool anyway.
This tent would for sure be easier set up with 2 people, but on my first try I did it alone, though I learned a couple of lessons that will make it more straight forward next time. You totally need to practice the set up at home first.
In the photo of the rain fly, I don't have the fly pulled out and staked. You would WANT to do this IRL! When I camped in SE Colorado a few weeks ago, my son's tent had those guy strings to hold out the sides of the rain fly. I tripped over them EVERY time I walked by, couldn't get it through my head to avoid them.
This is a nice big tent once set up, and just takes a bit of practice and caution till you have it down pat.

product_name: Mizuno MVP Baseball Batting Gloves
review_text:
Not good compared to alternatives. Background: I am working with my 10-year old to develop him as a batter. Our goal is at least 120 hits every day. At this point in his progression, batting gloves have become an indispensable tool to mitigate blistering and hand fatigue. So far we have tried extensively 3 different youth batting gloves. These are the classic Franklins, and also Marucci and Mizuno MVP. The Franklin batting gloves are by far superior. Below are the reasons why, with pictures. In the pictures, I have used the Mizuno MVP and regular Franklins.

1. All 3 models are difficult to attach the Velcro strap single-handedly. This is especially a problem on the Mizuno MVP. The reason is that the Velcro strap is made too short. The Velcro strap on the Franklins is by far the longest and easiest to use by the batter when putting on the glove on his own.

2. The Mizuno MVP wrist opening is hideously tight. But not as bad as the Marucci one. I do not know which designer in China came up with that look/design. In combination with a shorter Velcro strap, the Franklin is much, much better in terms of convenience to put on snugly.

3. Stitching: The main problem on the Mizuno MVP is the interior stitching. As you can see in the pictures, the Franklin has exterior stitches on the fingers area. This makes the inside of the fingertips as smooth as can be. The Mizuno MVP has interior stitches. It doesn’t get noticed on hit 1 or 10, but by the time he hits 20-30 balls, the kid starts complaining of discomfort at the fingertips, especially at the index finger on the driving hand.

4. Venting and moisture wicking: The Frankins have these tiny punctures along the finger length. At first they seem unnecessary to the design, but they actually help vent the glove a lot better. The Mizuno MVP gets completely wet on the inside after a 200-ball batting session. The Franklins also get damp, but roughly only half as much.

5. One thing I like better about the Mizuno is the black cloth material, which hides dirt and mold a lot better than the Franklins, which are solid white. The Mizuno also looks nicer overall, but the functionality is poor compared to the Franklins. The Mizuno MVP, if you look at the fingertips, each fingertip is designed differently with different materials, angles and stitching. It makes no sense at all. Mizuno totally went for looks over function.

6. The Marucci youth gloves are a total disappointment for us. That’s why I don’t even comment on them. I would not necessarily call them junk, but we are one-and-done as far as the Marucci glove brand is concerned. I guess, Marucci should stick to making good bats instead of branding third-party designed apparel.

product_name: Byway Tire
review_text:
Wow! Confidence inspiring stability on mixed surfaces.. UPDATE: Just about every time I go out I get a flat what's the tiniest object like a small piece of metal or a very small thorn. I'll have to get some kind of thorn protection liner. The other thing is that they wear very fast. I switch them out for a while for winter tires I just recently put them back on and I've noticed that they were nearly worn out on the main tread surface.

These tires really improved my riding experience. Paved riding is fast but provides confidence inspiring stability on mixed surfaces.

Since the mid-1990’s I rode my Bianchi Axis cyclocross bike as what we're calling today a ‘Gravel Bike’: rough paved commuting, moderate mixed surface exploring (not racing). The bike is stable and my Continental touring style tires were just fine.

Recently I built a new Surly Straggler that has quicker steering, coinciding with different local that frequently transition from paved to loose granular hard packed surface. My first ride out was really unstable and scared the crap out of me. I searched high and low looking at virtually every brand from Continental, Vittoria, Schwalbe, etc. These other brands had some good choices, but availability of a tire suitable for paved surfaces was a major issue, so I finally settled on these Byway tires.

I think they are a perfect mix of fast riding center tread strip with the small side knobs that really help with granular hard pack surfaces. They stop that tendency to slip sideways in a turn or transitioning from paved to hard pack. I had no problem going over the low concrete curbs separating paved from hard pack surface. I purchased 700cx40 so I was able to run the pressure a little low which seems to have little impact on my speed but made a difference in riding comfort.

review_text: Manufacturer claims this contains cat's claw: UNTRUE!!. Believing the manufacturer's claim that the product contains a species of Cat's Claw (they state on this site it is the species Uncaria rhynchophylla, Gou Teng), I purchased this only to discover that the fine print on the label states that it contains "cat's claw" from the source ranunculus ternatus, also known as catclaw (not cat's claw) buttercup. It is a 12" wild buttercup that grows in China and has no use in Lyme disease or other tick-born illness. The Cat's Claw used in Lyme disease (either Uncaria tomentosa or Uncaria rhynchophylla) is a 100 ft. woody vine that grows in the South American Jungle. I called Samsara twice leaving a message describing my concerns and asked for a call back to discuss this before writing a review. review_text:
Durable, Better Design. Hoverboard buggies are FUN! Like VERY, VERY FUN! Every child and adult has had a blast on ours! They take a few minutes to figure out how to shift weight to start, stop and turn, but then it’s easy muscle memory. (There aren’t brakes on buggies; you shift your weight back to stop.)

This one in particular, was the second buggy we purchased for my son’s hoverboard. The first one fell apart in one day. It was a similar design but the Velcro straps weren’t tough enough and the design of many others has the straps dangling down, and thus ripping and getting caught throughout use. This one does NOT do that! The engineering behind the straps was thought out and they stay close fitting. The company also threw in 4 extra straps which was a welcomed surprise. We won’t need them most likely. But if something WERE to go wrong it would probably be with the straps and now we wouldn’t have to return or exchange the whole buggy.

The only caution I would say is that the seat is a little snugger than some others and therefore Moms and Dads may not fit comfortably to sneak in a ride here and there!

Overall, really great product!!

product_name: niupipo Pickleball Paddles, USA Pickleball Approved Pickleball Paddles Set of 2, Carbon Fiber Face, Polypropylene Honeycomb Core, Pickleball Rackets with 1 Pickleball Bag/2 Covers
review_text:
Great Paddle For Beginners. I've extensively reviewed around 15 paddles from various manufacturers over the last year. I was never a fan of Chinese-made paddles because they seem cheaply made and clearly inferior to the USA-made paddles from companies like Paddletek, Selkirk, and ProLite. The Explorer Pro paddle comes somewhat close to the superior quality of the lower-end American paddles.

The Explorer Pro is slightly softer and has more control than the Niupipo Explorer which is important because the regular Fiberglass Explorer paddle was too hard and unforgiving for most situations. The Graphite face of this Pro model improves the control, but not enough. There are many shots that bounce off erratically because the Explorer Pro is simply too rigid. The manufacturer claims the Explorer Pro is "Carbon Fiber," but that's misleading since this paddle DOES NOT have a carbon fiber weave face. Graphite is often referred to erroneously as carbon fiber, and paddle-makers use the term knowing most people are ignorant of the differences.

Beginner players tend to use harder paddles because they rely on driving the ball and want a paddle to do most of the work. Higher skilled players focus on control and placement, waiting for the right opportunity before attacking with velocity. The rigidity of the Explorer Pro makes it better for the beginner/intermediate player who wants a hard-hitting paddle.

The handle length is a bit shorter than some paddles and may not work for those who use a two-handed backhand but is ample for most players.

Overall, the price is the selling point for this paddle. If you want a decent paddle for under $70, this is the one. If the price goes above $70 or are a more advanced player, I would take a look at some American branded paddles. Of course, at the 4.0 level and higher, you probably already have a higher-priced performance paddle because spending an extra few dollars is no big deal for advanced athletes.

I'm hoping for an Explorer version with a true Carbon Fiber Weave face which will further increase the forgiveness and accuracy albeit with a higher price tag. I see many manufacturers adding a carbon fiber option, but it requires deep pockets for the luxury. Or even better, Niupipo should make the polypropylene core more forgiving and add multiple layers of graphite to increase the touch like other manufacturers while keeping the price low.

Lastly, this is not even close to my favorite paddle. There is a rather obscure paddle I was lucky enough to review early in 2021 called the "Baddle Pro Circuit" which retails for almost double the price but, surprisingly, dominates every paddle in performance. I'm keeping the Explorer Pro as a backup but a mediocre paddle with a graphite face isn't anything special.

A true Carbon Fiber Weave face would be a gamechanger, so wait on that model.

product_name: Oticon ConnectLine TV 3.0 for Oticon Opn
review_text:
Crisp sound directly from electronic devices. A streamer that shoots sound (music, movies, computer) wirelessly into your hearing aids gives much clearer sound. For a while I bulked at the high price of the Oticon ConnectLine TV 3.0 for Oticon Opn. But I jumped for it when it went on sale (from Hearing_Aid_Accessories in the UK), and I'm glad that I did. The sound is awesome.

You pair your hearing aids once to the streamer. Pairing adds a new mode; so now I have NORMAL, CLASSROOM, and STREAMER; hold down the right HA button for three seconds to move to the next mode. Five minutes with no sound moves you from STREAMER to back NORMAL mode, presumably to save battery power; sometimes this is convenient and sometimes not -- but it takes only a few seconds to bring STREAMER mode back. The connection is very stable; if the sound starts breaking up, change the batteries -- they are almost dying anyway. You can move a pretty good distance and still keep the connection; this is good for doing exercise videos or for jumping on a trampoline during football games.

The photo shows my setup. My external speakers are on the bottom; the top has a 4-output amplifier on the left and the Oticon streamer on the right, both secured to the top by velcro strips. The wired amplifier input goes into the back of my TCL TV and gives whatever sound goes with the main screen (computer, TV, Roku streaming, whaever). Amplifier output 1 goes into the speakers underneath, 2 and 3 go into pillow speakers (these give quite good sound when your head with HAs rest on the speaker -- this is a a cheaper alternative but limits mobility), and 4 goes to the Oticon streamer (with the amplifier at max -- click the hearing aids to regulate volume). While I can adjust the sound of all four independently, I use the streamer most of the time.

If you want the sound louder, max the volume on your hearing aids and lower the audio going into the streamer. If you overload the streamer, the audio quality suffers.

For additional HA and streamer features, get the free OTICON ON app for your android or apple phone.

If you're on the fence, buy this device -- the sound is amazingly good.

product_name: H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board 10'6''/10' × 30" × 6" with Premium SUP Paddle Board Accessories & Backpack, Ultra-Light, Wide Stable Design, Non-Slip Deck for Youth & Adults
review_text:
So far seems like this is going to be a great SUP. My wife and I have wanted to get on the water with SUPs or kayaks since trying them on a tour a few years ago, however, unable to have any storage at home, we have been unable to. Then we saw inflatable SUPs and thought we’d be able to give that a try. I had the opportunity to get this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board and I jumped! Of course, we live in a hot weather state with summer rainy (storm) season and I’ve had major surgery this year with a longer recovery, so unfortunately we have not yet been able to get onto the water. But as the weather calms and I’ve been cleared... we’ll be out there sooner than later. In the mean time, we finally had a chance to blow up this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board and so far so good - we are sure this is going to turn out to be a great thing for us! This H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board comes with several items to get you going (able cuff, repair kit, pump), but do not forget, you’ll want to have some sort of safety vest (required by law in our state - NOT INCLUDED in this kit).

The pump to get it inflated is included and for us, worked pretty well. We took turns to pump it up and while it took some time (and strength we’re both currently lacking post surgery and injury) we were still able to get it “almost fully inflated.” I say “almost” because the company recommended 15 PSI and we only got to 10. That 15 is for “optimal use” and no higher. We felt like the 10 would be good, but when we are out there (and I have more energy back) we will go a bit higher than the 10 As you can see in the pics, it is very inflated and looks good, my wife able too and on it and feel firm and secure. Standing on it she said it felt like (on water) it’ll have good, solid balance and allow a feeling of security on the water. This SUP looks and feels “narrow and long” to us based on our experiences on tours, but something we both would feel comfortable on. We will update this review once we can get out there. In the mean time, we are really happy with this SUP and how easily it went together. Or blown into shape. The removal of air was easy and took only a couple minutes. I’ll say, when she first opened the valve there was a LOUD HIGH PITCHED!!! sound that hurt both our ears, but it went away pretty quickly. Then completed the air removal. My wife did point out the ONE CON is this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board has a VERY pointy and painful value piece you push on - it was not at all comfortable and hurt her finger enough she grabbed a piece of the wrapping it came in to cushion her finger.

We have not used nor opened the paddle that came with. We felt like its weight in the bag was alright, but had a chance to get another that was lighter. We will try both. But we also feel like having two paddles is safest - one with in case something happens to the second.

There are hooks on the deck where you can attach a kayak seat for sitting down - something I prefer. I have weaker ankles from years of sports, so I can tire easily on SUPs. I’ll look forward to this addition - NOT INCLUDED in this kit, but available from H2O as an add-on.

Overall this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board is a great board and we are even more excited to get to our coast and use it. In the mean time, we are very happy with how easy this SUP gets set up and takes down and feel like it’s sturdy and well made enough it’ll be great for a good long time.

I caught a couple of smallmouth bass as well. I found the trick in the morning was to cast out where the fish were surfacing and chasing minnows, and would instantly get hit hard.
Some of the cons are that when casting the hooks can catch on the body segments and make the retrieval awkward. You also have to retrieve it quite quickly in order to get the lure to swim naturally, which is fine during warm water fishing and fall fishing when fish are active and feeding. During the spring and cooler temps when fish are less aggressive this lure would not be ideal.

They truly sink slowly which makes it great for weedy areas and shallow water.

Bought During the Great 2020 Panic. I bought this bar during the great gym equipment panic of 2020. First one I paid a lot of money for and ordered it took 2 months to come back in stock to ship, and then never even made it to my address and wound up somewhere else in my town. That's not the bar's fault, and the seller refunded my money despite my extremely high suspicion it was the Post Office's screw up.

Next order found it arriving here via UPS, with the truck backing out of the driveway as I was entering, which blocked him in. He drove right back up to the house and pulled the bar right out of the back of the truck, saying he couldn't find it and was going to give up, but thought he'd give it another look.

He was going to steal it.

These bars were worth their weight in GOLD at the time, and though I haven't used it much I have enough experience with them that I know I'll probably keep it for the rest of my life because it's extremely high quality and does what it is supposed to.

I'm working out at a gym again now that everything is back to normal of course, but I'll always keep this bar even if it sits in the closet. I went through too much to get it.

review_text:
Great product value for the price. For around thirty dollars this is hard to beat. It's not the most attractive band or watch but it's not bad looking. I've had it for ten days or so now and it's still over 30% from the initial charge. I compared the heart monitor to my phone's built in monitor and they seemed consistent with each other so it appears accurate to me. My main reason for getting it was to track my heart rate as I'm running. For that it works great. There are a few nice extras like the Alexa built in mic and for work a nice periodic reminder to get up and move around and sleep monitoring that seems to work well also. The face is configurable but default options are a bit limited.

As for the app I rate it a little lower for a few reasons. First I'd like to see some option for either a dedicated app or a way to set the Wyze app to default right into the band portion of the app. It just seems cheap to have to navigate through a home automation app to find my health monitor band around a bunch of lightbulbs etc. In addition the heart rate monitor is on a timed checking system. It works great but that data and the heart rate data from your workouts are kept completely separate. That might be a good thing but a combined view might be nice. For example during my workout I peaked around 160 but the daily monitor showed my max heartrate at 109 for the day. I had to view the workout directly to see the higher numbers. Lastly, I'd like to see the app integrate with GPS so when I start a workout it maps my path and distance until I stop the workout. Address some of those features and it's a 5 star for me.

Update: Found one more small issue. It should not record time on my desk charging as me sleeping...but it does.

review_text:
Fundamentally flawed design. I really want to like this cycling computer. It's not too awful to set up. The display is very easy to read. Battery life is good.

It is operated with one button. You activate it by pushing down on the bottom edge of the bezel. The button is actually on the back of the unit; the whole unit pivots slightly in the mount and a nub on the mount pushes the button on the back.

That is the flaw. Normal-sized bumps jostle it enough to push the button. I'm not jumping curbs -- these are ordinary imperfections on paved streets and trails. I look down at it and it has switched to some random mode. This happens at least a dozen times on a 90-minute ride.

With my first Padrone, after two years and nine months (nine months past the end of the warranty), the random mode switches were happening pretty much continuously. Then the unit almost completely stopped responding to my *intentionally* pushing down on it. Then it reset spontaneously and lost my odometer reading.

So what did I do? I bought another one, because I like it. And it is randomly switching modes again. I must hate myself.

Decent, lightweight landing net.. I took a long break from fly fishing while my kids were growing up.
When I decided to get back into the sport I took a long look at my 20+ year old gear and evaluated what needed to be replaced.
My old, wooden landing net was one of the casualties of years of disuse.
The nylon netting had all but disintegrated and fell apart with only minor effort.
I as looking for a lightweight, compact replacement that I could easily attach to my vest and wouldn't get in the way.
I stumbled upon this one and decided to order it.
It only weighs about 7oz, folds in on itself for handy transport and storage, and seems fairly robust.
My only complaint is that the netting isn't rubberized, so occasionally a fly will get caught in the threads...when that happens though its pretty easy to remove.
The elastic shock cord lanyard attaches to the loop on the back of my vest, keeping it out of the way, yet easy to access when I need it.
Overall, I'm quite pleased with this net.
The price is excellent for what you get.
Highly recommended.

review_text: READ BEFORE BUYING!. GoTrax ships a pretty decent product - well built and seemingly rugged.  But be warned, if ANYTHING happens beyond their absurdly short warranty period, the scooter you paid money for is junk.  We bought a fleet of GoTrax scooters for our family for Christmas.  10 months later, after quite normal and infrequent use, one of the most expensive of the GoTrax scooters began having trouble, requiring a new controller.  Obviously out of warranty, I'm willing to pay for the controller (they're $15 on ali, but has GoTrax specific connectors), but told unless they're on the parts section of their website (which is a joke), I can't buy them.  Also told to take it to a local bike shop, who obviously have zero interest in anything remotely close to this stuff.  So, $500 out the window, it's junk.  Do your research, find a scooter that has parts available.  A controller is a very vital part of a scooter or bike.  Batteries only last so long, but should also be available.  Otherwise, accept that you may have an expensive piece of junk after a very, very short warranty period...  For what it's worth, they sell a very expensive "extended warranty" when you buy from manufacturers website.  Forums are saying getting a replacement is very difficult, and after paying to ship a heavy scooter to them, claims are being denied, saying damage is due to misuse...  Best of luck...

product_name: Grounding Half Sheet 10% Silver with Grounding Cord, Grounding Sheet Native Cotton for Better Sleep Healthy (36 x 91 Inch)
review_text:
Buy a larger size to wrap yourself up in - makes a huge difference for chronic pain!. I previously had a similar sheet to this but as it's not a fitted sheet it didn't really work to use as a sheet as such. This time around I decided to get a much larger sheet and use it as a top sheet that I could basically wrap around my body under the blanket before I go to sleep. This means that even more of your body is making contact with the fabric. I wasn't sure if it would make a difference but since I'm a big fan of grounding pads I wanted to give it a try. Right now I have a grounded pillow case but I just couldn't get a long term grounded sheet or pad solution working for the rest of my bed because it would be kicked off or crumpled up.

I can say for those of you who do respond to grounding pads for pain/inflammation that it makes a HUGE difference to wrap yourself up in it. It's harder for me to notice now that I've been using it consistently but when I first got it I kind of felt drugged! Back when I had tried the smaller sheet that was bunching up my husband didn't know what this was supposed to do and spent many days passed out in our bed trying to attribute the calming effect to something else! So grounding is very real. There are tons of studies on it and if you suffer from chronic pain give it a try right away. Especially if you've had relief with pillows, pads, the difference between that and a full sheet or in my case wrapping myself up is pretty big!

Another cool thing about this is that it's 10% silver threads which should in theory give an antibiotic effect so your sheets are fresher longer. The sheet is even softer than my super expensive silver thread (but non grounding) sheet set I got and is not thin or flimsy. I have autism and I'm really picky about sheets and this one is totally fine.

product_name: Bowflex Max Trainer Series
review_text:
Great for nine months of 6 days a week use.. tldr; I would say that you could likely get something else at a fraction of the cost and use the rest of your money for some free weights. Heck, you could probably get a gym membership and a personal trainer for at least a few month to get your desired results with less headache.

This is the first piece of equipment that I have owned that is also mechanical and solely for exercise. The Max Trainer m6 was purchased after some research. I thought that, 'Yes, it's expensive, but you get what you pay for. Right?' Well, not me. The machine was purchased online in August of 2020 from Bowflex and it took 2.5 months for me to get it, which with 'rona going on I wasn't surprised by the delay.

When I received the machine the setup was pretty easy. It took about an hour and a half with my own basic tools (screw driver, ratchet, box wrench, hex or Allen wrench), and then I was using it. There was a squeak that developed after a week, but I used some WD-40 on all the joints and never heard it again.

Sorry but this kinda gets gross. When I use the machine in the summer I sweat a lot, and the two bars where the magnetic tray attaches for the tablet can also be used as hand holds. In the JRNY app, I did a guided workout where the trainer said to use the bars to really push through certain parts of the workout. That said, I know the bars are not just for the tablet tray. So, where the bars go into the main console the holes are not sealed, with the result of my console collecting sweat while I worked out. It eventually fried my console and I had to have another one sent out, which took a month. The only reason I found out that that was the issue is because when I took the console off to switch it, the sweat drained out. YUCK. After I switched the console out for free, the new console stopped adjusting the tension correctly. I was working out with the machine when it rapidly went from level 5 to 16, then back again without my input. After that it would sometimes work and then on other days it would keep the tension very high, so that level 1 to level 14 didn't have a difference.

Today I got pissed and took it apart mid-workout, tired of the constant interruptions to my workout schedule. I seemed to have fixed the issue by adjusting the tension cable that goes from the torque arm to the magnets, but something else will likely just break again soon. My thoughts are that the m6 is poorly designed and manufactured. In other words, a piece of junk. You are buying a name. It's really just that piece of equipment that well-to-do, skinny-fat people have in their dwelling to make it look like they give a damn about themselves. As for us fat bodies trying to make a difference, we should look elsewhere. In my opinion, this machine should cost $500-$600, and that's being generous.

JRNY App
The JRNY was OK to use, but the guided voice is very bad. If anyone has played Fallout: New Vegas, imagine hearing Yes Man, or any other annoying voice you can think of every time you exercise. Those hard workouts just got harder, but maybe Bowflex is working you out psychologically as well. The video workouts can be substituted with your preferred video platform and the trail running videos seemed a little gimmicky. Maybe if I had a screen the size of a wall it would kinda feel like I am running somewhere in Utah, but on your tablet or smartphone it just doesn't cut it. I had to sign-up for the service when I purchased it online, because the box to uncheck the JRNY service was greyed out. They did give me some free usage, but you will likely just have to call up customer service to cancel it. Some of the music was good, which is about the only good thing I can think of for the whole experience.

I will be going to the gym for now on. Bowflex, thanks for the education.

review_text:
Small, cools for short time, but easy access on top. We’ve been using this cooler for the past three months at my daughters travel soccer tournaments. Three sandwiches, three drinks, and three snacks, and maybe some extras fit well in this cooler and leave enough room for either either or freezer packs.

We typically pack our lunches and hit the road for the journey to the fields. I’ll start with the nice things first about this cooler. First, the magnetic access hole on top of the cooler is a great feature to grab drinks out of the cooler for those times when it is wedged in between things in the back of the car. Simply pull up the tab, reach your hand in and grab what you need. This ensures that you don’t have to unzip the top, or in other coolers, push the button on the side to slide the top down. Another great feature is the built in bottle opener on the side. The strap clip includes a slot where you can use it as a bottle opener….perfect for those adults beverages that aren’t twist off!

While it is an Under Amour brand and it’s got some nice features, I have to tell you the number one thing I’m looking for in a cooler is the ability to keep my food and drinks cold. This is where this cooler suffers. We started using ice to keep the drinks cold, but quickly found out that the ice would melt into cold water in less than 7 hours. We then switched to the cold packs to avoid the liquid in the cooler, but found that they got wam quicker than our other coolers as well.

Unfortunately, I think some of this has to do with the access port on the top (the one I raved about). It is a THIN insulation on the lid which I’m assuming will let a lot of the cold escape. The side walls also aren’t much to write home about so don’t expect this thing to keep your stuff cold overnight or all day.

It’s a fun little big for drinks, but if you’re looking for a container to keep your food and drinks cold for a long time, this isn’t it.

review_text:
Good rower for the money. I've used a Concept 2 rower for the past 15-20 years at the gym, which I found to be an awesome machine. However, when it came to a home machine, I didn't want to spend that much money so looked for something similar. I chose an air machine as the sound it makes gives good feedback to the amount of effort you are putting into the workout. From reviews of magnetic machines, it sounds like they are quiet which would have seen odd based on my experience.
One of the attributes I used to compare rowers with was the weight. I figured a heavier machine would be built more solidly and I wasn't wrong in my strategy. This doesn't look like it will fall apart anytime soon.
I read some reviews that it doesn't give a good workout. As another reviewer pointed out, it is apparently user error. I don't pull that fast but do pull hard. Even in the easiest setting, I am huffing in now time flat.
The only ding I can give the machine is that one of the feet did not screw in. On close examination, it could be seen that the threads were malformed. Customer support was super responsive and I am getting a new one, albeit with a delay as it had to be back-ordered. A piece of wood suffices for now so at least I can use it. This wasn't enough of an issue to deduct stars and I am very satisfied with my purchase.

product_name: Kinderkraft Baby Balance Bike SPACE, toddler balance bike, bike without pedals, 11 inches toddler 2 Wheels bike, with Adjustable Seat, bicycle no pedals toddlers, balance bike 2 3 Year Old Kids Toddlers
review_text:
Big for 2.5 years old and way short for 5 years old. So I have a 2.5 year old niece who wants to ride the bike of her just-turned 5 years old sister. I thought this balance bike would be great for them, especially as the older child is still so nervous about balancing her bike on her own. The younger niece was so excited, but even at the lowest setting, it seemed to be difficult for her to "walk" to bike with both feet while sitting on the seat. She's almost walking on tip-toe. She's big for her age. She also didn't seem to like the hard seat and found it uncomfortable. It'll probably fit her better at age 3. The older niece wanted a try, so we put the seat at the max height line. She's about average height for her age, but she was too large to use it to learn to balance on 2 wheels. It was awkward for her to walk it and will be difficult to coast it even if she lifts her legs outward (as she can't use the built in foot rest). So we're a little disappointed. (UPDATE: Actually, the older girl can coast on it and has gotten quite good at balancing, but it's still awkward for her and she complains that the seat is uncomfortable. The pictures show the 5 year-old.)

The assembly instructions were a couple of crowded diagrams with the brief text instructions on a different page. The text added nothing to the diagrams. I was getting ready to put the bike together before the nieces arrived to visit when my dad (grandpa) saw what I was doing and took over. He promptly proved that you can't just guess about how it should go together and then, yes, you really do need to align the pieces the way shown in the diagram. However, once he started following the diagram, we did hit snag with the handlebar section. The front wheel comes up through the shaft and the handlebars go down in the shaft, then you tighten a band over both to hold things in place. It wasn't until the plastic spacer on the wheel section was removed that enough of the bottom pipe was exposed for this band to effectively tighten over and hold everything in place and aligned. It looks sturdy now that it's together.

review_text:
Helps Make Yoga More Comfortable. Those who like to do yoga will agree that it is best when performed on a mat made for this purpose. Mats are not all the same- some are certainly better than others and more suited to the task at hand. A good choice for yoga practitioners is this Yoga Mat from the YR Store.

Unroll this mat from the package and you will notice that it is approximately 6 feet by 2 feet in size. The bottom is designed to grip the floor, so you don’t need to worry about sliding around. The top isn’t flat and smooth- it has indentions, that are like tiny grips and are deigned to make yoga more comfortable.

I spent 2 hours on my treadmill and it counted 300 steps...
Samsung Health and Google Fit tracked about 5k steps from the phone in my pocket, which sounds much more accurate.
I will caveat this, though. This was on my treadmill desk while I was working. My hands weren't always swinging at my side.

I mainly wanted to use this for step and sleep tracking, and the step tracking seems to be a bust. I'm still on the fence about just returning it for something that does sleep tracking better.

review_text:
Way better quality than other brands.. First and foremost these are way better quality than the other woobies sold on Amazon. I had a couple of the made in China Multicam ones that included stuff sacks and they weren’t even in the same ballpark. I HIGHLY advise you to skip those and go with McGuire. If they don’t have the color you want on Amazon then order directly through McGuire or another vendor that stocks their stuff like venture surplus or thunderhead outfitters. (I had to buy my Multicam one elsewhere because it wasn’t in stock here)

Ok, now onto the product itself. Several people are saying these aren’t as soft as the issued ones. That’s because they are brand new and must be washed a few times. When you get them they will be a little stiff. Just like a pair of jeans gets softer after a few months of wearing and washing these woobies do as well. My advice is to wash it 2-3 times as soon as you get it. Dry it on low heat and it should come out softer. Use it for a month or so and it will be ALOT softer. For whatever reason, my Multicam one came in super soft straight from the factory. The black one requited washing and some use to get soft. As for sizing, I’m around 5ft 11in and I can tuck it under my feet and still pull it over my head completely enclosing myself in the blanket as is needed when it gets really cold.

Also, you may want to tie all the strings up into bows like a shoe lace or something because if not you run the risk of them getting caught in the washer or dryer and ripping either themselves or the blanket. You can also elect to do what I did and use a seam ripper to remove the strings and sew paracord loops in their place like the Kifaru Woobie has. I ended up with 14 loops total, 1 in each corner, 2 on the top, 2 on the bottom, and 3 on each side. I used a different color paracord for the 2 loops at the top of the blanket because I wanted to easily be able to identify it. This is because I don’t want my face to be where my boots or feet have been. I made the part with the tag the bottom because I didn’t want it rubbing my face either.

I did save 1 of the included strings and looped it through one of my sewed on loops on the bottom corner near the tag. This allows me to gather the bottom of the blanket up and tie the string around it forming a makeshift foot box. (See pics for details)

All in all for $40 I think this is a solid product. It’s not nearly as warm as a Kifaru but it also packs down to about 1/3 the size and cost about 1/5 of the price. I also find it softer and better feeling against my skin than any other Woobie I have tried to date.

Again I state, skip the other brands and buy the USA made McGuire. Been there, done that. Nothing else comes close to the quality of these except the Kifaru but it’s a different product altogether. A lot thicker, bulkier, and not even close to the same price.

I especially like the orange and black color scheme of this daypack because it is attractive and easily recognizable. If you've ever had to stow your gear with other travelers, you'd appreciate having a brightly colored bag like this each time you went to retrieve it. If you prefer a more subdued color, this bag also comes in blue and black options. The main compartment of this daypack is also roomy and comes with a laptop pocket with decent padding at the back. The only things I would change about this bag would be by adding some more padded reinforcement at the bottom, and include a rain cover that would protect the open top compartment above the brand logo. All the same, I can still get a great deal of use out of this bag as a lightweight daypack or overnight bag.

product_name: Heated Glove Liners for Men Women, Rechargeable Electric Battery Heating Gloves Liners, Touchscreen Anti-Skip Heated Mitten Liners Hand Warmer for Skiing Hiking and Arthritis Hands by Dr.Warm
review_text:
Warm, yet thin enough to feel like they’re not even on. I’m a nature photographer who really enjoys shooting in winter (we get snowy owls!). I developed Reynauds syndrome, however, and my hands were so painfully cold even with gloves that I wasn’t able to shoot all last winter.

I have another pair of heated gloves that I bought last year for that purpose, but they were way to bulky and proved to be useless for photography.

These gloves actually do the job. They are liners that can also be worn as stand-alone gloves. Being liners, they are thin and fit snugly enough to move along with my fingers.

My camera has a touch screen, and the touch tips on these gloves actually work. They are sensitive enough to be completely usable on both my camera’s screen and that of my phone. In fact, they are sensitive enough for me to play games on my phone while wearing them.

The heat function works really well. The gloves heat up in seconds, and you can feel the heat through the entire length of the fingers as well as the back of the hands. The only part of my hands that still felt cold when I tested these were my palms.

I have two complaints that may be specific to me. I have very narrow wrists and hands with long fingers. I ordered these based on the sizing for the width of my hand. They fit fine that way, but the fingers are short on me, so they feel a bit like they are webbed. This constricts the movement of my fingers slightly. If you have long fingers, you might be better off going up a size.

My second complaint piggybacks on the first as the battery is very bulky and kind of cumbersome. That may not be an issue with someone with typical sized wrists, and it’s definitely not a dealbreaker even for my tiny wrists. The battery is one that is used on many other small heated items (think socks, scarves, hats, etc), so I really don’t know what if anything they could do differently to make it less bulky.

I also don’t believe these are waterproof or even water resistant based on the fabric. I have not tested them in this way yet however, so I may (hopefully) be wrong here.

Overall I’m pretty psyched to have these and finally be able to get back to doing some winter photography again.

I know there are a ton of heated gloves on the market right now, and these are not cheap, but I would recommend them. I vhope this review has been helpful to you.

review_text:
Bought to use with neti pot BUT read on. When quarantine first started, I began researching what I could do to stay healthy. I occasionally use a neti pot for allergies, and I came across a blog where a user used baby shampoo, neti salt packet, and this product in a neti pot and it knocked out his recurring sinus infections for good. So I decided to try that to see if it helped with allergies. I added a capsule to warm water, added 2 neti pot salt packets (salt and baking soda), and J&J baby shampoo and did nasal irrigation on each nostril. These capsules did not completely dissolve, so there were particulates visible in the water. It slightly burned when using but the worst of it was that I smelled garlic for probably A WEEK! I guess that's good if the premise works but since I didn't have an infection, just allergies, it wasn't alleviating anything but definitely was not enjoyable. Eventually it wore off, I kept using the neti with just the baby shampoo and salt.
In the past year, there have been various studies and several more ongoing trials, to test out baby shampoo and covid. Studies show that baby shampoo knocks out 99% of the covid germ in 2 minutes of neti pot use. Also, I told my Allergist dr that I did the garlic neti, she had never heard of anyone doing that but that doesn't mean a lot since she isn't a natural healing type doctor so I don't think she spends time on alternative remedies.
All that being said, I have continued to take these pills when I have a cold. I don't think they can hurt taking them orally and maybe they help. They taste strongly of garlic but I haven't noticed any garlic burps after taking. The price is not cheap but if I only take them when I'm sick, that's affordable.
I think the neti garlic is only for those with serious sinus infections, unless you start with only using maybe 1/8th of a capsule and work your way up.

product_name: OutdoorMaster Ski Goggles PRO - Frameless, Interchangeable Lens 100% UV400 Protection Snow Goggles for Men & Women
review_text:
Ok budget goggle (update: pretty good budget goggle). Unboxing: Well, to start off, there was no box at all. The Outdoor Master goggles shipped via Amazon in a plastic bag. Inside the bag were the drawstring pouches containing the goggle, and the extra lens that I also ordered. I currently wear a pair of Scott Unlimited II OTG goggles, with the blue pro-lens. It's available for about $80USD, so I think this review of the Outdoor Master Pro (OM Pro) is a fair comparison.

The OM Pro is a spherical lens goggle, and right off the bat I see that the frame (in orange) is more curved than my Scott, also a spherical lens. As well, the OM Pro double layer lens, is thicker than the Scott and less flexible. So when integrated to the magnetic frame the goggle feels heavier and more rigid than the Scott; and doesn't mold to your face as easily. To get around that problem, Outdoor Master uses a thicker layer of foam around the frame (but cheaper closed cell foam). There are 8 small magnets on the lens and frame, changing lenses gives a satisfying click and the connection feels secure. However there have been reviews saying the lens flys off in a real crash, so I reserve judgement until I get a chance to test them in the field.

As for OTG... well yes and no. On my Scott OTG I can comfortable take the on and off over my glasses, the OM Pro has a notch on the frame, but the thick foam gets in the way of my glasses. I have to change to a smaller pair of glasses, or like some have done, cut away the foam to make these truly OTG.

Now for a couple of gripes. First, the OM Pros are larger vertically, perhaps more suited for longer faces. Again, the size coupled with the thick foam presses down on my nose making it hard to breathe freely. You can rotate your helmet back a bit to move the goggles higher on your face, but you end up looking out the bottom half of the lens. So again like some reviews have said, cut away some of the foam. Second, there are NO vents whatsoever on the lens. Partially due to the magnet frame needing to be rigid, there is no place you can drill any holes or cut the lens without damaging the weather seal. This could potentially lead to fogging issues. You only have the top and bottom frame vents to clear moisture.

The lens has minimal distortion and not any more glare than my Scotts. The spare lens pouch is a nice idea, but could they have tried a bit harder to match the curvature of their lens?

For now, 4 stars as a budget minded goggle. I might revise this review once I get some ski days in with this pair of goggles.

**** UPDATE ****
After some on-the-hill testing, this is a pretty good alternative to the name brands in the sub $100 category.

The first day I tried these with the iridium blue lens in sunny conditions. I suddenly felt nauseous .. until I realized like I said earlier, the goggles forced me to look through the bottom half of my bi-focals. So if you wear glasses, this will really depend on your prescription and frame size. The second day I switched to a smaller frame and the goggles let me position it so I looked through the center of my glasses, and all was fine.

I ended up shaving some of the foam to fit better around my nose, and that gave me a more comfortable fit and worked better with my helmet combo. Also, cutting a slot in the foam where my glasses arms were helped with taking them off and on.

On the slope, it was sunny and dry, temps varied from the low teens to near freezing. I did not experience any serious fogging issues, only a little in the gondola with a face mask on. One day it was mixed snow and sun, I was able to swap lenses easily on the hill. I also crashed face first once, and the lens did not pop off. After shaking out some of the snow, it fogged up a bit, but cleared on the rest of the run down and did not fog up again.

In summary, I won't throw out my trusty Scotts (they fit my face better and more comfy for me) but these OM Pro goggles are a pretty good pair of budget goggles, especially if you consider the ability to swap out lenses.

review_text:
Good for occasional snowshoeing. I do a lot of snowshoeing and I have a pair of MSRs I won't part with. However I wanted some shoes for my kids who only like to go out occasionally. These are reasonably well made, and very lightweight, which makes them a good value for anyone starting out who doesn't expect to get too serious. I think these will be fine for snowshoeing that is mostly on trail and avoid any really steep terrain. I've seen pretty much the same shoes being sold under a couple of brand names, so I assume these are re-sellers for a Chinese brand.

I like the ratcheting front straps and the snap on the back strap. These are simple to use and reliable. One think that I hate about some high-end shoes are the needlessly fussy straps. Nobody wants to take their gloves off to fiddle with straps when it's freezing cold. I have tried it on some hard pack off trail and they did fine. I took it into some lighter snow and sunk enough to tell me these aren't for powder. However if you are hitting a well trod trail in a snow park these will do great. And I think the construction is good enough for years of occasional use. If you are going out a lot, hitting terrain and more varied snow, I'd look for a different set of shoes.

review_text:
Good for the money, not great. For a cheap hand exerciser these aren't bad. The weight is adjustable, the grip feels good in your hands and there is a counter to keep track of how many reps you've done.

The big downside is how you adjust the resistance. There's a label on the side that loosely lines up to the spring sticking out of the top of the thing. You tighten or loosen a screw to move the spring forwards and backwards to increase or decrease the resistance. It's easy enough to do, but it's not clear what weight/resistance you're set to. It's also almost impossible to get both grip things set to the same level of resistance. Since the screws are hand adjustable they're also easy to move on accident. I spent a good 2-3 minutes eyeballing and adjusting and getting both of these things set to the same level of resistance and then my 6 year old picked them up and moved them. In the process of picking them up and moving them the resistance changed and they weren't even anymore.

My solution to the resistance thing is to not let anyone mess with them, give them a quick eyeball before using and then just switch hands halfway through. So if I do 20 reps, then I'm going to switch grips/hands and do 20 more. I figure that'll even it out.

I wouldn't buy these again unless there was nothing else available, but they're not bad enough to return. So if you can't find any comparably priced options this is fine, just know it's not great.

review_text:
Small but powerful LEDS. Don't like the strobe, though.. The device comes with one battery. You unscrew the bottom of the device, put the battery in, and screw it back together. Then you unscrew the top and use the included USB charging cord to charge the battery whenever it's low. A red light next to the USB port indicates charging and green is charged. You screw on the top to use. The button is at one end and the lights at the other. The three LED therapy lights are very small, but they seem quite powerful. They shine brightly through my hand joints. My initial impressions are that this does help with my arthritis inflammation. The light should be used against bare skin and can be held directly against the skin. One of the lights is infrared (heat), so the head can get warm and you may need to let it cool (while off) before continuing to use it. It has 10 minutes before automatic turn-off, and the head only gets mildly warm by the end of that time . The therapy area (lighted area at the end) is 0.75" across, so the downsize is the limited area that you can treat at one time while the advantage is that it's battery-powered portable. The power button sequence is: one press = on, two = off, three = strobe light, four = off. I don't like how fast the strobe light pulses and so will never use it. You never have to see the strobe if you just hit once to turn on and once to turn off (and wait before turning it back on).

When placed on a hard surface, the little stand will hold the light pointed where you want it. I see no point to using the stand as distance decreases the penetrating power of the light hitting your skin.

review_text:
150 hours. This bag ring has been used for 150 hours to pick up litter, and it has carried out 900 pounds of litter from the streets, trails, and parks, so far.

I use 13-gallon kitchen trash bags with this bag holder. Any larger trash bag will drag on the ground and will slip out of the holder when it goes over the weight limit. This holder comfortably holds weights up to around 11ish pounds (a 13-gallon kitchen bag is meant to hold around 8 pounds of garbage) and then the bag will very slowly begin to slip out of the holder. At around 15ish pounds the bag will fully come out of the holder, but at that much weight in a 13-gallon bag the bag will be ripping and disintegrating anyways unless you double-bagged. If you use drawstring bags, you can loop the drawstring around the handle and that adds extra security. Double-bagging is also possible, which increases the structural integrity of your bags if you're anticipating extra weight.

I haven't seen any evidence of damage to the ring, even though the edge is often whacked with a metal grabber in attempts to dislodge sticky bits of litter. There are still no cracks or anything. I bought a second one just in case, but I've not needed it yet.

Highly recommended.

review_text:
Good idea, poorly executed..... About 2/3 of the rings would not tighten on either my Redding or RCBS dies. I quickly determined the reason was simply improper machining. The gap at the ends of the lock rings was too small. So, when tightening the Allen screw, the ends met before clamping on the die. I did get them to work by removing the screw, and using a grinder to widen the gap by about 0.030". They then tightened properly.

The other issue was the wrench. Upon seeing a stamped steel wrench, I was skeptical. As it turns out, with good reason. It contacts the die in only two places, and spins very easily, preventing you from tightening or loosening the lock ring. A very deep socket would be excellent, but a simple forged wrench would turn it into a 5 Star product.
