product_name: Arcturus Military Wool Blanket - 4.5 lbs, Warm, Thick, Washable, Large 64" x 88" - Great for Camping, Outdoors, Sporting Events, and Survival Kits
review_text:
needed some care before use. I love the smell of lanolin. I'm frustrated I can't find products that retain a good lanolin scent because all companies try to refine the smell out. A freshly cleaned and new bedding filled stable with clean animals meant a successful day and healthy animals so new, clean (not old odor build up) animal smells are not bad to me. I can understand the people who say it smells like a barnyard and why they may find it unappealing if they didn't grow up around animals but I never understood the people who say wool smells like chemicals.

Well after this blanket now I do.

My cheap ~$12 50% wool blankets I got for the dogs to use smell like clean lanolin. If only lightly due to how much polyester is in them. My 90% wool ektos brand blanket I have been using to keep warm in my drafty 1800s farmhouse smells wonderful. I wish the smell wasn't fading so I've already been looking at ways to spray it down with new lanolin and fabric refresher in place of washing options. Unfortunately ektos warns in their listing that even their 100% wool blankets are rough and suggest having a layer between you and the blanket. My one attempt to sleep with it resulted in waking up to the scratchiness where it had gotten under my comforter. So I went looking for something softer in about the same price range.

This blanket smelled horrid. Not at all like good lanolin. I hung it over the back of my chair until I could wash it but the smell was burning my nose and causing a rash where my bare arm rubbed against it. I stuck it in the washer with kookaburra wool wash on handwash/wool, light soil setting and a light extra rinse/spin hoping it would improve. I originally wondered if the detergent they use to clean the wool or the finished blankets was breaking the lanolin down. When lanolin is separated into it's individual parts some of the different resulting materials can smell like refined chemicals. Such as a few mechanical lubricants that are at least partially derived from lanolin to avoid using oil based products.

Unfortunately the blanket was much much worse when I opened the washer door. The closest thing I finally decided I could come up with, as I tried to hold my breath while carrying it upstairs, was rancid oil. With our society relying on all vegetable oils I've rarely smelled rancid animal fat or oils from it but after thinking about the few times I have that definitely matched the best.

I decided not to try rinsing it out and you don't air things outside in Iowa in winter. Aside from it being subzero there is barely any sun. I doubt sunlight and fresh air would have been enough anyway. Maybe if I left it outside for 3-4 days but UV light is damaging to all fabric. Short periods of airing out are good. Frequent or long periods can be harmful. Instead I took a spray bottle and added 1/4th cup kookaburra wash, 1 tablespoon of Soak brand biodegradable handwashing solution for delicate items (citrus scent), and an estimated 1/3rd cup of the least refined, thickest lanolin oil I've found so far. I filled the bottle the rest of the way with warm enough water to help dissolve the lanolin. Oil+ water problem... but the biodegradable detergents were partially included to help dissolve the oil better as well as cleaning and deodorizing.

I folded the blanket in quarters and hung it up with a fan, my spray bottle of custom mix, and a soft bristle fabric brush. I sprayed each side down thoroughly with frequent shaking of my spray bottle to keep it mixed and started brushing very lightly. It spread the mixture into the blanket and gently removed all the loosened wool from washing. Every time I flipped the blanket over or opened it up to refold I got hit by that horrible smell until I sprayed down and brushed out the next section. Many handfuls of wool lint with a line of it to the trash can despite gentle brushing and most of the bottle of mix later I could barely detect any of the remaining scent beneath normal lanolin and clean citrus. I hoped any remainder would go away when dry. I set the box fan on high, flipped the blanket over some hours later before bed, and it was dry and free of all bad odor by morning.

In the end it is overall good quality material and turned out quite soft for the cost and type of wool used, barely sheds and what's left could be solved with a little more brushing, and has a light pleasant scent now. Also I don't get itchy, reddish skin where it rubs against the blanket like started to happen before rinsing and brushing it clean. It just took some extra effort to get it to this point and I don't know enough about the process of making wool blankets to be entirely certain what seems to have ruined the original lanolin in the wool. Maybe it was some low grade or bad oil in the detergent used to initially wash it or the detergent itself.

Simply rinsing or airing it out for a day will work for normal lanolin if you dislike the sheepy smell overall but I doubt it would have ever improved whatever happened to this particular blanket. In my opinion if you get a blanket that definitely smells beyond what normal lanolin does I suggest washing with wool wash or biodegradable washes for delicates and then following directions you can find to "lanolize" wool with a good quality product. If you really dislike even normal lanolin scent the washes for delicates and maybe some biodegradable fabric refresher may not restore the waterproofing and dirt repellent properties as well as lanolin but should be suitable for cleaning and improving the smell of natural wool on their own. Many no rinse, hand washing solutions can be used in a washing machine as well.

A soft bristle fabric or other brush also works better to remove loose fabric or pet fur with potentially less damage than a washer or especially dryer for many materials. That's how I handle the cheap wool blankets the dogs use. Spray with a good pet deodorizer, brush them with the fabric brushes, sometimes vacuum it off if the fur is more than I want to spend time manually scraping away, and give it back to the dogs nearly the same as new. Brushing also usually softens both natural fibers and synthetics like polyester better than washing because it evenly separates the clumped up fibers. Just make sure to match the firmness of the brush to how easily damaged or pulled apart the fabric is. It needs to be firm enough to be effective but soft enough or used lightly enough to only remove or separate what's on the surface without pulling fibers out of the weave.

The Good: super lightweight and compact; the bad: everything else. I gave this a 1 star simply for the fact that it is a very compact, lightweight towel. But here's the reality, and I'll start with the good:

The Good: soft, lightweight, compact at a fraction of the size (when folded) of a regular beach towel, decent at absorbing water.

The Bad: Does NOT, I repeat, does NOT dry quickly despite what you will read in the description and in reviews. We took these towels to the beach. First of all, sand sticks to it and DOES NOT COME OFF AT ALL no matter how much you shake the towel off. Then you're left with a sandy towel to dry yourself with. Yes, it'll dry you, but it'll get sand on you in the process because, again, the sand sticks to the towel material and won't come off no matter how much you shake. When back at the hotel, we hung up the towel outside for THREE DAYS and it was still not completely dry by the end of the 3 days. I could have gotten over the fact that it does not dry quickly.

I'd pass on this, as it's not worth the small space in your suitcase.

review_text:
There are things I like and things I don't care for.. What I like is that the ease of the roller ball, and the hardness of it, allows you to roll right over your clothing... so if you do not feel like getting undressed (other than after a shower, or any other reason why you are not clothed), it seems like it is still effective even thru "average" wight clothing. I am sitting here with sweatpants and a thermal shirt on, and the rolling motion is still felt thru my garbs. The instructions on the box do not say anything about "skin," and just mentions "affected areas."

Now I will go the opposite direction with this... let's now assume I am now in only my birthday suit, and I want to rub in a lymphatic massage oil, or any other herbal oil or body butter... can I use this roller to roll over or to apply something to my skin that also helps my lymphatic fluids to move? The directions on the box that this ships in do not mention anything about using this product with oils or creams. THEN i did just look at the sales/info order page here on Amazon and it does mention using it with these products. I only checked here to double check it's usage. Good to know, but I with this was printed on the box or came as an inserted instruction. But, now I know and will proceed to try that!

The only other negative that I noticed, and this is probably just me, but I felt my soft tissue on my upper outer arm kind of hurt, like light bruising, after rolling this over that area a few times. That sore feeling did go away after a couple minutes. I got this becasue I have lymphedema swelling and liquid retention mostly in my left leg, becasue I had uterine cancer and 50+ lymph nodes removed 16 years ago. My arms are fine, but I do have fibromyalgia sensitivities, so that is probably why this would have felt like it hurt. (Kinda dumb observation on my part I admit, being that I am the one who controls the pressure! Not the fault to the product! But I guess it doen't take much pressure to use this ball, and that can be a good thing.) THis said, compared to other lymph massagers, like wooden U shaped sticks and wands, they tend to massage up a larger and flatter swath, involving more skin area with each stroke. This one is more like a rolling acupressure point. I an not tell which method moves the lymph better... I am going to guess this is personal preference.

review_text:
For $28, this is a useful and durable bargain. I own a lot of hammocks, and I own a lot of tarps. I bought this Redcamp 10x12 for $28 on sale. It is strong, durable, lightweight, and has multiple tie outs to make several tarp and tarp tent configurations.

Sometimes you can't string up a hammock and have to go to ground. This tarp, along with a trekking pole or long stick is plenty to stake out several one and two-man tarp tent configurations.

The stitching is excellent, and the grommets are on corner-sewn straps. Still, a little shock cord will make it last. The only issue is the stakes are serviceable, but not the best. And the guy lines are totally trash. You'll want to replace those ASAP.

I have lighter silnylon tarps, but they aren't as durable, nor do they have all the tie outs I need. I have thicker and heavier tarps (cheaper too), but they are just that; heavier and cheaper. Many of them are not ripstop and at the added expense of weight are not as durable.

This is a great deal.

product_name: ComforTrac Wave Cervical Traction Neck Support & Stretcher – Made in USA, Provides Ergonomically Correct Support for Relief of Pain, Headaches, Cervicalgia, TMJ & Spine Alignment
review_text:
Helps relieve back and neck pain. Over the past eight months, I’ve tried a few different neck traction pillows. I’ve found they are all quite similar and accomplish the same goal, with only slight variations in design. This one, like most others, is made of a hard foam with just the slightest bit of give when you rest your head on it. It’s possible to use the pillow in either direction, one way providing a more gentle stretch, the other, a more intense stretch. This pillow does not have the bumps and nodes that some others have which are supposed to provide some acupressure and massage to your neck, though I can’t say that they make much of a difference for me. This pillow does, however, have a softer cushion in the center that makes it a little more comfortable on the back of my head. It's a very nice feature.

If you’re new to this type of device, go slow. When I first used one of these pillows, I could only lie on it for a few minutes at a time, but have worked my way up to 10-15 minutes twice a day. I also recommend starting with the side that gives you the more gentle stretch. For me, using a device like this has provided quite a lot of relief to my neck and shoulders that tend to carry a lot of tension since I sit at a computer all day.

If you’re looking for an alternative to medication for some relief for back and neck pain, this is definitely worth a try.

THEY HOLD AIR!. EUREKA! Finally I found a pair of inner tubes that will hold air. I've been through 4 sets of inner tubes since January 2021, and not one set held thier PSI for a reasonable length of time. Whether riding regular or not, there is absolutely no VALID reason that I should have to air up my tires weekly, let alone daily. I put these on about 6 days ago when my current rear tube went flat.
I currently ride a Eurobike 'gravel bike', 27.5/2.1' tires, and at least their bike was well worth the money, it was a meager investment for what if offered, and I am so tired of getting my expensive bikes stolen. (5 in 25 years) Nowadays I maybe put in about 50 miles tops around town on a good week, arthritis in my knees and hips is taking its toll. And I was skeptical about the frustration I might have to go through again with yet another set of inferior quality inner tubes. There is no reason that I or anyone else out there should have to spend much more than about $10 - $15 on a set of reliable inner tubes. I am not riding in the Tour De France, not trail riding, heck I rarely even jump curbs anymore, and I should not have to check my air pressure daily, or wait until I am riding and can feel the drag from tubes that losing air pressure during a longer ride. My current Eurobike tubes, that I purchased separately from the bike, would loose about 2 - 3 psi a week in hot weather, and not much better in cold weather either. . . and that was the replacement set they had sent me. (the set the bike came with was atrocious, but my last 3 bikes including a $1200 dollar Trek had come with bad inner tubes)
These are awesome. 61 psi front and back 6 days ago, have ridden about a modest 30 or 40 miles since, and today - 61 psi front and back!
I have 1 back up tube I carry with in case of flats, and of course a CO2 fast filler, and I now have an entire used Amazon box full of backups.
I have a set of Conti tubes on the way here, they are supposedly seamless, however the valve stem is only 40mm and I really need a 48mm for my triangular rims on this bike. I ordered the Conti tubes the day after I installed these Mohegia tubes, when I checked the PSI it looked like they had lost about 2-3 pounds overnight, that was before the air pressure gauge blew apart when checking the pressure on the front tire. I will most likely send the Conti tubes back without opening, since these Mohegia tubes seem to be holding up very well.
BTW, and off topic here, I have 4 manual pressure gauges all by Slime liner and NOT ONE GIVES THE SAME PSI, up and down on all of them. I have 2 digital gauges, same thing. YOU HAVE TO BE KIDDING ME! HOW HARD IS IT TO MAKE A CONSISTENTLY ACCURATE AIR PRESSURE GUAGE?
And I have one guage that I bought at a dollartree type store, metal - not a plastic pressure tube, and it is the only one that is consistent, and I have NO difficulty getting a tight fit on the valve stem. (does me no good to check the air pressure when the tire losses a pound trying to get a tight seal with the guage in the process) , Some times we get more than what we pay for, and other times we don't get what we pay for, that is what return policies are for.
I highly recommend these, and I would buy again... and again. And a fair price too.

I ordered this product with hopes that regular use, along with chiropractic and physical therapy, could help restore some of the natural curve back to my cervical spine as well as reduce pain due to herniated discs, pinched nerves, and chronic muscle spasms.

There’s no special rubber bottom for traction on the floor but it seems to hold very well without it. It doesn’t slip when I position my neck over it. I can’t get my head to hang backwards over it like advertisement photos demonstrate due to my neck curvature issues, but that’s the goal. I realize achieving the goal will take time and regular use so I wasn’t unrealistically expecting immediate pain relief.

I also use the raised upper ledge of the device to roll the muscles across as a type of mini massage. It’s also good for applying targeted pressure for trigger point therapy with the same technique of utilizing the raised areas.

It has not eliminated pain. I think that will be a long time coming, if ever, but it does help to reduce headaches for short periods of time with the trigger point work.

It is definitely, grossly overpriced. Other products are available on Amazon that are nearly identical to this one for half the price. Otherwise, I’d give it 5 stars. Hopefully, the seller catches on and does a reasonable price adjustment.

Surprise, surprise!!. [[VIDEOID:69699f40545e4fc3a48bd740de95fbbc]] I had little hopes for the watch, but 3 days in, I’m sold!! I just bought the green one for a friend who’s giving up his Apple Watch after years!

I use Alexa way more than I use Siri, so having a fitness tracker with a watch feature that I can use to create shopping lists, reminders, lights, etc, is way better than trying to get Siri to add something to my calendar that she usually gets wrong.

Forget Fitbit and those $100+ trackers! This is seriously all you need to watch those steps, or for me, weight train. I’m 6’1”, 215lbs and the band is great on my wrist, love this thin band that doesn’t even feel like wearing anything!

review_text:
For the price it's fine. I would have bought something else knowing what I know now.. I bought this board to get around from place the place on my college campus. Overall, I'd recommend something else, but I'll get to that later.

The trucks can be loose enough to rub on the board, so be careful of that. The stock bearings are pretty crap, a cheap set of just about anything else is better. But I used the stock for 5-6 months so it's not something a beginner will notice to much. Just put them on the list of things to buy.

The middle flexes a lot, enough that 155lb (+40lb backpack sometimes) me worries about it. Put your weight over the trucks and your fine. Other reviews show cracked boards. Just be smart about it.

The turning is pretty tight, it's easy enough to learn on and get the hang of. I recommend tighter trucks for learning, then loosen as you get more skill/more comfort.

The wheels won't push anything out of the way, if there's a rock, the board will stop. And you'll keep moving. I know from experience.

It's a pretty smooth ride, certainly way more then a normal skateboard and will go faster then a normal skateboard. Won't do any tricks other then just leaning the front wheels up and turning a little, but it takes a lot of practice. A normal skateboard does that way, way better. Leaves tricks to normal boards is what I'm getting at.

It acts more like a longboard then anything in my opinion, but you get the downsides of it not being a longboard and having smaller wheels, and the only upside is slightly tighter turning vs a 38" longboard (drop thru style board) It's not much of a difference.

Here's why I'd recommend something else, at least for someone like me using it as transport across campus.
A longboard is just better. It's that simple.
A longboard is smoother, faster, more stable, turns almost as well (depending on board), kicks rocks out of the way instead of you going flying, easier to ride. The list goes on. Unless your super strapped for cash, spend a few more bucks and get a longboard, you'll be glad you did.

I now have a 38" drop thru style longboard w/ reds bearings and it's all I use. I don't use this board anymore at all. For the price, I feel I got my use out of it, so I'm not complaining necessarily, but I would have just bought a different board to begin with. But this was my first board I've ever owned, so I didn't know.

I will never go back to anything else. I love this rope.!. I love this jump rope. I am not new to jumping, but I’ve always used much thinner ropes. Even the speed rope in this set is bigger than what I’ve used in the past. I thought that’s where it was at, but after using this rope I cannot go back to my think rope.
I love that I can feel some weight in my hands. I’m not sure the physics behind this, but I am able to jump much more efficiently with this rope (less stopping/mistakes) and my heart rate is definitely more elevated. When I lift this rope, the weight makes me want to continue jumping. My arms get more of a workout too. This isn’t considered a weighted rope, I believe those at are t at 1/2 a pound, this one is barely 1/4 pound, so it’s really not heavy, but my body certainly feels the difference. I can’t wait to jump again once done. I even use it to get steps in and elevate my heart rate when my watch tells me it’s time to stand or if I just need a quick pick me up.
Quality-wise, the rope itself is solid and doesn’t keep links or bends, which also helps it be more efficient. The handle fees very high quality and doesn’t slip out of my hands when sweaty due to the material. Cutting to the appropriate length and fastening it in the handle was simple and easy and they also come with extra clips, which was nice, just in case. I wonder if you could order just the fasteners from epitome fitness if necessary though. Or maybe it’s free, that would be a bonus. But maybe I’ll never even need extras.

If you’re looking for a rope that gets you a real full-body workout and motivates you to keep going, this is it! Some reviewers mention the handles coming loose, meh. Just don’t drop the damn thing on the door all the time because the fasteners aren’t that tight. But if you tighten before jumping and place it down with care in between sets or circuits etc., they stay in place. A slight inconvenience if you’re in the zone and rushing and don’t have softer surfaces or mats to drop it quickly, but that wouldn’t make me return it. Sometimes we require way too much convenience, it’s really not that big of a deal, probably adds 1 second to your workout time each time, and hey… use that time to be more mindful of the kick-ass workout you’re doing while taking care of your body.

product_name: AMBIO Lightweight Snowshoes for Men Women Youth Kids, Aluminum Alloy Terrain Snow Shoes with Leg Gaiters and Carrying Tote Bag
review_text:
Reasonable for the price - not sure how long they'll last though, durability feels low. These performed well through half a dozen uses during my first winter with them, but I'm concerned they won't last more than a couple years. The plastic material that makes up the face of snowshoe gets very stiff when it is cold so I made sure to store them inside my heated home instead of in my garage to try to preserve them as long as possible.

The straps that loop over the top of the foot are a bit odd in that they're continuous with the rubbery base that your shoe sits on, this means they have to bend a lot to get around a shoe which gives me additional durability concerns, especially if stored in an unheated space.

The strap that loops around the back of your shoe is not rubber like the others, but instead is a very flimsy strap of nylon webbing which does not stay in place nearly as well as something more rigid.

The snowshoe surface pivots well around the toe of the user which feels comfortable, but the mechanism it does this by is by twisting a rubbery strap that spans across the width of the frame. For now it works well, but as with other components, I have concerned about how long this will last, as once it fails at one point, the snowshoes will be worthless.

The poles that came with these were pleasantly surprising for the pricepoint of the set. Are they amazing? No, but they do the job and are included with the snowshoes. They're adjustable and I had no issues with them slipping from the length they were set to. Additionally, they have an internal spring that allows them to compress roughly an inch when loaded heavily (but they rebound back to their originally-set length after) which is nice for taking some of the blow of a heavy impact out of them. The only limitation here is the length - they are not for tall people. I'm 6'-0" and use these at their longest length, so if you're taller than that, you'll probably want separate poles.

All in all, these have performed well through one winter. I have durability concerns long term but don't want to knock them too hard if it turns out durability isn't an issue. I will update in future winters if parts begin to fail due to poor durability.

review_text:
Great for the Price. This is I think the most basic offering by Allen Sports for a 3-bike hitch-mount bike rack. Allen Sports offers quite a range of racks and features at higher price points, so feel free to ignore reviews criticizing this model for not having this or that. At this price, this is a great bike rack.

You probably already know that for cars/SUVs you can do hitch-mount, trunk-mount, roof-mount and put-it-the-trunk-mount. Hitch-mounts come in hanging and "tray" versions. If you already have a hitch, this hanging version a great bargain. You can easily pay upwards of $800 for the fancier hitch-mounts. Also, if your car is hitchless, buying and installing a car hitch will cost you several hundred dollars, so maybe this is not the way to go. The advantages of hitch-mounts? Generally faster and more convenient bike mounting/unmounting than trunk- and roof-mounts, much faster trunk access (for rotating or swinging hitch-mounts) compared to trunk-mounts, and better gas mileage than roof mounts. One of the bigger annoyances for hitch mounts is having to use straps and padding in strategic places to keep the bikes from rubbing against each other and the car. If you are getting a lightweight hitch-mount, like this one, it also has the big advantage of ease of removal and transport and storage.

So...IF you will be using this rack only occasionally for that beach weekend or road trip, but otherwise want to store it in your home or garage, this is a great choice. It is well made, solid, lightweight and does the job. You are "giving up" many features, but if you need those, simply pay more. What you get: solid construction, fold-down arms, rotation for trunk access, a decent look (compact with stylish logo), ease of removal, compactness, and light weight. Here's what you don't get that might move you up the price scale (and how far up the scale is indicated by $$ signs): fast hitch removal (e.g. via a twist knob instead of a bolt) ($), lever for hanging bar rotation (instead of a removable pin) ($), lever for hitch rotation release (instead of a removable pin) ($), built-in hitch lock ($), built-in security cable ($), tray-style ($$ to $$$), super-rigidity ($$), rust-proof (all aluminum) ($$$).

By the way, you can loop a cable through any "hole" in your car hitch or chassis then through the triangular opening at the bottom of this rack then through your bike frame/wheels. This will probably achieve better security than the thin cables and unsophisticated key locks that come built-in with pricier units.

Also, getting more than 2 bikes on any hitch-mount rack is a pain. I got the 3-bike version because it makes a 2 bike mounting easier.

BOTTOM LINE: Gets the job done AND can be removed and stored relatively easily.

Very Nice Fenders, Great Price. Good soft fenders are among the most important accessories on our boat, and these fit the bill just fine. They are just the right size, and they appear to be made well enough to last for years. The rich black color will look super with our pontoon boat.

It's great that they come with nice black hanger ropes; not only do I not have to dig around for ropes to string them, but they will look just that much better in use. The ropes are very nicely pre-looped and very good quality.

I also like the storage bag. I have a nice big compartment for these on the boat, but it normally is pretty cluttered. The bag is not super heavy-duty, but it fits four fenders nicely, and it will help me tidy things up.

I've never bought bumpers like this that arrived deflated, so I've never inflated one before. I inflated the first one with the hand pump provided; it's a nice basic pump and it took me just a couple of minutes. I inflated the other three using a compressor, and they filled up very quickly. I wanted to be careful to not over-inflate them, so I just got them close to full with the compressor then finished them off with the hand pump.

I'm not entirely sure why they sent four inflation needles, but they tend to get lost easily so I'm happy to have them.

Bottom line, these are very nice fenders, and this is a very complete package for the price. I'm highly satisfied, and these are highly recommended.

review_text:
Feels Cheap, but Looks Good On Camera. To be super clear, I would not offer these hats to customers - they feel cheap and flimsy and the uneven stitching is readily apparent even on a cursory examination. I would never sell these to people. So if you're looking for a base for your custom embroidery or screen printing business, you should skip these, you'll get a bad reputation.

HOWEVER.

My use for these is different. I was looking for a cheap way to match the color of my hat to the color of other articles of clothing for music videos, and these are EXCELLENT for that. I'm planning a set of music videos in which I take a character concept and instead of "cosplaying" in the traditional sense, I'll be turning the characters into modern outfits and wearing those while performing songs about the characters. So for example, Spinal from Killer Instinct is a skeleton and his only real characteristics are that he's a skeleton and he has a bright red bandana. So, I'm using the bright red hat from this and decorating a work shirt with bone pieces. It's very low-budget, but it's effective, and using these hats saves a ton of money over buying "real" ones but it still allows me to play with this idea I had.

So if you're just using these on camera or from a distance, you're fine. The colors are bright and clear, the fit is... fine... and the assortment covers a pretty decent range of colors. There are a few seemingly minor things make it useless as a tactical pack.  First, once you put water in it the back gets heavy and starts to sink down.  Not really a problem for me it is going in my pack.  If I had to take it out and wear it on my back my day has gone horribly wrong.  But it would be nice to know that I could do so without the design, or more accurately the lack thereof, getting in the way.  Second and possibly most important this pack attempts to force the user to commit a cardinal and unforgivable sin of infantrymen.  While the pictures show it as ambidextrous, there is only a hole on the right side for the drinking tube.  This puts the drinking hose over your firing shoulder, exactly where it doesn't belong.  The hole that the hose was threaded through was so tight I could not get the end through.  I had to cut the hose and refit it to the quick release. product_name: Bowflex Max Trainer Series
review_text:
Not like an elyptica, more like a stairclimber-- WITH SUPER DEEP STEPS!. I bought this primarily for myself but for my mom, who is a bit elderly (shh, don't tell her I said that) and lives with me and is only 5' 2", to use too. The thing is GREAT. It's super-sturdy, like the kind of quality you'd get at a gym, not at all flimsy or teetery or any of that. The thing is, I'm 6' 1" with a 34" inseam, so long-legged, and the plunge of each step is even deep for me. I won't mind it because I'm still young enough that I've got decent knees and can handle it, but for my mom, who is a foot shorter than me, each step is ginormous, even deeper than if you climb regular stairs two at a time, which I do but my little mom never does.

WORD TO THE WISE: IF YOU'RE SHORT OR HAVE BAD KNEES, THEN PASS ON THE BOWFLEX MAX TRAINER.

My only other complaint about it is it's hard to get going. When you step on it, the pedal goes to the bottom of the cycle. Usually, with an elipitical, if you just give some forward or backward pressure, not down pressure, or if you just push with one arm and pull with the other, it'll get going, NOT THIS. It stays put. To get it going, you have to push down with the upper foot, sometimes so long and so hard that you rise off the bottom foot, meaning you're putting all your weight on that one knee that's already in a deep bend because of how deep the steps, and even doing that, sometimes you rise all the way up and it still doesn't move, you have to do this wiggly kind of dance to get it going-- and this isn't on some high resistance level, mind you, but on the very lowest, on 1. Once it gets going, it's fine, but getting it going is a bit of a bear and awfully hard on the knees. I've tried all sorts of things, like stepping on it really quick to try and get my other foot in place and pushing down before the foot I step on it with reaches the bottom of the cycle so that I can basically have the inertia of keeping it going, but while that sounds great in theory, it doesn't really work in practice. That bottom foot hits the nadir or apogee or trough very quickly and doesn't really have any momentum or inertia to carry you through.

That's probably because it's so much more like a stair climber than an elliptical. Imagine an elliptical on such a steep setting that when you hit the bottom of a cycle, you didn't feel your foot move backward at all but instead just start to rise right back up as you pressed down on the top foot. Another example of this is how with a normal elliptical, you'll sometimes go forward and sometimes go backwards with your feet because it uses somewhat different muscles and a different motion process. On the Bowflex Max Trainer, going forward and going backward feel identical. That's because your feet are just going up and down at an angle, not circling around in an ellipse.

It'll work for my needs, though I do fear for my knees a bit with it. But if space is a concern, you really can't beat this, because an actual elliptical, which I word argue this is NOT an elliptical at all and Bowflex should quit using that word in its marketing of the Max Trainer, takes up a lot more space. The length of space needed for an actual eliptical is a foot and a half to two feet longer. AND IT IS STURDY AND QUALITY!

ANOTHER GREAT THING ABOUT THE BOWFLEX MAX TRAINER M3 ($999) -- AND THAT'S WHAT I'M REVIEWING, THE M3 -- IS THE M3 IS IDENTICAL IN EVERY WAY THAT MATTERS TO THE MUCH PRICIER M6 ($1,499) AND M9 (1,999). All the extra $500 for the M6 is getting you is: one, a few extra speeds or levels of resistance, not greater resistance, just more choices, but the M3 has 8 and that's plenty; two, stationary hand sensors for heart rate, the M3 coming with a Blue Tooth chest strap instead; and, three, the ability to hook your phone up to it and pay money to subscribe to classes and trainers and interactive experiences, Bowflex's answer to Pelaton. All the $1,000 to an M9 gets you is: one, a few more speeds or levels of resistance than the M6, but why anyone would need that level of nuance in resistance, I can't imagine; two, motion hand sensors for heart rate, meaning Bowflex has put sensors on the moving handles instead of just the stationary ones; and, three, a small screen so that you don't have to use your phone. That seems like an AWFUL lot of $$$ for each of those upgrades. If you're not going to pay for a subscription and use it interactively like you might a Pelaton but instead plan to just listen to music or watch TV or whatever, then save yourself the $500 or $1,000 and get the M3 for two-thirds or half the price, respectively.

IN FACT, Bowflex must've gotten game to how people were realizing the M3 is EXACTLY THE SAME PRODUCT as the M6 at 50% more expensive and M9 at 100% more expensive ($1,999 instead of $999), because Bowflex no longer even sells the M3 on its website. All that's available now on Bowflex's website anymore is the M6 and the M9. Amazon, though, still sells the M3 for $999, what Bowflex sold it for, so if a Max Trainer is what you want but you don't want to spend $500 to $1,000 extra for superfluous add-ons that in no way should cost that much, that should cost at most $100 more, if that, because the equipment being added (like an extra set of heart sensors and notches on a dial is what you get for $500 more and a second extra seat of heartbeat sensors, a few more notches on a dial, and a small LCD screen half or quarter the size of a monitor is what you get for $1,000), THEN BUY THE M3 FOR $999 WHILE SUPPLIES LAST!!

Seriously, if you ask me, Bowflex should charge less for the M6 and M9 because of how much money they're making off the subscriptions. Since all that display equipment the M6 and M9 have on them that you're paying an arm and a leg for is totally useless unless you pay a monthly prescription, it pressures many if not most into paying the monthly subscription. Otherwise, it's kind of like options in a car you don't have but the car company still puts the totally useless buttons for, continually annoyingly reminding you and nagging you about what you don't have and being glaring to others what you don't have because they don't work-- only worse since it's the entire display in front of you that's useless without the subscription.

Basically, the M6 and the M9 are like if you paid 50% more to twice as much more for a car so that it would have a fancy dash board you'd install yourself via your phone (the M6) or that would have an all-digital display (the M9) but then had to pay $19.99/mo. in subscription fees for them to work (the $10/mo. rate is only introductory), and if you didn't pay the subscription, most of all of everything you paid all that extra money for wouldn't work at all but just sit there in front of you mocking you, telling you, "I'm not working even though you paid a buttIoad of money for me," and ever cajoling you to sign up to pay $19.99/mo. in perpetuity, something Bowflex really rakes in on for all those folks who go on long hiatuses from working out but, just like their gym memberships, never cancel because it's too much trouble or because they feel like that's conceding to failure and so keep it going with the idea that they will start working out again soon.

For me, I'll pass on that, which is why I went with the M3, something lots of folks were doing, which is why Bowflex no longer even markets the M3 on its website and is phasing it out.

product_name: Curing the Incurables
review_text:
It's worth the effort. I was diagnosed with Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia when I was discharged for 20 years in the navy. I remember when the doctor told me that I was devastated. I wasn't even really sure what it was or how bad it was. I started studying very hard to see if there was a solution (this was in 2012). One day it hit me. My sister had given me this book but I blew it off. Then, I took things into my own hands and did exactly as the diet suggested.

The first 3 weeks were, one week nothing but water and carrot juice. Next week the same but with apple juice. Oh and herbs that cleanse and strengthen the body. The third week with grape juice. Week 4 would be back to carrot juice. Week 5 apple. Week 6 grape. But, at the beggining of week 4 you can start introducing fruits, vegetables, grains. I even started eating fish once a week.

I continued doing that for about three months. I was already in decent shape. I had been training for a marathon, however while doing the diet I stopped running. The funny thing is even though I stopped running I could easily go out and run ten miles and not be sore the next day. This is when I was in my early 50's.

After 3 months I went back to the doctor and did some blood tests the week before. He came into the room and I was crossing my fingers that my white blood cell count was down. He came in and said, "we're not sure what you have. Your white blood count is almost back to normal." I just about fell out of my chair. I did several more check ups and my health was great. I found out something I never knew. All my life I couldn't breathe very well in spite of being in sports. It used to take me a few miles of jogging slow before my airways would open up and then I could take off and run. After a few months my lungs cleared up and I didn't need to warm up. I could just take off. I've often wondered since then that maybe I had light asthma. But now it was gone.

Well, it's been about eight years. I got lax and only did the diet about 2 years. In those times I never felt better or happier. I don't know the terms too well but the chemical that gets released in the brain that makes you feel happy, I felt that beautiful feeling everyday.

I would gladly suggest this program to anyone especially if you are up against a tough problem. I'd say if you were diagnosed with some kind of cancer that if you did this program it would help tremendously to help your bodies ability to fight it. I won't say it cures cancer because I know that's a drastic statement to make in the medical and health world.

I think if you try it you will see miracles. One caution is I see a lot of reviews where people say they tried variations or portions of the diet. Please go all in with this diet and you will see miracles and you will be happy to see your health get tremendously better.
Best of luck.

One more word. I see the 'top critical review' saying it was an overpriced advertisement.' Comments like that make you feel they were paid to say that. It works.

product_name: Blue Magic Petroleum Jelly 12 oz.
review_text: Fabulous!. I bought Blue Magic's Petroleum Jelly on a whim, and I'm glad I did. I've heard of this product from them before but found it for the first time at my local hair supply store in NYC. I used it as a sealant for my 4C natural hair after washing, deep conditioning, and then moisturizing it with hot water and aloe vera gel. What's most interesting about this product is that it's not really a grease, but it's too shiny, too oily, and too smooth to pass off as petroleum jelly, it's also too white in color to even pass off as something like Vaseline, which is an off-yellow color. I was skeptical at first as to how my hair would respond to this because this product is very in-between, and also odd, in many ways. It's scented but its scent is barely there, like there's a slight floral smell, but it's really hard to detect it, sometimes you smell it, sometimes you don't. Using this as a grease on your hair makes you feel like you're using what I'd call a "clean" grease, where it doesn't have the heavy coloring, fragrance, and oils like their original blue or green Blue Magic, it's just petroleum jelly infused with aloe vera, safflower oil, and vitamin E. To my surprise, this product worked just like those greases. It's not too heavy, but it's not too light either. It held my two-strand twists together very beautifully. It actually gave my style a slicker and smoother look to it, and my hair was so moisturized. This is advertised as being like an all-purpose petroleum jelly where you can also use it on your body, hands, lips, etc. but I think you're better off just using straight up Vaseline; I just don't think it quite works in the same way because, again, it's just way too shiny, oily, and greasy for that, but as a sealant on moist/wet hair? Fabulous. I wouldn't go out of my way to just buy this product, but if I go back to the shop to get my favorite products and I so happen to see it's in stock still, sure, I'll grab it!

product_name: Prevention Easy Healing Stretches: Follow-Along Routines - Guided Stretching routines to Alleviate Pain, Boost Energy, and Feel Amazing
review_text:
Strengthening and Stretching Step-By-Step - Pilates and Yoga Based Exercises and Stretches!. Kathi Ross-Nash is a wise, beautiful and elegant instructor who obviously has a lot of experience with Pilates and yoga. She has a slim, toned and strong body and can do exercises with advanced precision. It is a joy to watch her body move through all the poses and stretches and I especially loved how her makeup was done. Her voice and chatty style lulled me into a relaxed state almost like hypnosis. I found her instructions calming and soothing.

Some of the exercises are done in a chair like the face and neck exercises. You will do shoulder shrugs and stretch the neck side to side. Then you will do eye exercises and facial exercises that help relax your jaw. You may find these exercises and stretches especially healing if you work on a computer all day or if you tend to clench your jaw from stress.

Other exercises are done on the floor with a yoga mat. The hip exercises and stretches have some easy and advanced poses that are inspired by Pilates. The leg stretches can be modified with yoga blocks and include active stretching that test endurance and strength. You will move quickly from one pose to another.

For the Feet and Calves you will need a chair and two yoga blocks. If you've never exercised your feet before like this you may want to take the rest of the day off or try the chest openers next.

The Chest stretching was actually one of my favorite parts of this DVD. You will feel your core being strengthened too. You will need a strap - a yoga one works great.

To do some of these stretches you will need to be able to get down onto the floor and back up again. Not so easy for me now that I'm over 50 but I pushed through and did it anyways. So I would say this DVD also tests your resilience and endurance not to mention patience and flexibility. I could have easily done all these exercises with no problem in my 20s, 30s and 40s! So if you do a lot of yoga and Pilates you may find these exercises very relaxing and invigorating.

There is a bar on the left side of the screen to clue you in to how long you still have until completion of each section. It is not distracting once you get used to it and seems helpful.

Some of the props you will need include 2 yoga blocks, a strap, a clean dry washcloth, a rubber band and a small ball for the foot exercises. I managed without the small ball but definitely used the strap and found a rubber band in my drawer that worked. The washcloth is used for the jaw stretches but nowhere else.

Some of my other favorite DVDs for Stretching and Strengthening include:

Simply Stretch by Jessica Smith
Yoga for Inflexible People
Pilates on the Go by Maria Leone
Face Aerobics
Karen Voight Full Body Stretch
Stretch and Strength by Anne Pringle Burnell (Especially geared for those over 50!)

I think it is a worthy goal to collect as many of these excellent DVDs as you can because stretching DVDs are what you need to feel good and flexible as you age. This Easy Healing Stretches DVD has five sections that you can do over a period of days to increase your whole body's strength and tone. Enjoy!

~The Rebecca Review

Keeps cool for a LONG time!. I bought this with the intent to bring it on our upcoming trip to Disney World (summer in Florida... need I say more?). My plan is to dedicate this water bottle to filling with ice, and then divvying up said ice between my family of 4's individual water bottles throughout the day. So, knowing this is strictly going to be our "ice" water bottle, my kids & I decided to do a "speriment" (as my 3yo daughter called it, LOL) to see just how long we can anticipate our ice to stay frozen.

Upon receiving the item, I hand washed it and then filled it to the brim with ice. I did this at 8:33am on 5/23/22. My kids and I would check on it every morning and night, draining off the melted-ice-water that had accumulated in the bottle so we could better see where the ice level was upon each inspection. It took until 6:30am on 5/26/22 for the ice to be fully melted!! Now, granted, this was sitting inside my house at a lovely 70 degrees, not outside in the sun in 95 degree weather, but still. 3 days of ice is pretty darn good if you ask me! Overall would definitely recommend, and for the price you can't beat it!

product_name: Beurer Professional Ultrasonic Cleanser with Digital Timer for Jewelry, Rings, Coins, White, 18.5 Fl Oz
review_text:
Good for Loose Hard to Reach Dirt on Things. I had set my expectations too high with this ultrasonic cleaner and really any other small household ultrasonic cleaner. The first thing I wanted to try cleaning was the coffee stained spoon with soap and water but it seemed there was really no change. Scraping the stain off with my fingernail did way more than what the cleaner did. I realized for the price I shouldn't have expected that.

Instead these what it's good at are for things with dirt or gunk from our oily sweaty dirty body that gets built up that is hard or near impossible reach with a brush. For me that's been useful as a parts cleaner for my radio control cars mainly plastic parts using a 10 part water to 1 part of simple green.

The cleaner without the basket has a max physical capacity of 6x5x1.5" (1.5" max water line) that yep you can fit a CD/DVD mentioned on the product box and product photos in this listing.

There is a drain hole at the bottom if there's ever a chance water gets past the top gasket when being dumped out.

As another reviewer pointed out there is conflicting information about what can be cleaned with this ultrasonic cleaner and that reviewer is correct. In the included manual does warn not to clean things like glasses and dentures yet the product listing and photos here says you can. These same product photos and information is listed on their shop-beurer website too.

In the end these warnings about not cleaning certain things is to protect themselves from any liability if something gets damaged and only using soap and water if one gets injured if using chemicals not in a well ventilated area which I completely understand. So why the conflicting information?

Extra technical stuff.
It uses a ChuangXin CX-768 stuck to the bottom of the bowl to produce the 43kHz frequency. There's not much information about that part other than it's used in some other ultrasonic cleaners sold in different countries which I assumed priced similarly as this Beurer.

I found someone with the same tent to tell me how to put the cap on, but I still haven't figured out how to put the flap up.

That being said, I love this tent. I'm 5'1" and I can put it up by myself in 5-10 minutes. It's withstood rain and heavy winds with no issues at all. The seat is very low to the ground, which has pros and cons to consider. For example, I have been to a private beach which would not allow chairs to be set up unless they were short ("can't block the beach view"), and these are perfect for that. review_text: 4 month upadate. I'm a 75 year old man who has been riding a regular bike for years and years but my knees were telling me that hills were no longer their friend. I moved from a place with NO hills to a place where hills are everywhere so I decided to look in to an ebike that was within my budget. This bike seemed to be just what I needed so I decided to give it a shot...First thing was it was very easy to assemble (Youtube helped)..then I decided to take it for a spin. This bike is a completely different experience so my advise would be to practice in a place that's deserted...so here's the low down on my first week of riding on a regular basis....first, this bike will get up and go and reach 20 mph very fast, and for me that was my first surprise, then getting a feel for the 5 levels of resistance 1 being the most and 5 is where you hardly pedal at all, but here's where you need to pay attention....the throttle takes up about half the right handle bar so it's very easy to accelerate when you don't want to so pay attention...then there the issue with the kick stand which seems be very wobblily and a little unstable....having said that, I really like this bike, it's very easy and fun when you get used to it...quick note, I would not leave my house with charger plugged it just to be safe...So now on July 13th or having the bike for over a month the only thing that is driving me nuts is the kick stand...it flops down over and over again even after tightening the so called locking mechanism..it is aggravating and turns my bike ride into a hassle.....it's a terrible TERRIBLE design....................*******.........So I've  owned the bike almost 4 months and I continue to love this bike, I replaced the kick stand and replaced the seat with one a lot more comfortable, The one thing that, for me, makes the ride safer and more predictable is....if I'm riding near people or on roads with intersections I keep the resistance on 1 or 0 and use the hand throttle to provide power to the bike. I used to keep it on 2-4 but found that when I wanted to stop if any pressure was put on the pedals when trying to stop immediately throws the bike forward when you're not expecting it..I learned the hard way and it wasn't pretty..In my opinion controlling the bike with the hand throttle is the safest except if your riding on a trail or on a road with no stop and go...This in my opinion is the best and safest way to operate the bike with the electric assist....aside from that this is a great entry level bike at a very good price.  I look forward to many more miles of fun...

review_text:
Great facial steamer with a fantastic look!. [[VIDEOID:a6226cb3f85010349ed640dec3d79e96]] What do you get:

1- The facial steamer device.
2- A stainless-steel skin kit including 4 tools.
3- Instruction manual.
4- Oil pad and its mount for using essential oil.
5- A measuring cup.

This facial steamer works great. The first thing I noticed was the fantastic and stylish design. It comes with a fairly long power cable to reach the plug conveniently. Using the device is very easy, you fill the measuring cup that comes with the device up to 80ml and pour it into the device, add essential oil on the pad if you want and place it in front of the steamer nozzle and turn on the device by pressing the power button.

It takes seconds to start the stream of the steam and the good point was that it was a consistent stream both in the flow and its temperature. The stream is warm enough to feel good on your skin and as long as you don’t move your face very close to the nozzle, you won’t have any problems with the steam burning your skin. Adding your favorite essential oil will add a much more pleasant scent to it as well. It is mentioned in the instruction to use the device for a few times a week and no more than 10 minutes each time. Based on personal experience, the device doesn’t run more than 20 minutes with 80ml but that’s more than enough for one person.

Pros:

1- Stylish design for the device and the plastic dome.
2- Decent length power cable.
3- Consistent stream of steam and temperature.

Cons:

1- The refill capacity is only 80ml which is not very much but more than enough for one complete use.
2- The plastic dome doesn’t sit stable enough and the slightest push can move it, so you have to be careful with it.

Overall, this facial steamer is fantastic. I would highly recommend this if you are looking for something convenient for at-home usage.

review_text: Great price....but useless outdoors. Yes, the price is quite good.  The device itself is probably better than what you might think based on the price.  But I returned mine.  Why? And yes I suppose I could pull the phone out and check the results.  But then why bother to have the Amazfit?  I could just use my android phone to perform most of the same functions.  OK not heart rate etc.  But the accuracy of those readings on the Amazfit can be off.  Plus my Tic watch - admittedly larger/heavier etc - can perform the same functions as the Amazfit.  Battery life on my Tic watch does not even come close to the battery life on the Amazfit.  But that seems irrelevant considering I can't read anything while out hiking.  Ultimately I ended up returning it.

review_text:
Arrived With Odor. When I received the zeolite rocks I noticed an urine-like odor on the bags that came with them but I thought it would dissipate later. Yet, after a few hours it was stronger, so I removed the rocks from the bags and put them in two cut tee shirt sleeves, it was better than the bags but still smelly. Finally, I put the zeolite in plastic cups which, again, was better but didn't dispel the odor all together. I thought in time the odor would dissappear.

On the second day, I sprinkled about six or seven of the rocks on an unused basement bathroom floor behind the door where one of the original odors I was trying to get rid of was strongest, but after awhile it became unbearable. My nose, throat, face and chest were burning. I collected the rocks and put them away in a drawer. After contacting the company about the odor and receiving no response, I decided to return them.

On the third day, I put them in foam bowls in the sunlight to air out. Even after two hours the odor was still there. I put the zeolite and its bags back into the original packaging. The return was picked up today, the fourth day after I used them.

I considered what could have gone wrong. There were river rocks already in some of these places which I had to remove because the odor from the zeolite clung to them. Also, in two places I had plugin negative ion emitters. But after removing them, the odor grew stronger. I can only conclude that the urine-like smell from the bags was the original problem.

I believe that the zeolite outgassed the odor from the bags that came with it. The odor still has not dissipated from my home though it's not as strong as it was before. I'll have to wait. Hopefully, it’ll be gone soon.
The zeolite did get rid of the odors in the places I placed them in. Even behind the basement bathroom door. But the pain and burning I received in return was, of course, not worth it.

review_text:
Avoid if you need total all-day calories counted (active & passive). For the price, this watch has a lot of great features! It feels more smart-watch than fitness-tracker. And if you don't mind it not counting your calories all day (aka, using your heart rate to determine the number of calories burned every minute of a 24-hour period), then this product will be great for you. Unfortunately, since the main reason I wanted the watch was to give me a daily calorie burn (active and passive calories), this watch was mostly useless for me. It gets 2 stars because outside of that specific thing, it seems to work great. But only 2 stars because that one thing was the only thing I really needed

Some of the big Pros are:
1. Customizable watch faces - displays time, date, heart rate, calories burned, battery level, # of steps - whatever you want.
2. Light, barely notice it's there
3. Lots of 'apps' like weather, notifications, blood oxygen, stress, breathing, female tracking, calendar, music controls, etc.

Can't figure out how to enlarge font of some of the items on the watch face (font is very small for some things)

review_text:
There is good and bad about this tent. [[VIDEOID:5ba8346c8190be257fcfb02066a45a3e]] I was hoping to take this camping and really give a great camping review, however the living room setup will have to do. This tent definitely has some good and bad things about it, let me elaborate:

The good:
1. Setup is really easy, you can pop this tent up in less than 1 minute.
2. It’s surprisingly lightweight, the entire thing likely weighs less than 5 lbs, you’ll have no issues with it.
3. It’s relatively easy to break down and roll back in the storage bag.

The bad:
1. There’s 0 ventilation in this tent. The top is not mesh and keep this in mind as you’d have to leave the doors cracked (the inner lining is not mesh either). This is a bad design because likely leaving the doors unzipped would not be a great idea (bugs, animals etc.)
2. The tent is cheap, like you definitely get what you pay for, this is a low level tent that would probably not last for years and years, a couple max.
3. This is water resistant but the fabric definitely wouldn’t hold the rain out in a large storm.

So, really what it comes down to is what you’re personally looking for. This would be a GREAT tent for the beach or for a kids backyard play tent in the summer, I wouldn’t recommend it for any serious campers out there. The main thing I worry about is the lack of airflow, this is the main reason I only rated it 3 stars.

product_category: Cell Phones & Accessories | Activity & Fitness Trackers
review_text:
Better than expected. 1: First impression: Hard to open. The packaging did not indicate how you’re meant to actually open it. There’s a little grey tab (unmarked) on the side of the box you’re meant to pull so that it tears the box open for you. Took me way too long to figure it out.
2: The instruction booklet is practically useless. I read it but it didn’t really help me learn to use the watch.
3: The watch itself is not accessible for people with bad vision, lacking fine motor skills, or who are technologically inept (like me). Overall, I would not recommend this product for the elderly. The screen is very small. It is a touchscreen face but again very small with means any and all text on it will also be very small. To turn it on there is a small grey oval on one end of the watch face. That’s the ‘Home’ button and it turns the watch on and returns the user to the main screen. You can swipe up or down to view the other features and you can tap to go further in depth with each feature.
4: The strap is hard to put on snugly. I primarily use this to measure my heart rate so for me purposes I need it to lay flat against my wrist which I can do because my hands are affected by anything like arthritis or shaking.
5: Accuracy wise I can only speak for the heart rate measurement feature (again as that the main reason I’m using it) and when comparing it to a metronome at the same bpm it reads at, it matches. I am confident in its accuracy. However, having said that, it is NOT a constant monitor. In the app settings you can adjust how frequently the watch measures your heart rate and the most frequent setting is every minute. Next intervals are every five minutes and every ten minutes.
6: the app is very customizable but can be confusing because there are so many options but I like that it allows the user to hide features they won’t use so there’s less clutter.
7: the battery lasts for a while and after a full day I’ve seen it drain about 10% ish so I’d assume it’s meant to last a week before needing a recharge.

I’m satisfied with it as a whole and it works for me and my purposes but I don’t think this is the best fit for everyone. It’s quality for the price and I’m happy with it.

product_name: TETON Sports Backpacking-Tents Mountain Ultra Tent
review_text:
Quality fade is readily apparent.. I have an older Teton sports mountain ultra tent that I bought in 2015. It was a great tent for a great price. I have recommended Teton Sports to many people because of that tent. The quality of this tent is not the same.

The ways that this tent is different from previous generations and things that I hate about this tent are: The tent floor is of light weight material and not at all durable. The seam sealing is poorly done. The tent is poorly sewn together so that the zippers no longer are one handed opening. The ridgeline pole ends make contact with the rainfly and will quickly wear a hole in the thin material in the rainfly. Last but not least the tent no longer comes with a footprint.

My question is what is in store for the next generation of tents? Are they going to continue to increase price and reduce quality until it is useless?Are the doors, poles, stakes, or the rainfly going to be sold separately too?

If you are going to buy this tent be prepared to buy the footprint or use a piece of 4mil painters plastic, and be prepared to make modifications to this tent. I made and sewed a sleeve on for the ridgeline pole to keep it from puncturing the rainfly. If you are going to buy the grey color, it is not grey at all it is a bright nonmetallic silver. It does not reflect heat and it is not dark enough to blend in or reduce light transmission. There is a lot of mesh so you can get some airflow which will reduce condensation inside the tent. It could also be bad if camping in cooler weather.

All in all this tent is not terrible, but it’s not excellent, and it’s not what it used to be. You can find better tents, and you can find much cheaper tents.

My conclusion is Teton Sports has lost my trust and respect with the quality fade of this new generation tent. They have lied about the color of the tent which makes me think that if they will lie about that, what else will they lie about? Their warranty possibly? It is for this reason that this tent has to be returned and it is for this reason I will not recommend any Teton Sports products to anyone ever again.

review_text:
Aw well. My bedroom is very bright in the morning and I love to wake up to that, so when I want to go back to sleep I put something over my eyes. I was excited about getting this (free, through the Vine program). Figured it would be perfect. Not for me, unfortunately. Too bad, as it would make a lovely (though perhaps naughty seeming) gift. It comes in a lovely box and it feels heavenly on. So soft!

However, the size and shape of it are really off, at least for me. For reference, I have a small and rather narrow face. That’s why it is surprising that it’s a bit too narrow for me. Also, the notch for the nose is very shallow and because of that light gets in from the bottom. It simply does not fit my face properly. It’s good enough, but if you want solid darkness it is doubtful you will get it. Perhaps it will fit someone who has a flatter nose? I don’t know. product_name: Premium Handcrafted 25 Momme Mulberry Silk Eye Mask for Sleeping (Purple Passion)
review_text:
It's Nice, but not $35 Nice. First, I think this would make an excellent gift for anyone on your list who sleeps. Research shows that even small amounts of light in a room while sleeping can trick your brain into unhealthy sleep patterns and restless nights. And with every electronic gizmo in the world these days emitting some kind of light, a "dark room" can end up being not that dark (I am talking to you Alexa-with-a-display). For that reason I sleep with an eye mask to make sure that all my peepers see is... nothing.

As a gift the presentation of this silk eye mask is nice. It definitely comes through as a luxury gift in a fancy box.

But I can't imagine spending $35 on this for myself. It's no softer than the polyester eye mask it is replacing.

I did notice that my head size resulted in needing to extend the adjustable strap almost to its limit. I don't think my head is that large, really, so this may not fit a very large person.

If you have money you don't need, I think you'll find this eye mask is an excellent way to lighten some of that load.

product_name: Schwinn Air Center Floor Bike Pump, Guage Fits Schrader and Presta Valve Types, Multiple Colors
review_text:
Good pump, but the valve design is backwards. Pros: It has metal step on bottom, with a nice size gauge that is easy to read. The pump motion is smooth and with a nice flexible hose, although it does not have protective shielding on it so it could get pinched and cause leaks, but that remains to be seen. The pump head (part that goes on the valve stem of tire) is all plastic.
Cons: After using a few times, even though the directions were clear, the pump head design is counter-intuitive and completely backwards. You have to "close" the valve lever BEFORE you install it on the valve stem of the tire and then you have to "open" the head clamp/lever to clamp it on tight.
This is backwards of over 70 years of hand pumps built all around the world where you close the lever to attach and open the lever to get it off. No one uses the presto stem hole on this side of the planet so it makes for a bulky clumsy pump head design that is tight to fit between the spokes on a bike AND for that I give one star for ease of use and bulkiness.

review_text: Fine cooler - READ BELOW. This is a fine cooler - but you have to follow a few rules, otherwise don't complain about ice "melting too fast".  First, pre-chill everything that you plan to fit in the cooler. Sometimes I'll even freeze my drinks for a few hours (not soda cans!!)  Second, make sure the cooler itself is not sitting in the hot sun before you pack it.  I actually place the cooler itself in the fridge the night before I plan to use it.  As other users have mentioned this is a floppy kinda cooler.  Find a plastic bin at your local store (Wally World) that will fit inside this bag.  Then add your cans or drinks, fill almost to the top with ice (ice cools from the top down, not the other way around), then I add my food items (usually wraps or sammiches) on top of the ice.  I take this kayaking with me in the blaring sun and never had all the ice melt before I had the chance to eat and drink most of what I brought.

review_text:
Excellent value given the features. This is a full-featured fitness tracker with all the bells and whistles you'd want to see in such a device - heartbeat monitoring, workouts, steps, sleep, etc. It uses your phone for GPS, but that's fine. The touchscreen works well, although occasionally it can be difficult to see in direct sunlight. So far with heavy use I haven't seen any scratches on the screen, and it's possible to buy replacement bands in a variety of colors for very little money so if the color you want isn't in stock keep that in mind. All in all, I really like it.

The only knocks on it are that sometimes it will give a different step count than the phone (maybe that's the phone's fault, who knows), the aforementioned screen brightness issue, and I've had nights where I knew I was awakened by work issues where the sleep tracker listed those times as REM Sleep. None of those are enough for me to not recommend this device - I think it's absolutely great given the price and it fundamentally does everything I want it to do.

review_text:
Looks good! Will update soon!. So far so good! I haven’t been able to test it yet, but here a few thoughts so far. I was going to return it because I ended up with multiple paddleboards after Amazon Prime Day, but I’m hanging on to it. My husband used the Shop-Vac to inflate it mostly in our living room, then we both took turns with the manual pump. The pump says “new” on it, so maybe it’s an improved version. The pump worked fine. It’s important to realize that the psi won’t even register until about 5 psi and even then it takes a while for the needle to move. On the bottom of the paddleboard, it says that the recommended psi is 12 and that’s what we are planning on for all of our paddleboards. 15psi is the maximum. I would not recommend that you try using any sort of inflation option without leaving the last amount of inflation to the manual pump. No doubt it’s hard work and more difficult for a shorter person with a “belly”. It’s best to have two people sharing the hard work! One observation is that there are NO d-rings to attach a seat. That’s a drawback and something the company might want to address for future improvement. Many paddleboards have d-rings for a seat. Four are needed towards the middle of the board. The other observation is that the green version has a lot of white on it, so it could get dirty-looking over time depending on where you paddle. Other than that, it looks good so far! The foam top looks good and the inflation valve worked perfectly. On the manual pump there are two openings at the top. You need to connect the hose to the one that says “out”. I learned this much! The bag seems fine and I’ll check out the paddle and update my review.
Happy Paddling!

It thankfully didn't rain too much on our trip so I can't vouch for how water resistant it is, but it seems pretty good.

review_text: Very flimsy plastic lid that breaks easily!. We have now owned several of these water bottles, as they are a really great size, and we enjoy the flip top feature; however, before purchasing, please know that the plastic lid has a weak point that will break if dropped on basically any surface at all.  While we try very hard not to drop our water bottles, accidents occasionally happen, and the lids of two of our water bottles are now broken.  I was hopeful that I could find replacement lids either on Amazon or on the Stanley website, but, evidently, they do not make replacement lids for these bottles.  I contacted the Stanley company just to make sure that they do not make a replacement lid (I explained that the lids were broken due to drops, and I was hoping to purchase new lids).  I received an email back stating that all Stanley products are covered under a lifetime warrant, and they then asked me to submit pictures and fill out a detailed form, which I did, though, it took me a long time to compile all of the requested information, and I had to resend the email 4 times as their email kept telling me that it was "undeliverable".  A few days later, I received an email saying that my "ticket" had been resolved and closed, but I had never received a response from my original email.  So, I emailed back stating that my issue was not resolved, and I resent all of the information that they had originally requested.  Weeks later, I received an email apologizing for how busy they are and stating that the warranty doesn't cover accidental damage, and that I should look on their website or Amazon for a replacement lid.  So, basically I just wasted a bunch of time submitting useless information that they never needed and never received an answer to my original questions.  So, that's that.  If you buy this water bottle, just know that if it gets dropped at all, the cheap, plastic lid will break, and you will be left with a very nice, but useless water bottle.

review_text:
Small BUT Mighty! Excellent Choice for Day Hikes. I love, love, LOVE this backpack!!
In my decade of hiking, I can't believe it took me this long to find a backpack that suits me perfectly.
The quality is wonderful, and the olive color is bright and cheerful. The zippers slide open and close smoothly, and the mesh backing allows for optimum breathability for sweat. There is an nice arrangement of compartments to help keep your essentials organized and tidy while on the trail. I found this size to be perfect for a half-day hike, as there is space for a 30oz water bottle (or water bladder), a dry bag, some fruit, sunglasses, tissues, a small towel, and a safety tool. I love the fit of this pack; it hugs the body so well. The shoulder straps are very supportive and comfortable. I appreciate that the pouch in the front even has space to store a bike helmet. My favorite feature is the waist and chest straps that ensure a secure hold while hiking (or any other outdoor activity). There are two zippered compartments along the waist strap that are the perfect size for my iPhone 11, as well as a safety whistle built right into the chest strap. I'm impressed with the intention and quality of this design.
If you're on the market for a super minimal, lightweight, high-quality backpack for your lighter hiking or biking needs, look no further. This little guy is mighty and will not disappoint. What a world of difference it is to downsize! I highly recommend this backpack as a way to lighten the load without having to sacrifice useful storage space.
I posted some photos to give you a closer look and hope that they, along with my experience, help you out a bit with deciding what's best for your outdoor needs. Thank you!

review_text:
Love Amazfit products!. If you are going to use this with an Android, do yourself a favor and get the Notify app instead of using the stock app. You can use it without trusting the cloud, and Notify provides SO much more data and so many great charts!

In fact, get one of these bands with Notify, then the open source OpenScale app (or GadgetBridge) and a compatible smart scale (for maybe $20) and a Bluetooth blood pressure monitor (another $20) and you can monitor much of your health 24/7, without providing Big Brother with personal data. You can use Tasked or a similar app to grab the output of these apps and USB it via MQTT to Home Assistant, or any database you like. Get realtime health updates on everyone in your family! Using the Alexa Integration in HA, you could do things like "Alexa, what is Grandpa's current heart rate?"

And if privacy isn't a big concern for you, you can use MyFitnessPal or any other caloric intake app to monitor your diet, and aggregate all of these things with Google Fit. Then you can sync Google Fit to your doctor's health care app (MyChart or whatever). Now your doctor can see it!

So many cool options. I wish I was half my age, because technology that is right around the corner will be amazing.

review_text: Great Value, Flows Well, Doesn’t Clog. I have been running tubeless for years. Last year I started running tire inserts as well. I started to have an issue with the valves sealing somehow against the inserts in some of my tires. I could still add air, but could not release air or use a pressure gauge. I like to keep my tires at precise air pressures so this was unacceptable. These valves have holes in the sides as well as the ends so they can’t get blocked by the insert. I replaced both major brand name valves in two of my bikes with these. They work perfectly, install easily (all of them sealed up perfectly on the first try), and look great. They are a great value for the apparent quality. They come with two different sets of valve caps, and both styles have core removers built into them. Even the packaging is nice.
