review_text:
I was skeptical, but this really works!. I saw a web ad for this shortly after a dental cleaning visit. As has been the case with recent visits, they were concerned about my gums, measuring many "3s" and some "4s". They said that if I didn't improve my dental hygiene, I was looking at more severe gum problems that might occur. I had also had some recent cavities.

Anyway, I got sucked into one of those 30 minute long Facebook ad videos on this product and I figured, why not run an experiment. So I ordered a set of bottles and faithfully took 2 capsules every day until my next visit, 6 months later. I was careful not to change anything else. Same diet (pretty healthy). Same brushing (once at bedtime). Same flossing (once in a blue moon when something was stuck in my teeth).

My teeth felt great heading to my next cleaning visit, but I was curious to see if anything changed. The hygienist was in shock, and she brought in the dentist to show him how my teeth were suddenly down to all "1s" and "2s". They were both intrigued and asked me what changed.

Since that visit, I went down to just one capsule, every few days. Yesterday I visited again (6 months later from above) and the hygienist didn't even do the usual thing of calling in an assistant and reading out numbers. She scanned over the gums with her probe and reported to the dentist that everything was great.

It's only anecdotal evidence; one experience of one person; it could be a fluke. Nonetheless, I'm here on Amazon buying more supply for me, and because my wife wants to start using them too.

review_text:
Great dump pouch for Saddle Hunting. Before the meat and potatoes of this review, to my brothers and sisters in the tactical arena - be aware of the velcro closures this has and the noise discipline issue this causes. I got this for hunting and it's a factor in that world as well but not as much as on an operation with the safety of you and your team in the balance.

Here are my initial thoughts: good camo pattern that is muted in color. Material looks pretty solid overall and the stitching is sufficient. Nothing jumps out at me as cheap or poorly crafted/constructed.

This is a nice change in dimension from a lot of the other options on Amazon as it's larger - dimensions in the item description. It seemed that all others I looked at were a significant price jump or were all the same 7-8 inches tall.

I wanted this to store climbing rope for saddle hunting. I have primarily hunted from the ground in the past and will continue to do so with minimal gear, but I'm now exploring the S.H. world and want the option to have my ropes with me if I decide to change elevation from ground to tree. That was a big factor in why I wanted a larger pouch, because I will be going out with 70' of 11mm line.

In the pictures you see this with a standard cooking spray can in one of the pockets (just to give you an idea of size capabilities) so you could easily carry bug spray, sun screen, 2 bottles of water etc. There is about 50' of rope (butterfly storage style) inside it and propped next to a 26oz yeti water bottle for size reference. The dump pouch has 2 external pockets with a bungee top to help retention.

With all that rope in the pouch there was still plenty of room for more rope, a bigger system, extra gear etc.

If not in use then this folds up easily back to the compact configuration which is a plus if you plan on using this in a manner of a true dump pouch, and would do well for the military/ tactical setting.

At the price point of $13 this fits right in with the Amazon "no name" products and is FAR less expensive than others and offers more features than the no name products.

As I mentioned above, the closure of the main pouch is velcro and there's no avoiding that making noise. Keep that in mind but I'm sure there are some crafty ways to quiet it down if it becomes a problem.

Lastly, the opening.. I really wasn't sure how I would feel about this and if it would be a hindrance. So far in my testing it has not been a problem.

In the photos as stated above there was about 50' of rope. I later tested this with 70' of 11mm Samson rope and kind of surprisingly had absolutely no problem getting it in. There was enough room that with carabiners, hitch cord or whatever this would fit without issue.

I broke my foot so I haven't been able to get in the tree with the pouch on my saddle as intended. Once that occurs I will update this review with anything relevant learned.

review_text:
Good, but it's still an air mattress. I got this sleeping pad for my kids after hearing that they weren't happy with the flat mat they were using (and started fighting over the slightly softer foam one). This is self-inflating, which is its own animal. So you'll want to keep a few things in mind.

For one, "self-inflating" doesn't mean "efficient inflating" or "fast-inflating." As other reviewers have noted, it inflates at its own pace, chiefly determined by the valve that you have no control over. I really don't like this, as on camping trips I don't have time to wait while it inflates -- when it's about to rain, we often move VERY quickly as a family to get our tent set up, and we can't wait around for things to inflate.

For another, because it inflates, it is affected by temperature. This is a big deal, as we now account for it for my wife and I's air mattresses -- we just assume we'll need to top off the air each day before we lay on the mattress. It's determined almost entirely by the temperature change. In the Northeast, the temperature swing in Spring and Fall can be significant between day and night, so this is to be expected -- but with this mattress, you're giving up the ability to adjust it.

Finally, consider where you store it. The aforementioned temperature shifts wreak havoc on these sorts of inflatables. Don't think you can leave it in a hot attic, shed, or the trunk of your car and then just whip it out and use it. The swings in temperaute cause expansion and contraction enough that it will destroy the valve over time.

Now for the good stuff: if you don't have a pump in the wilderness, which happens a lot, it works great! The mattress essentially inflates itself. Deflating isn't hard but does take more effort as you have to squeeze the air out as you roll out. But then if you're tent camping you know how to do this already (we get better at this with every camping trip).

If you want an air mattress without all the inflating, this will work nicely. But it has all the downsides of an air mattress as well. We go with foam mattresses for this reason.

review_text:
overall a good bike. Only issue, the seat is very uncomfortable. There isn't much in the way of shocks on this bike, and I live out in the country so there are a lot of bumps in the road and such here. So I will have to replace the seat with something a bit more friendly to the posterior region. Other than that small issue, it's been good to me overall since I bought it.

I have heard other people say that the battery burnt out after only 47 miles (a local here in town bought the exact same one and mentioned it to me) but mine is still going strong for now anyway. I DID think ahead and I bought the 2 year extended warranty for it, as well as renter's insurance to cover lost or damaged property, so I should be covered should anything go amiss with it.

Overall though, this is a great bike for people who may have some mobility issues and can't actually pedal a bike, but would like to get out and be more active. (like myself) for me, it was worth every penny.

The frame is very solidly built with very smooth and professional welding throughout. the wiring is all tucked away within the frame so it keeps the moisture out of the lines, and I love that it has a nice convenient little speedometer that tells you how fast you are going, and how much battery life you have at a glance. it really helps prevent getting stranded.

product_name: Sea Eagle 3 Person Inflatable Portable Sport Kayak Canoe w/Paddles
review_text:
writing titles is the hardest part of a review. Overall, this is great. It's so cheap that if something happened to it, I wouldn't be that upset about it, but it's tough enough that I don't expect to have any issues with it.

Comparing to sit-on-top tandem hard kayaks also sold on Amazon:
Sea Eagle 370 inflatable kayak is $250, 12.5' long, holds 650 pounds, weighs 32 pounds, has two skegs, can move a seat to the middle for one person, and comes with two paddles (about a $70 value).
Perception Rambler hard kayak is $700, 13.5' long, holds 550 pounds, weighs 78 pounds, doesn't have any skegs, the seats don't move, and doesn't come with paddles.
Ocean Kayak Malibu hard kayak is $663, 12' long, holds 375 pounds, weighs 57 pounds, doesn't have any skegs, the seats don't move, and doesn't come with paddles.
So looking at the basic metrics, this kayak is superior.

If you want to say that this kayak is not as tough as the hard kayaks, then you can look at Sea Eagle's whitewater kayaks. Remember, all professional whitewater tours use inflatable rafts, so just because it's inflatable doesn't mean it's not tough.
The Sea Eagle 380x inflatable kayak is $950, 12.5' long, holds 750 pounds, weighs 40 pounds, and comes with two paddles. So more expensive, but still much lighter and can hold more.

So let's review this Sea Eagle 370 kayak in depth.
1. Portability: Throwing this in the back of your vehicle is way easier than hoisting it on top. In addition, you don't have to have roof racks, either permanently installed or strapped pads. You don't have to worry about getting a hit on your MPG because it's on top, you don't have to worry about it getting stolen because you left it on top of your vehicle in the hotel parking lot, you don't have to worry about it not being strapped down properly and coming off, and you don't have to worry about damaging it pulling into a garage because you forgot it was up there. If you do want to inflate it at home and transport it on top, you can still transport it on top.
2. Inflating: Super quick and easy. You're talking about a couple of pounds of pressure, unlike your bicycle tires. The foot pump works great, and you can also get a pump that plugs into a wall outlet or your vehicle's 12V outlet. I'm not talking about a pump for your vehicle's tires; I'm talking about something that pumps up pool toys, with a pump hose about an inch wide or so.
3. Storage: Take a towel and wipe it down, deflate it, and put it in the provided storage bag. The bag is big enough so it's not difficult to use, and comes with a shoulder strap to carry it around. The kayak is bulky enough so it's not really easy to carry it around, but it's not a big deal.
4. Tracking: the longer the kayak, and if it has a skeg/fin underneath, the better it stays in a straight line. This 370 has two skegs, and tracks pretty well. The skegs are not removable (unlike Sea Eagle's Class IV kayaks). They seem pretty sturdy, however, so I wouldn't worry about them in whitewater. The instructions talk about how to heat them and bend them straight if they get bent. I was surprised how quick and straight this kayak was, maybe because my expectations were so low.
5. Seats. Yeah, I'm not crazy about the seats, which Sea Eagle calls "deluxe". I let out some of the air in the seats, and that seemed to help. If you want different seats, like the ones that hook onto D rings, there are no D rings on this kayak. Which also means that if you flip this kayak, there's a chance that the seats will come out. The back isn't very high, which means the back of my life jacket is always wanting to ride over the top of the seats.
6. Width. This is a thin kayak, 15" wide, with high sides. This is good for keeping water out and balance, but if you have a life jacket that has pads all the way around your waist, you may want to get a life jacket that just has the inflatable stuff in the front and back, as the sides of the kayak were pushing on the sides of my life jacket.
7. Foot wells. There are no foot wells, like with a hard kayak. I don't think that's an issue, as I'm used to getting all gnarly in a canoe, and that doesn't have foot wells. And whitewater rafts don't have foot wells. My hard kayak is short, and my knees get in the way of my paddle using the foot wells, so I don't think of this as a big loss.
8. Looks. I'm not crazy about how it looks, as it looks wimpier than it is. Maybe if it was another color or something. The rope dressings at the ends are nice for carrying it.
9. Length. It may be 12.5' long, but the interior is only 10'8" long. Two people are tight, especially if you're storing stuff. If I was ever going to upgrade to their Class IV kayaks, I'd get the 420x, which is 14' long.
10. Paddles. I think they work well. 3.0 pounds each, and lighter carbon fiber ones are 2.5 pounds. I've never used carbon fiber before.
11. Handles. Can use the ropes up front, but there are no handles on the side. Would have made carrying it easier. Meh.

I paid $285 in early August, and as of early September, it's gone down to $250, so I guess I should have waited for the season to end. Make sure you think you'll like it, because you can't return it, unless it's torn or something. The picture shows a yellow 8.3' kayak underneath it.

SIZING: Large worked the best for me, average size male, 190lbs, the Medium is too small and would probably work best for females.
SHAPE : Outdoor Master feels square, not rounded, inside and less ergonomic. It is not snug to my head shape.
K2 feels round inside and fits better for me. It's snug and stays put when shaken or bumped.
HARDWARE: Almost the same for both. It looks like it's designed and probably manufactured by the same factory. :)
Outdoor Master has a soft chin guard. It's not a big deal and not critical for me.
VENTILATION: Practically the same.
CONCLUSIONS: How it fits on you is more important than features. Because it's your safety. I recommend trying a few brands and models to find the one that fits you best. It's k2 in my case.

Current Reviews Fair and Accurate. [[VIDEOID:fe884e70f15564691a2d584d980dc285]] Reviews of the smell and taste after initially opening the bottle are correct. When I did that, I saw a lot of milkyish residue come out. And the weird taste and smell dramatically reduced. Hoping with prolong usage, that will no longer be an issue. There is no structure to the bottle (as it needs to collapse) so be careful when filling the bottle with water. Takes time to get used to drinking from it with the lack of bottle structure. Easy to collapse/bend with water in it as well. When this occurs, water does spill out. Do not try to change the shape of the bottle with the cap on. Will mis-shapen bottle. Collapsing and expanding bottle should be done with bottle cap open. I really appreciate that it’s light weight and ability to collapse and take up less space when needed. Fits in the bottle holder in my bag and comes with the clip that can be placed on my keychain or pant loop. I’m excited to use it for hiking and traveling.

10/2/22 Update: The company reached out and this is what they said. Hope that helps.

About Taste or Smell - Our water bottle is made of BPA FREE material, and passed certification of Food and Drug Administration in America. Please do not worry about its safety. If possible, please wash the bottle thoroughly with purified water. The water in the ordinary water pipe generally contains bleach substances or similar disinfection components, due to the particularity of the silica gel material, its molecular structure will adsorb some other substances in the water, which may appear as you see the white powder. The silicone material has very good stability, these white powders are not the material of the water bottle itself, you can rinse it directly, so please don't worry. Here are some advice to get rid of the silicone smell. Please add some dishwashing liquid or lemon slice in BOILED WATER, immerse the whole bottle and its cap in the water for 2 hours, then wash the bottle with clean water completely.

review_text:
Official Team Ball - My Go To Going Forward (Thanks Amazon). I travel moderately for work. While not as much as I used to, I am usually deployed to all the major metro areas several times a year. As a father, you try and get souvenirs for your kids and one of the things I started as a tradition was to get him MLB team logo baseballs. Baseballs are, easier to carry than an NBA basketball or NFL football. Plus, there are a ton more teams in the MLB.

One of the problems I've found is, that sometimes I'm rushed. I used to get these in major airports but I've found many airports lacking when it comes to souvenirs. review_text:
soak and/or cook by itself before adding to other food to get successful rehydration. Pointing out a few things brought up in reviews:

1. This is DEHYDRATED zucchini, NOT freeze-dried. Very different methods, different results, different pricing. While Mother Earth does carry some freeze dried, they do not have freeze dried zucchini. Another way to tell? With freeze dried foods, they can be eaten as is (crunchy snack) or rehydrated. Where as with dehydrated foods, most all (except fruits, usually) will need to be rehydrated in order to consume them (too tough to eat). This will require soaking and/or cooking for a period of time. Can't just toss it in the dish you are making and expect it to cook up quickly. So for this, it says to simmer 1 part zucchini to 2 parts water for 10-30 minutes. This very well may take longer. I let it cook for no less than 30 minutes before adding it to what I ultimately want to have it be part of. Another way to get it started is to let soak, then follow up with a shorter simmer.

2. 1/2 cup dried zucchini = 1 cup cooked zucchini. I made up 1/4 cup and it made a very good sized portion. See my pics.

3. End result is NOT EVER going to be same as fresh. Stop that. Then stop blaming the company/brand. YOu will always be disappointed. Best thing to get if you cant get fresh or frozen is to find a company who makes freeze dried. Even then, you are expecting a lot from zucchini. This is similar to others, and there aren't many out there to choose from.

4. Shelf life can be very very long, if not indefinite if stored under proper conditions. Freeze dried for sure, but dehydrated can last a very long time. Be sure to keep it in well sealed container, out of light and dampness. Maybe keep in freezer or further repackaged into mylar or vac sealed jar.

5. Taste is neutral. Kind of like how zucchini can be. I could tell it was zucchini though! I found that with proper rehydration it worked well in adding bulk to tacos, and can always be added to soup. I see it as a nutritional item rather than a way to have a plate of zucchini. Nice way to bulk up meals, add vitamins and minerals, yet not have to rely on fresh (for various reasons). I noticed that the skins were more like late summer yellow squash/zucchini. Kinda reminded me of regular squash- like butternut skins. Not tough but had more "presence" I shall say. DID not taste or feel like "tree bark" in any way.

6. If planning on using it in zucchini bread, muffins, cookies, or sauces, I would recommend running it through the blender after it has been rehydrated. Make it more of a puree. This will impart flavor and decrease any tougher bits.

7. Says processed and packaged in USA, but WHERE do they get their vegetables from?? That I havent seen, here or on their web page

8. If you dont like this packaging, they also offer mylar bag style.

OVERALL: I think it is fine, and it as expected. I love seeing it in my pantry knowing that I have a variety of dehydrated foods to use when I cant get fresh, or food is scarce, or food doesnt look good, or I cant afford it that day. Buy a little here and there and stock up those cupboards. Would like to know where the zucchini comes from?

PS. I miss when we could comment and ask questions of other reviewers. One person just said "poisonous". Like, what do they even mean by that? I had this a few times and doing well so far :)

Other than that, spend the money and get this chair if you're looking for a double camp chair. :)

review_text:
Good concept, doesn't feel very effective. I've been having a rough go of my chronic illnesses lately and have been looking for simple self care additions to incorporate into my regimen. My eyes have been struggling and uncomfortable lately, so these eye makes sounded promising. I'm not super fond of them thus far, however.

The packet features simple instructions and individually wrapped masks. It's easy enough to remove the lining and place the thin masks atop your lids. I've used them during my red light therapy sessions at home and the effect seems to be more of a calming ritual versus cooling.

If I press the mask to have better contact with my lids, I can feel a verrrrry subtle amount of cooling. The product against my skin sets off my sensory sensitivities, however, and makes me a smidge squirmy, so direct eyelid pressure is a no go for me.

I have sensitive and reactive skin and I've placed a patch on my forehead after my eyelid time was up to see how it feels....and the patch did cause a slight itching sensation.

I'm bummed that this product doesn't cool very much, and that it might not work for my skin. I plan to wait a few days and try another. I'll update this review if needed!

review_text:
I like it, but it spits at me!. I really like this because it's not easy to get a 32 oz bottle that fits in a cup holder. I like that there is a hook, that is also like a clip so I can clip it to a bag if necessary. I also really like that there is a lid for the the mouthpiece to keep it protected. It's cute, easy to carry, but when left in the car, it spits at me when I re-open it! A couple of other people have mentioned it on reviews as well. It's not worth me returning for that reason alone, but I would probably look elsewhere next time since there are so many other options.
Update - I've now had this a couple of months and traveled with it on an airplane. My old water bottles would occasionally "spit" from the pressure change on the plane, so I was fully ready (with my sleeve over the spout) to catch the water from this bottle. Oh, wow...it was like Niagara Falls! The funniest part was that the water ended up in my lap, so it looked like I just didn't make it to the rest room in time. I thought it was hilarious, but I can see how some would not. On the flight back, I just unscrewed the lid a tiny bit to release the pressure and no issues. The hook came in super handy when I wanted to clip it to the outside of my backpack.
The real reason I am updating my review is because it was hard to drink out of the straw due to the suction. As dumb as this sounds, I found myself drinking water less because of this issue. I went back and read some additional reviews and a couple people mentioned removing the little piece in the cap that effects the airflow. Eureka! It now works perfectly! I'll be using this bottle more often now.

review_text:
Makes quick work of filling a bicycle tire - short hose though. I really like this pump - I have an electric tire pump that worked well for bicycles, but it gets its electricity from a 12v cigarette lighter in my car and with our current electric car it's a bit of a hassle to use (gotta have the EV running before you can use the 12v outlet) so I was looking for a manual pump for convenience. This one does the trick.

The pump is very easy to use and tops up my bicycle tire with just a few pumps. However, I have large tire rims (28") and the pump's hose is too short to reach the valve when it's at the top of the wheel, so you have to rotate the wheel further down to pump it. The hose is also fairly inflexible, so getting it locked on the valve is harder than it could be with a more flexible (and longer) hose. Subtracting one star for these two hose shortcomings.

review_text:
They work!. I struggle with my hands constantly being uncomfortably cold, and have recently gone back to working in the office so temp is more of an issue when I can't control the thermostat and where space heaters are subject to discovery by the fire marshal. I've had other hand warmers in the past and they really do make a difference. It was time to replace the previous ones and these ones had great reviews PLUS they were on the early Prime Day sale, so I decided to spring for three sets - two for myself and one for my dad who has worse circulation but is retired and doesn't need to go into an office.

My previous hand warmers were a different shape (a flattened capsule shape) and I wasn't sure whether the cylinder shape would be an improvement or a downgrade. The cylinder handwarmers arrived and I realized that my coworkers (they're jokesters!) might come up with some obnoxious cracks because of the shape but so far that hasn't happened. In day-to-day use, the cylinder shape is much better than the flat shape. It is easy to grip, keeps palm and fingers warm at the same time, and I don't need to rotate it in my hand to get to "the warm side" which was a drawback of the flat type.

In terms of heat, there are two settings - the low setting seems fairly hot by itself and works well when my hand is SO cold that the high setting would be too much (the low setting is great for my mouse-using hand). The high setting is hotter (obviously) and is good when my hand is only a normal level of cold (the non-mouse hand). It isn't so hot that it seems to pose a burn hazard (at least for adult skin) but it is probably at the upper end of the safe temp range, which I love.

They charge in a reasonable amount of time, so that is good. I haven't really kept track of how long they provide heat, but one pair will get me through the workday no problem. If I forget to take them home and recharge, they will help me for much of the second workday too. One reviewer pointed out that the large power button on the end is easily pressed inadvertently and that is true. I keep them in their little carry bags (provided) to try to reduce the risk of that happening.

They seem like they will do well in coat pockets, but it isn't really coat weather yet where I live, so I haven't done that. I can't imagine that there would be any issue with that.

I did get a postcard asking me to review the product in exchange for more hand warmers, but the content of my review is honest...it is a great product and I would LOVE to get more of these - this cold hand issue runs in my family and this will certainly be a much-appreciated gift.

Bottom line - I absolutely recommend these!

product_name: TITLEIST Tour Speed Golf Ball
review_text:
This ball is underrated, kind of a sleeper. I really like this ball, but it's not very popular, it seems. The thermoplastic urethane cover definitely has a firmer feel and sound than a cast urethane ball, but I have no trouble finding these used for $1.50/ball and since I lose a few every round, that matters to me.

I like the compression at 80 since my driver clubhead speed is about 90mph, so balls like the Pro VI aren't quite as suited to my medium swing speed. PLUS, the Pro VI spins quite a bit off the clubs since lots of people who play that ball like to "work" the ball (cut and draw)...I don't do that yet. I need a ball that maximizes distance and has minimal sidespin off the driver and other clubs. Finding fairways and maximizing distance is what this ball excels at. It doesn't sound as good or feel as good as a cast urethane ball, but the performance is suited for the golfer who knows what their game needs. I need all the help I can get to stay straight.

You also lose about 10% of wedge/short club spin (according to data from multiple reviews), but I don't need the ball to rip back off my wedges on approach shots. These balls feel pretty soft off my short clubs and check up nicely on greens. They also feel a little firm off the putter, but again, that's just preference and prejudice. A cast urethane ball feels better off the putter face, but that doesn't mean it's performing better. These perform really well without being jumpy off the putter. They sound firm off the putter face, but again, that's not performance, that's perception.

MANY people play Pro VIs really should be playing this ball instead. It's cheaper and performs much better for the average golfer (I shoot in the high 80s), so even though this ball is overlooked by a lot of people, it really should get more love than it does.

review_text:
Perfect holiday gift!. Beautiful packaging! Excellent for a gift, much better than the standard packaging of most hand warmers (I have four)

The hand warmer itself has an elegant design, with covered ports, a stylized drawing, and golden touches that contrast with the blue/grey color of the warmer.

As pretty as the hand warmer is, it is thicker and shorter than most other hand warmers (see photo for comparison) and even a hand as large as mine can only cover one of the sides of the warmer, with the fingertips holding the other side.

A window shows the percentage of charge left in the battery. That is unusual in a positive sense; most hand warmers have three leds to show the charge left, as well as the intensity of the heat setting (only listed in celsius/centigrades).

Three heat settings: 98 F (normal body temperature), 113 F, 125 F (the highest setting feels very warm, almost uncomfortably hot).

Even though the manufacturer promises 5 hours at the highest heat setting, my unit kept working for over 10 hours--very warm all the time!

Time to charge from 0 to 100% through micro USB (only input): about 5 hours

Because of functionality (easy to use power and heat buttons, heat display, power display) and aesthetics, this is the hand warmer I like the most out of the four I own.

This hand warmer would make a very nice holiday gift!

product_category: Tools & Home Improvement | Sports Water Bottles
review_text:
The perfect water bottle?. This water bottle is very well designed. The bottle is triple insulated so it is very thick (the sidewalls in the main part of the bottle are at least 1/2 inch thick if not thicker, this also makes it a bit heavier than most bottles. Given the sidewall thickness, they made the bottle taller so it is still easy to hold.

The bottle has a coating on it that is easy to grip and feels like it will hold up over time. It is also the subject of my only complaint with the water bottle. At least on the black model, sometimes greasy finger print marks show up on it. I don't detract a star for this because the rest of the bottle makes up for this.

The bottle has a grippy bottom so it won't slide of a surface and is quiet setting it down. The lid has a large drinking spout and a tiny air hole so that you water flows freely. This is probably my favorite design of the bottle and makes it very easy to drink quickly and easily from the bottle.

I put the insulation to the test and put ice water in the bottle and was able to confirm that the ice last over 24 hours in the bottle. I have not tried using it for anything hot, but I can say this is large enough to hold a whole bottle of wine!

The top fits securely, and I love the one-handed release button to access the straw, since it means I don't have to touch the straw in order to drink.

The sleeve and shoulder strap are nice and it's great to be able to have my hands free while I walk. I wear it cross-body and am easily able to lift the bottle to drink without having to remove the strap. I did end up having to use a big safety pin to secure the padded piece of the shoulder strap in place, because every time I lifted the bottle to take a drink, it would slip back behind me and I'd have to turn into a contortionist to get it back in the right position.

Although my phone (a Galaxy Note 20 Ultra in a bulky case) does fit in the phone pocket, it's a very tight fit and due to the curve of the pocket over the water bottle, I am not comfortable with the amount of pressure exerted against the phone, so I do not use that pocket for my phone. Instead, it carries hand sanitizer, chap stick, and poop bags for my dogs.

All in all, it's a great thing to have when walking/hiking, and my walking buddy liked it so much I ordered her one too, and she loves it.

review_text:
I use this to help make my horse's fly spray!. If you ride horses you probably have flies and buy fly spray. It's expensive and filled with chemicals.

I looked around for a homemade homeopathic spray and found this one.

I use this rosemary essential oil as one of the ingredients in my horse's fly spray. It works great, but note that it is not long-lasting. I also put fly boots on my horse which helps to significantly reduce stomping.

Here's the recipe:
• large spray bottle
• Two Cups *each* of water and apple cider vinegar
• Two T olive oil
• squirt of dish soap
• any three essential oils (but not citrus), 8 to 10 drops each
Mix well and spray. Be sure to shake before each use. Keeps well at the stable.

Commercial fly sprays can cost between low $20s to low $30s. I figure this homeopathic spray costs less than $1.50 per bottle.

review_text:
Nice Water Bottle/Thermos!. This water bottle is pretty nice!

Things that are nice about it:
- It's stainless steel! We have been trying to switch our plastic water bottles over to stainless steel.
- It holds 32 oz, which is a great size in my opinion.
- The top is secure and airtight.
- The top flap positively holds itself away from your face when you take a drink.
- The handle moves 90 degrees from flat to upright; making a good handle to open the thermos.
- The outside of the thermos has 2 flat surfaces at 180 degrees to each other for a positive grip. The coating feels a tiny bit rubbery and allows you to keep hold of the thermos.
- My husband made some hot cocoa in it for deer hunting and said it worked really well for keeping things hot even while being outside in cold weather. He said he warmed up the thermos with almost boiling water, then dumped that out and put in about 20 oz of very hot chocolate. After being outside at about 37 degrees for 1 hour, he poured out 5 oz into a mug and it was too hot to drink. He did so 2 more times at one hour intervals and it was still too hot to drink until sitting out for a little while to cool. Finally, after 4 hours, it was just barely cool enough to drink out of the container.

So, it functions as advertised and I have no complaints. I would recommend it.

One day in the Navy, I was ordered out of the pool to be fitted for a wetsuit. So I'm dripping wet in UDT shorts (like Navy Speedos) and two clowns that outranked me are taking measurements and the second clown is writing it down in a book. Clown One reads the tape of my head and the Clown Two lights up and says "Congratulations Zero-five, you've won the prize for the biggest melon!"

I didn't care that they'd dispensed with such trivial stuff as all my hair or my Christian name. They could have at least bothered to learn I was Petty Officer Zero-Five. I have feelings.

Being a young man, I failed to grasp the truth of the situation which was that I was the Super-Orc on deck being fitted for his armor by two dispensible Orcs, even from the Navy's point of view mission-wise. And instead of my feelings being hurt, which they were, they were lucky I didn't unlock the jaws of my award-winning cranium and bite their heads off. But I wanted that wetsuit, so I just cried myself to sleep that night on my enormous pillow.

I didn't tell Orc 1 he had a pear-shaped ass and could he even swim and did the rejection of pretty girls ever get to him?. Or that Orc 2 looked like he had never done 50 good push-ups in a day much less, a single set. But they can crack wise about my head, and I have to show nothing because of my rank. I'll never forget I was Petty Officer of the Watch when my friend, Petty Officer Courtemanche saluted me and requested permission to go ashore. It was his last day and he was out of the Navy and he tells me how sick he is of having to salute first and call lesser men, "Sir." Reluctantly, I returned his salute and granted him permission to go ashore for good.

product_name: Vivicreate Camping 20000 BTU 2 burner stainless steel panel auto ignition Propane Gas Outdoor Garden Fishing Hiking Camp Restaurant Stove Burner
review_text:
Not recommended for the USA Market. I really wanted to like this product. UNFORTUNATELY, that is not the case. The main problem is that the supplied regulator that connects to the LP gas tank has a POL style connection. POL valves haven’t been used in the USA for many years and small LP tanks (think standard 20 lb gas grill tank) used in the USA these days have an OPD valve/connection. Bottom line is this stove will not connect to the 20-pound LP tanks generally available in the USA (things may be different in other countries). So, for that reason, this item gets only 1-star.

Even if you have a way to connect it to a gas source it has a protective film covering the polished metal, presumably to prevent scratches prior to installation. That would be a feature EXCEPT that the film was applied during manufacturing prior to final assembly and therefore parts of the film are covered by parts of the stove. Since the film must be removed prior to use, you must disassemble the stove, remove the film, and then reassemble – doable but annoying, and many of the metal edges are sharp enough to cut you unless you are very careful.

Since I happen to have access to a gas tank with a POL valve and wanted to test the stove, I removed the film, reassembled the stove, and fired it up. What I can say that is favorable is that the stove lit and produced a nice flame. But unless you have a way to supply gas to the stove, I do not recommend this product. That said, I’d like to see the manufacturer offer this product with a regulator that is compatible with LP tanks in the USA and apply the protective film so that removing it doesn’t require disassembling the stove. If they do that, I'd give that revised version of this product 5-stars.

Not perfect, but works moderately well for my injured finger. I have no idea what this should cost, so I can't speak to whether it's overpriced, and I got mine in exchange for a review. That said, $17 feels expensive for what this is.

It's nice to play with, and it softens as you use it. I found it moderately but not immensely helpful with an injured finger and hand.

In spite of claims that it's non-oily, you can see that it arrived at least a little oily. After a couple uses it all worked either into the putty or out onto my hands, so I don't have any issues with oiliness now.

Because I needed to work one finger and part of my hand, I pulled off smaller chunks to work with and would put them back with the main putty once I finished. It pulls apart with a satisfying snap, and it works back together into the main glob without too much fuss.

I got this for an injury, but it has also helped with hand and wrist cramps, and it's a pretty enjoyable fidget toy.

Overall I'm satisfied with this product, even if I had to work out the oil and I feel like this has to be a little overpriced.

product_name: Inviguri Roller Yoga Wheel for Back & Neck Pain, with Spinal Groove. Medium to Deep Pressure for Heavy Duty Foam Rolling. Made from Natural Cork.
review_text:
Even works well for taller/bigger individuals. Back in summer 2019 a number of bad choices and some poor lifting habits (not fitness lifting, but rather large dogs and landscaping) led to a case of two bulging discs in my lower back, and a serious case of sciatic nerve pain and physical therapy (PT). A few of the key exercises I did at those PT appointments involved versions of rings like these, but due to their composition and size (much too small for my 6'4" and 300-something lb frame) they weren't really ideal for me as they either had too much give or were very narrow and hard to keep running straight back and forth. So I'd do a few reps and then need to reset the ring to keep it in that sweet spot to help with the sciatic pain relief exercises.

And while the most severe pain did eventually subside, every now and then (usually after some rough housing with the aforementioned large dogs or moving a large piece of furniture) I'll feel a twinge of pain as the sciatic nerve gets irritated and wish I had one of these available. And now I do, and not only that, but these Inviguri rollers are slightly wider than what I had available at my PT appointments, so now when I do these exercises at home I find that I'm able to stay on track with less deviation on the part of the rollers than what I experienced at my physical therapist's office.

The cork is quite strong and the diameter is just right for someone my size to make it easy to get just the right angle for relief. Before I was just using some of the basic PT stretches and yoga poses when I'd get a sciatic nerve pain flair up, but these have really changed that for me.

The cork texture doesn't bother me, and I actually prefer it to some of the dense but cheap foam alternatives I've tried. For me, cork is definitely working better and when I'm using these I never feel like there's unnecessary give occurring in the roller that's reducing how effective the exercises are. Hopefully the cork composition means these will maintain their shape longer, but if not I'll update my review to reflect that.

product_name: Inviguri Roller Yoga Wheel for Back & Neck Pain, with Spinal Groove. Medium to Deep Pressure for Heavy Duty Foam Rolling. Made from Natural Cork.
review_text:
Love These Inviguri Rollers!. The design of these rollers make so much sense to me. This is an Australian company, and a physical therapist developed these tools. The indentation for the spinal cord really does make a very big difference. It allows the spine to set comfortably in the groove as you roll back and forth, while the wheel is able to massage deeper into your muscles. I was skeptical, however, that I would be able to use the large wheel comfortably because I'm not as strong or agile as I used to be (I'm 74). I didn't think I'd be able to maintain the proper form. That wasn't the case. It's a good fit, but if you care to, the smaller roller can be used as a beginner prop or if you are of smaller stature. It will be a little uncomfortable, as would a deep tissue massage. The result when you are done is a real reduction in that achy back. I used it today after too much bending and lifting, and it felt great. Very stable, rolls easily. no wobble.

The smaller wheel is great for the neck. I have some arthritis in my cervical spine, and placing my neck correctly with the spine in the groove and rolling my head back and forth is like a massage for the neck. Very nice. Actually, just lying back on it for a few minutes is relaxing and gives your muscles a sense of release.

The ball is a nice touch, but it does much the same thing a tennis ball does under the ball of your foot. It's a great foot massage in any case.

I received a card with the rollers that directs you to the company's website, which is Inviguri.com. There you can get a lot more information about how to use these rollers, including a link to a video demo. It is helpful to watch someone using these props, and it might help you to see how they work. It helped me.

As another reviewer mentioned, this is much more stable than the thin cork rollers. It feels sturdy, but the design still gives just a little. My experience with cork is that it lasts quite a while, but if that is not the case, I'll come back and adjust the review.

Five stars.

Decent bar for the - Brass bushings would have been better.. This bar is nice around the 100 - 150.00 price point. For 200 +Rogue bars look more attractive.

Pros
Has center knurl for squatting
Mild knurl - with surprisingly good grip - can do power lifting without tearing up hands
Black oxide finish also helps with bar grip with some rust resistance
The metal in bar seems like quality steel.
Snap ring vs bolt for holding end caps is a plus
28.5 mm is good diameter for dead lifting.

Cons
Finish on the bar ends is cheap chrome - it can flake off loading / unloading standard plates.
Ribbed bar ends - I prefer smooth bar ends - personal preference.
Bushing material = steel. ( durable material, but needs more maintenance and oil to keep bar ends spinning -smoothe if didn't oil for extended period of time, corrosion would reduce spin of bar ends - Most premium barbells use brass for bushings ).

Really liked this bar for deed lifting,. Even though I sold mine for Texas Power bar which has a slightly more aggressive knurl.

review_text: A wonderful curling iron that heats up quickly!. I have strange hair. It is very straight, fine but I have tons of it! The barrel is smooth and doesn't snag your hair and does a great job of getting a curl the first time. I really like the temperature adjustment wheel, instead of up and down buttons and the temperature lock so you don't accidentally turn it up or down when using it. The power button works much the same way, and on the side (YAY) so I don't turn it off with when using it, a problem I have had with others in the past that have the power button just at the end of the barrel and arm. It heats super fast from off to 300 degrees is just under a minute. a huge improvement over my old one. This is a keeper!

review_text:
Good quality goggles, comfortable and clear. I'll say upfront that I am NOT a skier or snowboarder. I got these to wear while snowblowing, walking, or working outside in cold weather, because the wrap-around sunglasses I have been using in the past finally wore me out with their fogging up. So, I'm not in the target demographic group; but should still be using them in ways they should be right for.

APPEARANCE: These look good (although that isn't a big deal for me). I imagine they will fit right into the typical ski outfit.

FIT: It took a little experimenting to get the fit 'just right'. There are two slide buckles on the strap, and you have to adjust them each in turn, because the inside of the strap has a band of rubber (not a "rubber band"!) that holds the strap in place where you put the sliders. That is, I can't imagine the sliders will slide on their own - ever. So, once you put in the couple minutes to adjust them to your head, you shouldn't have to do that again.

COMFORT: Very comfortable. The foam inner rim is soft, and fits close to the skin (except a bit of a gap at the sides; but that isn't big enough to be a negative for me). And, the foam turns out to be nice and warm. (I haven't worn them in frigid weather, like near zero degrees, yet; but from my experience so far, I'm not expecting a problem then.)

VISION: Clear to the point of almost not being aware one is looking through something.... I am trusting the claim that they block UV rays - but they do it without clouding or darkening the field of view noticeably. I would be comfortable wearing these while driving, although I haven't done so yet.

DURABILITY: Haven't had them long enough to speak to this. They do seem solidly built, and I'd be surprised if they break due to being dropped or tossed (ever). The "lens" feels very substantial; it's slightly flexible, so I would expect it to resist 'popping out' due to minor impacts. The one concern I have is that the inner foam rim is soft enough that I could envision it possibly compressing over time due to sufficient wear, and perhaps to sweat affecting the foam. Time will tell on that.

OVERALL: A solid five-star product.

Final note - GLASSES? I wear glasses, and was hoping I could wear them under these goggles. The first time I put the goggles on, I thought I was going to be disappointed, as the inside foam rim caught on the sidepieces of my glasses. BUT - good news! - with a moment of playing with them, I figured out how to put the goggles on without catching on my glasses. It's a snug fit - but that has the added benefit that I shouldn't have to worry about my glasses sliding down on my nose as I work. Nice!

review_text: I am a Letter Carrier for the Post Office and I work in all kinds of weather.... I am a Letter Carrier for the Postal Service and I wanted full sun protection because skin cancer runs in my family.  This works great for shading my face and neck, both front and back.  I am female and the tension strap around the cap part works great for getting it snug so I don't have to use the chin strap in most light to moderate breezy conditions.  It works with my prescription sunglasses too, so that means it's snug, but not all the way down to my eyebrows.  It's been raining a lot here in Northern Ca.  I've had light rain, moderate rain, moderate rain and wind and today, absolutely pouring down rain, wind and hail.  This hat with a thin beanie beneath kept me dry in the light to moderate rain for a full day.  But the hard driving rain and wind day, it was soaked through, and my beanie was drenched too--had to wring it out.  So while this had covers a large range of weather conditions, it does have it's limitations.  And the beanie helps with any water splashing through the vents.  Also, the tension strap around the brow works great.  Even in strong winds with gusts above 40 mph, I did not have to use the chinstrap, which was great and kept the brim full and standing up.  It 100% blocks the rain from getting on my glasses so I can still see to work.  The only downside, and honestly, it's not the hat's fault was that the heavy rain day, the water was running off the brim and dumping straight onto the mail I was delivering as I was looking down.  Again, not much can be done about that, but I did feel bad it was getting people's mail more wet, rather than protecting it.  But for the money, this hat is a keeper!

review_text:
Warms Nicely But Some Improvements Would be Nice. These have been fine. They definitely warm up nicely and are much better than no gloves.

PROS
- Quick warm up: These gloves warm up fairly quickly. The heat is stronger on the palm, rather than the fingers but there is warmth everywhere overall.
- Easy use: The zippers allow easy access to the batteries. They easily come out/in the gloves but I usually charge the batteries while they remain in the gloves. The buttons on each glove are easy to change strength (single press) and turn on/off (long press).
- Reusable battery: This is great so that you don't have to be buy new batteries every time. This is a big deal.
- Carrying bag: Nice convenient place to keep the gloves.

CONS
- Finger touch screen: The ability to use phones through the gloves works fairly well but the placement is not convenient for me. My hand fits snuggly on my hand so the fit is good but I sometimes need to press at awkward angles.
- Low warming on fingers: It will warm up some but the fingers feel cold when compared to the palms.

These are very nice overall. Some things could be better but I still use them most days when it's cold. I wouldn't use them to throw snow but they make the day better.

review_text:
Updated 1/27/2023: Do not buy, not worth the risk. Updated 1/27/2023: I gave this stem another chance and the disappointment was doubled with a second one (was hoping to stock a couple different sizes). The second stem had the same fitment and scratching problems as the first stem. The nice matte finish was starting to flake off after the first ride. Some creaking when tightening despite not surpassing 4-5 nm. Out of fear of damaging my not cheap carbon fork and the potential of needing extensive dental work, I got rid of both stems. If you value your bike and pretty face, stay far away from cheap carbon stems.

I got this to match my rxl seatpost which has the same excellent color/finish (the matte UD carbon with tiny Italian stripe), but the stem isn't quite as well made as their other parts. The most obvious concern, when first installing it, was the abysmal tolerance and unevenness in where it mounts to the fork tube. It scratched the finish on the steerer tube a bit, but I stopped installing it before it became real damage. I was successful in smoothing out the mounting area with some 320 grit sandpaper, and it finally slid right in with very little resistance as it was supposed to. Stem stays put if torqued correctly. Other than the above discrepancy, the finish on the faceplate could use a lot more attention, but isn't immediately obvious unless you really stare at it. Weight is fine, about on par with a good alloy stem. Hardware is fine for such a low torque part, but probably won't resist corrosion for a long time. Overall it's a keeper for now, but it's definitely not the best value for the price. QC should have been a lot better.

review_text:
Portable, rechargeable slippers. My icy feet can finally endure winter in comfort.. These heated slippers are so great! They are wonderful to settle back & relax in the warmth they provide

But that's also where one of their drawbacks becomes apparent. When my slippers arrived I made sure to fully charge their battery packs & then settled down to enjoy their heat. Turning on the TV, I tilted back in my recliner to enjoy the evening. Now, I don't know about you, but when I lie back in the recliner I often cross my legs at the ankles. Doing that, the on/off button that is normally on the outside of each foot ends up pressed against the other slipper's on/off button. And yes, I didn't even notice it until I felt like my toasty toes weren't being toasted so much anymore. The slight shifting I'd done in my chair had turned my 'high' setting down to 'medium' on one foot & to 'low' on the other. It's a minor thing, but I wish there was some way to set the on/off button switch so it can't accidentally be changed by such a minor bumping.

My other minor quibble is with the relative 'run' time of the batteries. I like toasty feet and at the highest heat setting the instructions say I shouldn't really expect more than 2-2½ hours of use. If I'm in front of the TV for a marathon binge I can certainly spend more than 2½ hours in one evening.

Now, with that info, I explored Amazon to see if there were any questions about ordering replacement or supplemental battery packs. No questions, but a search for 'Kamlif battery' brought up just the 2-pack spare batteries that I was hoping for. As I write this they sell for $26.99. I ordered a set just so I can relax knowing that if/when one set runs down, I can replace them immediately with the back-up set.

With those slight drawbacks known, I can wholeheartedly recommend these slippers if you suffer from chronic cold feet.

review_text:
CoC or Grip Genie. I bought an 80lb and a 100lb CoC gripper to work on my hands, forearms and biceps from home since I don't have room for much else. That and I don't live near any gyms.
These work great and if you use the religiously, you'll see results pretty quickly.
When I first started I could only probably close the 100lb consecutively 10 times with my right hand and maybe 5 with my left so I had to work with the 80lb for awhile.
Once I got to the point that I could close the 80lb about 60 times consecutively with my right hand, I went back to the 100lb one.
Grip Genie had black Friday deals going on so I bought their 150, 200, and 250lb grippers.
I can now close the 150lb with right hand about 10-20 times consecutively as well as the same for my left hand.
I can also close the 100lb 40 times with my right hand and 20-30 times with my left hand.
The key differences between CoC and Grip Genie is that CoC has a silver coil, silver grips and the grips are a tad smoother.
Grip Genie has a black coil, the grips are color coded based on what weight they are and the grips are rougher.
I prefer Grip Genie since the rougher grip doesn't slip in my hand as well as them being color coded helps with quick identification.
CoC is still great though, so they get a 5 star review.

A small tip when it comes to grippers would be to always have the next weight up with you while working out.
Start with the heavier weight and do as much as you can, even if you can't close it all the way.
You'll be able to do a lot more closes when you go back to the lower weight one that you would if you didn't start with the heavy one.

Also my forearms have gotten wider than my biceps lol.

review_text:
Great on Cold Winter Nights, but Batteries Stopped Working.. For someone with cold feet the whole winter these slippers are great! They are very cushiony and comfortable with bottoms that grip. The outside is slightly stretchy fabric, and the insides are a soft fleece like fabric. The batteries for the slippers are rechargeable and they zip into a pocket on the top of the slipper.

There are 3 different setting of heat and each one is shown in a different color in the square on the side of the slipper. Pressing the square will change the setting from high to medium to low. It is very easy. These are perfect for anyone that sits a lot to keep feet warm, but they are comfortable enough to wear for long periods of time.

My only slight criticism is that I have small feet and wear a size 5 and these slippers in size small are for women sizes 5-81/2. There is a big difference between a size 5 and a size 8. There is a couple of extra inches left when I put them on, but I wear them most of the time while sitting so that isn’t a problem, I just want to point that out to others with small feet. Don’t be dissuaded these are great!

Update: After one charging of the batteries, both included batteries would no longer charge. Shoes are still useable, but they can no longer be heated due to the battery issue.

product_name: Scooter for Kids 3 Wheels Scooter Kids Scooter 4 Adjustable Height Lean to Steer Extra-Wide Deck Kids Scooter with LED Light Up Wheels for Toddlers Girls & Boys from 3 to 12 Year-OldLearn to Steer
review_text:
Decent scooter for little ones. Overall, not a bad little scooter for little ones, probably 4 to 7 years old or so.

Some things to like:
- adjustable handle so you can set it to the proper height for the child.
- NOT powered- I think to put very small children on something that is motorized is reckless- they are simply not old enough to handle it- with something like this they learn steering and movement totally within their control.
- The wheels light up when moving, which I am sure kids will like, although hopefully they remember to look up and where they are going instead of at the wheels. But it is still cool.
- I got the pink for a girl, and I am sure she will like it.
- Wheels seem pretty fluid.

It has a rear brake that is activated by applying your foot to the pedal on the rear wheel. Pretty standard, I guess, but I would have preferred a hand brake. Just seems that little ones may have a hard time maintaining full balance when doing so.

The steering mechanism is done by leaning right or left. That is good, but I wonder on longevity.

Overall, a good first scooter, the positives outweigh the negatives, although it may depend on price. As I write this, this scooter is priced at the upper range of similar scooters. I will try to update my review based on longevity and ruggedness as it is used throughout the year.

Durable, spacious, versatile Pickleball bag. First of all, the quality is very good. The material is a tough nylon "Twill Weave Fabric" that should hold up to rough handling. The zippers are of high quality with durable materials and pull clips. The stitching is very good with thick thread and well placed so I do not think this will pose a problem like in some cheaper bags. The handles are comfortable and well built both on top and for duffle use.

The bag can conveniently be used as a backpack or duffle. As a backpack, you have padded straps with a chest strap but there is no waist strap so the weight is all on your shoulders. Unless you plan on walking long distances, this is really not an issue. When using as a duffle, you can hide the straps in a sleeve on the back so they are not hanging loosely. The attachments for the shoulder strap are well built and should last the life of the bag.

There are numerous compartments, 2 specifically for paddles on the side. The 2 water bottle compartments are a bit small and will only holding narrow 12 to 16 ounce bottles. There is a nice collapsible shoe compartment that expands into the main compartment. It is made of what appears to be a waterproof or resistant material which is nice to place your shoes without messing up the rest of your gear. The main compartment is very spacious and good for placing balls, gloves, clothing and even more paddles if needed. There are a few other interesting compartments that could be used for other items but they probably are more than you need for a pickleball outing.

Overall, this is a very nice bag with the convenience of carrying as a duffle or backpack. It should last many years and be more than adequate carrying the typical pickleball player's gear.

product_category: Cell Phones & Accessories | Activity & Fitness Trackers
review_text:
For the price, surprisingly pleased.. This replaces the non-display Halo band. I was using a Casio digital watch and didn't want to look like a complete dork wearing two watches. I lost the Casio when I removed it to reset for standard time change. I figured I'd give this a try since it cost only slightly more than the Casio replacement would have.

I actually preferred the Halo when the subscription ran out. I didn't use the recipes or health hints and giving points for exercise and sleep was less useful than steps or time. These were reintroduced shortly before I lost my watch and I didn't consider it an improvement. Glad to see that there are no optional, for money add-ons on the Amazfit.

Looks like I can comfortably get about three or four days out of the Amazfit although I normally charge every other day. It charges quickly. I'm a light user, basically using it to count sleep and steps as well as using as a watch. Time steps and weather show up on the face of the band. Sleep is listed on app. I seldom change screens and have the simple basic, dark screen to save battery life. I have a separate app that I input steps and exercise converted to calories. I count steps and exercise from research on a university exercise site. This subtracts from a manual calorie counting app. I try to limit myself to 1800 calories a day.

The Amazfit counts fewer calories than my computed figures, the Halo counted many more. I suspect the Halo was computing calories burned from simply being alive as opposed to exercise calories. The sleep counter shows that I'm averaging approximately 8 hours sleep, the Halo showed 7. The Halo was more accurate at measuring actual sleep as opposed to simply being still and horizontal. Trips to the bathroom that showed up as fifteen minutes in Halo show up as only a couple of minutes in Amazfit. No big problem.

The Amazfit is a more accurate pedometer than the Halo which undercounted steps.

On balance I'm very pleased with the Amazfit. I think it's a better buy than the Halo. The range of functions is larger, although I'm not using most of them. Kind of hard to judge a display device with one that's simply a band. I think the Halo looks a bit more expensive than the Amazfit, which is fine because it is. If the Amazfit holds up, I'm happy with it.

product_name: Petzl, Swift RL Rechargeable Headlamp with 900 Lumens & Automatic Brightness Adjustment, Orange
review_text:
Bright as Day. Secure.. I wear it on night runs. I get asked all the time what kind of light it is during group runs in the dark because it is so bright and lights the entire road/trail ahead.

The lowest setting is not bright enough for fast runs in pitch black, but is OK for jogging. I use the middle light most of the time for faster runs and rough terrain, and the highest setting in pitch black and off road terrain. Most of my runs are less than 2 hours, so the battery last longer than I needed even swapping between the middle and high beam. Lots of fun to run in the dark with this light.

PROS:
• Ultra bright when needed, quick taps between 3 levels
• Fits secure on head, love the strap mechanics
• Works ok over a running/baseball hat
• Works great with winter hat
• Can swamp in a new battery if needed, but a bit tricky to do WHILE running
• Nice tilting action to cast light close to feet or flood further out
• Great coverage and beam of light

CONS:
• Difficult to get between the different modes where it does/does not auto dim
• Starts to hurt forehead after an hour of what (maybe I can loosen it a bit)
• A bit annoying sometimes when the light dims due to running past a reflective road sign
• Tuning if off requires pressing the light through all 3 cycles - really wish long-press turned it off

review_text:
Plasticky but Nice. I’m sad this wasn’t a good fit for me. I guess I just assumed the PolyTac would feel more substantial than it does. Maybe it’s just the yellow, but I thought it would be better looking in terms of obvious quality when looking at in person, but sadly this is not the case. I like the throw of the light, but I am not a fan of the flood so much.

I also don’t like how the light is framed when I’m using it at night, it’s an off putting distraction that fails to provide a clean view of the areas where I’m shining the light —so it also means the view in the dark is very narrow.

I justified this purchase as necessary to look out for coyote eyes when I’ve got my pooch outside, which it seems like it can still do, just as long as they’re not lurking near the periphery of where I’m pointing this flashlight —since I’d never spot it in the dark band that surrounds the bright middle light —or in his “frame” just outlines the thick dark ring separating it’s outer thin ring from the bright inner light if that makes any sense. If it doesn’t now, it will when your light arrives if you got the same model as me.

I absolutely hate the gummy button as it makes it hard to hurry up and snap the light on —or to turn on the light with one hand. Not a total deal breaker, but added to my issues with the edge circles it is reason enough for me to stay on my continued search for a solid edc I can count on in any situation —instead of just scenarios where I will only need a partial view of what’s going on, as well as more time to fiddle with a power button, while I also have zero free hands.

review_text:
pantry staple emergency or not. Some Augason Farms stuff I buy as emergency food, some I buy for regular use. If I can price out something in this form that is same price or less than other forms, then I go with this as it can be stored away or kept in my working pantry. I use a lot of Augason Farms, and I've been pleased with this.

Dehydrated celery is a great addition to the pantry. Sometimes I dont have fresh, or I have fresh that went bad, or I dont find it in the store, or what is there looks bad, or price is way outside my budget. Having some dried celery tucked away in my pantry really helps stretch the budget and brings value to my time.

I keep the recipe trifecta on hand, "mire poix": celery, carrot, and onion. I keep fresh, frozen, and dried on hand. Usually used in recipes that will help rehydrate these foods no problem. Celery is very easy to rehydrate. I usually just add to the cooking process and its good to go.

Food scarcity is legit, so if you can stock up when items are on sale, then I recommend to do so. Consider it insurance.

FYI: food and such are sold based on weight, not volume. There is 1lb, 2 oz packed in this #10 can (that reads, "number ten" not "ten pound"- it is a size of can). Using a #10 can means that it provides uniformity among storage. Emergency supplies are packed for long term and are packed to stack. They also float. They can be repurposed. Even if one gets a dent, contents are still good (unless and actual hole, which is not likely to happen). The food will not be filled to the brim, and also.. food settles after packing.

product_category: Tools & Home Improvement | Sports Water Bottles
review_text:
A failure in design and implementation. I have to say that my wife was really looking forward to this, but upon trying it out, we are not impressed. Yes, it looks very, very good. It looks like a quality product, in a nice box. However, if what makes this so different from a normal, $10 insulated water bottle is the electronics, then there is a big failure.

The bottle uses a unique charging adapter from a USB port. This looks cool and I guess it is done to provide a waterproof charging connection. The problem is that the adapter to the actual bottle top is connected so lightly that it just keeps falling off. I’m not talking about falling off if moved around, I mean it falls off when sitting on a table. The weight of the adapter and the USB cord is too much. The only way to get it to stay put is to lay the bottle down and wedge in the adapter. You could also tape it on, but doesn’t that take away from the really nice aesthetics of the bottle? This is just a bad design and implementation.

The instruction book is ok, but does not address how specific things operate, such as the display screen while charging. If you are charging, why should the controls turn off the display? Wouldn’t it be helpful to actually see that the unit is charging or not. The “not” part is about the adapter falling off.

If you don’t use the app, well you get basic information on the bottle top, but that really cannot be changed. I’m not a technophobe, as I began writing software 40 years ago, but is it really necessary that everything must be connected to a phone? Also, my wife was wondering why does it seem the manufacturer has some overwhelming need to focus on menstrual cycles? Having to bottle track the cycle is ok, I guess, but it would make more sense to address how the display works when charging than constant focus on a menstrual period?

So, an expensive product that has a primary selling point of electronic display that cannot be reliably charged and uses a proprietary charging adapter, well that isn’t a very good product. It looks nice, it holds liquids, but it just does not meet its promise. I won’t give this 1 star, but I will give it 2. If I’m only looking for an insulated water container, well I can get a lot better for a fraction of the price.

Note: I have been an Amazon customer for almost 20 years. I write all of my reviews to reflect my personal observations and opinions on a product. It matters not if I have purchased the item myself or if it was provided to me for review. My goal is to provide other potential customers as much real-world knowledge as possible to make an informed decision. In most cases I will return to my review in 6 months or less to see if I should alter my original observations. In no case will the cost of a product influence my opinions at all. In addition, I will try to include multiple images and or videos on each product, if practical.

review_text:
Nice pack, poor hydration bladder. I took this on a 12 mile trail run for testing and a 2 mile walk. This is a longer length pack than my normal hydration or equipment packs but it was very comfortable. I'm 5'5" and the pack might be too long for much shorter people but would be great for anyone my size or taller. The chest straps have an adjustment slide to allow for a good position no matter your chest configuration :) There is a safety whistle on the chest strap. There are reflective strips on the front straps, in the form of loops, and on the back pack body so you are easy to spot coming or going. The main hydration compartment has a pocket to hold the bladder along with velcro loops that secure it at the top and these two things keep it from bouncing. There is a second large compartment with 2 net pockets for securing small items and a small pocket near the top for smaller items and (my favorite) a small zippered pocket on the bottom of the pack that can hold small items and is pretty easy to access without taking the pack off. Two net pockets, one on each side, with elastic to hold water bottles or umbrellas. There is an elastic cord across the back to hold extra gear or tuck a towel into. The zippers have quality loop pulls that makes opening the pack, even with gloves on, an easy job. The color is gorgeous. The waist belt can accomodate a 44" waist- if your waist is bigger than this- the waist belt will not fit.
The downside was the included hydration bladder. The hose was lightweight and kept crimping. The valve wouldn't hold suction so, after each sip, air was sucked into the hose meaning each new sip meant sucking out all the air before getting to the water. I had to stop the run several times to straighten the hose and stop coughing from trying to drink an air/water mix. I will be replacing the bladder but the pack is a keeper. Another reviewer suggested there was no hose feed from the bladder compartment to the outside of the pack but that is incorrect. The hose is meant to thread out from the pack through a tunnel in the top of the pack shoulder strap or either side and then lay on the front of the strap to make getting at the hose easy. Many of my hydration packs have this construction but the feature would be easy to miss if you hadn't seen it before.
This pack can hold enough gear for a long run or walk and is lightweight and comfortable. Swap out the bladder.

product_name: Marmot Men's Rocklin Full Zip Jacket
review_text:
Great fleece, not great for layering in my situation. This is a great fleece jacket that is very pliant, soft, stretchable-enough and a light-medium weight where you could wear it, say, when it's just below 60 F inside your house as a lone layer and stay cozy.

Unfortunately this was purchased to be used in layering over a heavy form-fitting polyester hoodie and under a light jacket. For this, it's not so great since it's a bit baggy in the sleeves (especially the bicep, and somewhat in the forearm. It can be used for layering but only if you don't mind having movement inhibited a bit or wear a really baggy outer jacket.

Not sorry I own it but I do wish it were a slightly slimmer fit. Also, it's not very warm. Not warm enough to really want to use this as a midlayer. What I'm getting at is that this is a nice piece of athleisure wear to be enjoyed on its own.

The seams are nice and flat and don't bother me at all, and I'm easily annoyed by pokey seams. The two zip pockets go ALL THE WAY UP, the pocket that is, not the zipper, so once they're open you could really pack quite a bit of crap in there. I'm not sure I understand why Marmot does this with their jackets but it doesn't hurt. Could stuff a hat and gloves into one pocket alone, or a full roll of paper towels. Weird.

I've not been particularly careful with how I wash it, but even after 5-8 washes the fleece still has some water repellent properties, which is nice. Would totally buy this again. Great find on my journey for the perfect midlayer but not the last stop.

review_text:
Cold Hands? Problem Solved!. My wife suffers with severely cold hands when skiing and doing evening volunteer work at a local community Christmas light display. Electric heated gloves have been a game changer for her, and she has evaluated multiple brands and models searching for the perfect solution. These gloves from Royalrose have been the favorite she has tried thus far!

Pros
- Even heating throughout all fingers and thumb
- Battery life is very good with the included 3000mAh batteries (higher capacity than others we tried)
- Batteries are easy to install in zip pockets (this has been a problem with other brands we tried)
- Gloves are very comfortable and have kept hands dry all day in wet conditions
- Gauntlet style cuffs work great for fit over ski parka sleeves

Cons
- Touch screen feature just barely works for essential phone operations only (-1 star). It took a lot of time and saintly patience just to unlock the phone and swipe on a few emails. Forget texting. If you really need to use your phone productively you'll be taking these gloves off
- The cinch bungee on the cuff dangles out quite a ways and is a bit of a snag hazard on the ski lift
- Like many ski gloves/mitts, It would be nice to have wrist leash straps to keep the gloves attached to the arm when removed

Overall, the cons are relatively minor points that are outweighed by the very functional features and performance of these new favorite heated gloves. Very happy, and highly recommended!

Pro tip: If you plan on using these gloves for stretches longer than 3-4 hours you will want to pick up a second set of batteries. For all-day outings, a single set of batteries has come up short many times and left my wife suffering cold hands in the latter hours of the day. Before extra batteries, she would often resort to turning down the heat level to get the batteries to last longer, but that also left the gloves not really warming her hands adequately. Adding a second set of batteries has been an ESSENTIAL enhancement in extending the effective run time of the electric gloves by several hours allowing her to crack on in comfort at the highest heat setting all day.
