review_text:
disappointed.. I give it 5 stars for warmth - I have Raynaud's and I am constantly searching for better ways to heat my toes. Heated socks were good, but they had hot spots (that hurt) and had no durability. Last year I tried heated insoles, which work great in my extra thick slippers but the heat was focused on the instep, leaving my toes to still get cold unless I used the hottest setting. So far these heated slippers are better as they seem to heat my whole foot - my toes are pretty happy again.

I give it 4 stars for wear-ability. The fit is good (ordered the small and I have small feet, men 8.5), but when walking around I feel a slight tendency for my foot to roll off the side of the sole. This feels a little dangerous.

I give it 4 stars for operation. Three things I'd like changed: 1) the buttons are way too bright during operation. When sitting in my lounger watching TV, the lights on my feet are a distraction. 2) Once turned on, it is way too easy to accidentally change the power level when your foot brushes up against anything. I think the button should be harder to press, or that you should have to hold the button down longer for it to change levels (by the way, they say to hold it for 3 seconds to turn on or off, but it's really about 1 second). 3) The color code of the power levels is weird. I have other heated devices that have 3 levels and ALL of them go Red to Green to Blue (red is highest, blue is lowest), but these slippers have Blue as medium and Green as low - that's just weird.

I give it 4 stars for affordability. $80 seems a bit high.

Something strange, but charging these batteries the very first time broke my usb adapter (rated for 2 outlets at 2.1a each). I didn't notice when it broke, but when I checked on the batteries a few hours later, the adapter was dead. It's hard not to blame these batteries, considering all of the use this adapter has had in the last few years.

I just ordered 2 pairs of extra batteries (which are not a bad price at $27) so that I can have heat all day/evening.

Update (Jan 17) - the accidental button pressing is getting very annoying. I suppose if you sit perfectly still (never cross your feet, or place them sideways on the floor or against objects) then this isn't a problem, but if you move your feet around at all, you are going to be changing the heat level constantly. Now I'm looking at my feet about every 10 minutes just to make sure I've not bumped the button again.

Update (Jan 20) - Durability - sucks. I've only had these for 5 days and already they are barely working. The first 2 days these heated my whole foot. Now, even on the highest setting, I can only feel a little heat in the very tip of the slipper. My feet are cold again. Very disappointed.

review_text:
Perfect replacement for dog leash clip. I bought this to replace the clip on my dogs leashes. Honestly perfect in almost every way. My dogs are very athletic and strong despite how small they are. They love pulling me around on walk, everyone comments how weirdly muscular they look compared to their sisters. They are also reactive jerks, they got that from their mom. It doesn’t matter if it’s a person or a dog, if they’re on a bike, they will pull and bark. One’s gotten better at not reacting and the other, well he almost broke his leash clip. I needed something stronger for him. The leashes with a carabiner clips out on the market didn’t look very sturdy or lacked a locking mechanism, or the few that did they were ridiculously expensive for a single leash.
This carabiner had good reviews, so I tried it out. It was a bit bigger than i expected even after seeing pictures. But it’s very sturdy and the locking mechanism has not failed me yet. It’s very easy to open & close, just twist it. Once it’s in the right position it stays there. It is light weight for me, my dogs have never complained about it even though it is heavier than the usual dog clip they used before. I’ve only been using mine for about half a year maybe more, so the black coating is wearing off in some places especially where it gets constant friction but that expected. Overall it’s been in good condition and has kept my dog from breaking away from his leash.

The belt is made of a stretch type  nylon which allows it stretch slightly when you are engaging in work (or sporting) activity. It's different in that you can disengage the belt from the buckle by lifting the pull end of the belt and sliding the belt through the buckle clutch rather than unhooking the buckle itself. This allows for the belt to be loosened or tightened to any degree needed rather than relying on traditional riveted holes punched into a belt. This belt also has a loop to tuck the end of the belt in so it is secure and not dangling. I should have payed more attention to the length dimensions listed because I purchased the large size thinking that's what I normally would purchase, but in retrospect, I should have purchased the medium as the length is 4" shorter at 49" rather than the 53" for the large. Non the less, this belt works very well for my needs and I may well buy another at some point. For work or play this is a solid belt to own. Highly recommend.

product_name: Lifepro 4-In-1 Aerobic Step Platform - Adjustable Multifunctional Balance Board, Steppers for Exercise, Stepper Platform - Home Workout Step Up Exercise Step Platform For Balance & Gym Class, Non Slip
review_text:
This board is FUN.. Yes, I am a bit of a sucker for gadgets and doo dads that encourage so-called workout activity. I am not a person that is able to create and stick with a workout routine. Just the word “workout” is ominous and makes me cringe. The structure the word implies causes me to balk and rebel, and curl up under a blanket and switch a movie on. I do however, like to have fun, so like outdoor activities like hiking and biking. But I live in a climate not favorable to that for half the year.

The first thing I appreciated (and is most important to me) was the wealth of information Lifepro gives you in easy to digest images of how you can use the platform. You don’t have to spend all kinds of time researching yourself (requiring motivation and follow-through I just don’t have). There are ideas on the product page, in videos, on a poster provided in the package. Just pick one or two to get started, then pick a different one or two the next time, and on and on. You can’t get bored with this thing, because there’s so many twists you can add to change things up. The first day all I did was balance on it, starting with the two half moons for front-to-back stretching, then the center ball for 360 balancing. It felt so good to just stretch my ankles and calves. And, balancing is just fun!

The board is very grippy, so my footing feels totally secure in gym shoes. I despise doing squats, but something about my feet being at an angle or in balancing mode makes it much more entertaining – I think part of it is that my muscles just work better that way, and part is that psychologically I am focusing more on keeping my balance than the misery of my screaming, out of shape muscles.

The height of this stepper is pretty low, much lower than a jump box I have. Actually, this is a really good beginner jump box! I will try that tonight. On day 3 I simply used as a stepper after work one day and it was a way to get my heart rate up a little bit on a day I was too tired to do anything else.

A lot of thought went into the design. First, all of the various base components fit on the bottom at the same time for storage, so you don’t have all these spare pieces laying around. I will say the board is best stored flat, I am noticing each time I try to store vertically the various feet keep falling out. I understand if they fit too tight, they aren’t easy to change out, but I wish they fit a little bit tighter than they do. The handles on the sides of the board have covers that pop in and out, so are optional – so you can really maximize the space for secure footing, or remove the covers so you can use the handles for floor work. Once you’ve mastered some basic moves, you can also start incorporating resistance bands to kick things up a notch.

You really get a lot in a compact and affordable package, and others I’m seeing don’t really hold a candle to this one. Lifepro offers so much, where you’d have to buy (and store) several products to do what this alone does. There’s just no comparison. Five stars for a unique and quality product with all the tools to educate yourself on it thoughtfully provided for you!

product_name: Lmdex Dumbbell Rack Stand Weight Rack for Dumbbells Home Gym
review_text:
Solid. I got the Lmdex dumbbell rack to replace a much less substantial rack with only two tiers that took up about the same amount of space. Here in the beginning, know I am very impressed with this new rack.

Make sure you have someone to help you move this Lmdex rack into the general area where you are going to assemble it. It is quite heavy. Of course, if you're working out maybe you can do this yourself, ha ha. Don't hurt yourself. The metal they used in constructing this is not to a metal that will be easily bent so therefore it is heavy.

Assembly is easy. Maybe a tad more detail on the instructions would have been nice... like, "install rubber bottom feet before you put any of this together" and "don't tighten the bolts till the end or else you won't get them all seated in the holes correctly" and "use a socket wrench XX mm or 5/8 inch for bolts" (I didn't have a mm socket available) and "assemble in place so you don't have to move this heavy moose again." These are minor complaints and probably added 10 minutes to my install time. Otherwise it would've gone together in the amount of time it takes to tighten the 12 bolts. No big deal.

This rack holds a lot of stuff! As you can see from the photo, I am using it for more than just dumbbells. It basically finished off my home workout area. It is also significantly better because the bottom tier is high enough my Roomba can get under it. The old one was too low for the Roomba to get under it so cleaning behind it was a pain.

The welds on this are solid and neat. They did not give this to a noob to weld up (it irritates me terribly when companies do that and send sloppily welded items out). I'm not sure if the finish is powder coating or paint, but it is a good looking and seemingly durable finish. I scratched it during assembly and the scratch actually wiped off.

I am very happy with this rack. This is a good solid rack at this price point.

review_text:
Stinky, and won't stop stinking. The pros: feel solid, look cool; the straight, fully-knurled handle is thicker than some others, which is a plus for me.

-- I am moving from a set of 15-pounders of another brand (3.5" across the end) to these 20 pounders (5.5" across the end), and the rubber protrusions make these way bigger, so the few times I've tried them have involved them brushing against me because of the increased width of the end pieces. product_name: Upside Magnetic Golf Cart Phone Holder, Bluetooth Remote Control Included, Record Swing and Take Pictures, Powerful Magnet Mounts to Golf Cart, Includes Metal Golf Bag Cell Phone Clip, Swing Analyzer
review_text:
Limited tilt, but otherwise very handy accessory. I'm not a golfer, but I immediately saw lots of potential to use this phone mount with my Galaxy S21 FE. The magnetic mount holds very firmly to any iron/steel surface. The separate metal clip extends even further the possible things it can attach to.
The remote control gives me freedom to move away from the phone and snap the shot or stop/start a video without running back and forth for every shot. The farthest I could get the remote to trigger my phone was about 12 feet. The remote has its own little clip to attach it to something so I don't have to hold it in my hand constantly. It also is cool that magnetic power holds it in place on the bracket when not in use, so it doesn't slide off and get lost.
I nearly thought the remote didn't work, because my phone never did display it in the list of detected devices to pair with. Fortunately, I accidentally hit the side button on the remote and the phone volume bar responded. Turned out to be paired and working perfectly.
The downsides:
The ball joint in the phone holder tightens down firmly, but the phone can still wobble, because the plastic square that slides into a channel in the bracket doesn't fit the channel snugly.
The ball joint allows the camera to be swiveled to portrait or landscape orientation or anything in between. However, it is extremely limited in its ability to tilt the phone holder up, down, or side to side, because it bumps into the oversized wheel that tightens the ball joint. I have to attach the rig to a surface that is very close to pointing straight ahead to my subject, which might or might not be available. That's a substantial functional limitation.
All in all, though, a solid 4-star recommendation.

product_name: O'Neill Men's Reactor II 3/2mm Back Zip Full Wetsuit
review_text:
Works in a Pinch, But It's Not Good. Needed a 3/2 wetsuit for some unexpected good surf while visiting Florida from Hawai'i. Water was way too cold for me in only boardshorts (been spoiled too long with that tropical blue Hawai'i water..,) and the local surf shops didn't have my size. This was the only Large Short 3/2 wetsuit I could get with next day delivery.

The Good: It did the job. And for cheap; barely 100 bucks. Totally warm in 65 degree water on a moderately chilly 45 degree day (probably not objectively all that cold, but it's very cold compared to what I'm used to.) The neoprene was fresh, soft, and reasonably comfortable. I was expecting much less supple rubber for the cheap-o price. Seams were ok, not great. Sizing was true to Large Short.

The Bad: The key pocket was just a flimsy rectangle of fabric lightly sewn along the inside of the zipper. No loop or lanyard to lock your key in place, and it did not feel secure. You could easily rip the thing off with your fingertips. It didn't even close with a strip of velcro or anything. I kept thinking I was gonna lose my key and get locked out of my car. Zipper also wasn't great in general. I wouldn't expect it (or the key pocket) to hold up to repeated use.

The Ugly: No flush guard. The back zipper is pretty exposed without that flat piece of neoprene covering where your back meets the zipper. This means a lot of water getting into suit all at once from time to time. Didn't affect warmth much, but it caused a lot of very annoying "ballooning," where the sudden flush of water would inflate the small of my back and down to my legs. It was especially bad after deep duck dives and close-out barrels (the official state wave of Florida.) Never had this problem with any other wetsuit. It was a hassle to deal with and very distracting.

Overall: While it was a functional wetsuit for a super cheap price, the flimsy key pocket and the absence of a flush guard cost this wetsuit serious points. It was good enough to help me score a few days of chest high beach break tubes on the mainland without freezing, but I would have gladly spent a bit more money and bought something better if it had been an option. No can recommend, brah.

product_name: GZKYYLEGS 10 ft Inflatable Boat Canoe, 2-Person Inflatable Fishing Kayak Set with Aluminum Oars, Air Pump & Carry Bag, Adults Water Rafts for Lakes, Rivers and Islands
review_text:
If you pay close attention to the product description you'll figure this out. So, first let's be up-front about what this product is: last season's inflatable standup paddle board inserted into a separate inflatable pontoon. It's not a kayak, it's not a canoe, it's not a SUP. Given those facts, this is a nice adaptation for the price. Like all of these high-volume inflatables, get it out of your mind that you're going to use the included manual air pump to inflate these two pieces. The SUP part (or "bottom" as it's called in the product description) needs to be inflated to 15.0 PSI, which no manual pump can really do. The pontoon needs somewhat less (I'd guess about 9.0 PSI), but that's still a lot of pumping. There are two high-pressure valves, on at the rear of the pontoon as indicated in the product description on Amazon, and the other at the front of the SUP piece. Both of them have a twist-lock spring button closure valve, and you'll want an electric pump for them.

The "cushions" are just that: simple blow-up pillows that use a long insertion valve for inflation. Although the product description says they are "detachable," that is in fact their permanent state.

So far, what I've written is the result of experimentation, because no instructions are included with the product. I set my pump at 15.0 PSI for the SUP component based on previous experience with other inflatable SUPs.

Given all of that, this vessel is actually a pretty good value. There are plenty of rubber rope-holds heat-welded to the pontoons, and the promised side ropes run alongside most of each gunwale. I don't have the accessory motor mount, but the rubber brackets for it look sturdy and I don't doubt that the manufacturer experimented with this and thought it through.

If you are looking for a paddler that would safely hold you on a calm body of water, resist stones and rocks near shore, and be very stable while keeping you relatively dry, this little set may be what you want.

review_text: Fits big, vary warm!  you will have to repair leaks.. I love these waders, vary warm, super cheap compared to instore products.  These will keep you warm in -5 degrees hunting weather.  Boots are big!  Order a size or two smaller.  Now for the bad, my friend and I both ordered these for this duck hunting season, they worked great for about 4-5 hunting trips.  Then I developed a small leak in one of the seams.  Wasn't too bad, just a little wet for a couple trips.  However both of us had leaks, small but annoying.  Then on our last duck hunting trip I was up to my waste putting out my decoys and felt cold water running down my legs.  I got out and finished off the morning hunt, these being thick I didn't get too cold but felt wet the whole morning.  My friends waders were also leaking really bad.  When I got home and out of my waders both my legs were completely wet.  There is a large leak in the crotch area.  My hunting friends legs were also completely wet.  I figured at this price point I would have issues and need to make repairs on my own.  These do come with a lifetime warranty, but haven't reached out to see how well and easy this warranty works.  Hopefully they send me some sort of repair adhesive as the small repair kit that comes with it is not enough to seal up the multiple seam leaks we've both developed. review_text: Just getting started, but. Color is exactly what I expected. Arrived quickly. Great Price.  Based on some reviews, I expected to be frustrated with blowing this ball up, but it was super easy. It didn't take much time at all; definitely less than ten minutes. As a tip that might help:  If someone has pain in their foot, leg, or back, (or anywhere that causes them not be able to use the foot pump) then using an electric air pump (the small type used for a blow up bed) would do the job perfectly... and so fast that you'd need to pay attention to not over-inflate. I used the foot pump just to see if it worked and it was no problem; I set aside a few minutes and sat at a kitchen table chair, pumping with one leg for awhile and then the other. It was really no problem.  Other tips that might be helpful: 1) Before use:  pump the ball to about 80% and let it sit for 24 hours before pumping to 100%. I saw that tip online; I think it's to let the ball acclimate to your room temperature; i.e. loosen it up/take its shape.  2) The paper measurement that I received for the Medium ball was accurate, I verified by marking one of my walls at 22 Inches (with a removable sticker) and the ball's top height, once inflated to the measurement tape,  met that line. That was another tip I found online. 3) Once inflated, if you plan to use it for sitting (while working or for doing exercises--like hip movements, etc) then the balls inflation is correct when (once seated) your hips are slightly higher or even with your knees---  your hips should not be lower than your knees in a seated position--- this is very important for keeping correct posture.

review_text:
Fun oil to try. New to purchasing Palm Oil on purpose, and glad for this product. I wanted red palm oil for its tocotrienol source and for being a traditional food, and I use this for both culinary and body care purposes. I wanted a product that wasn't contributing to the ecosystem challenges of exploitive agriculture in developing countries. Fingers crossed this product is grown and manufactured as the brand claims.
The oil is a deep orange/red color, and this transfers into the food- its pretty wild on top of oatmeal or for cooking scrambled eggs or stir fry. It has a pleasant flavor and I look forward to using it in my food. I don't mind cooking higher heat with it, and it does smoke, but so does pretty much all oils I've used, so that says more about my lead foot on the gas pedal than anything.

On the body, it turns my caucasian skin orange, and any light colored cloth it touches gets stained yellow. Such a beautiful yellow though! It feels great on skin and does not contribute to clogged pores, unlike I have read elsewhere (my skin breaks out very easily, and doesn't with this). The tocotrienol antioxdants are nourishing on the skin, and to make it softer in a cold house, I have found it blends well with other oils (MCT, grapeseed, rosehip). I tried it straight up on one arm and not the other for a few days, and noticed a difference in my skin dryness and tone. It doesn't absorb quickly, so its good for massaging to get it soaked in. It seems to be pretty soothing, dare I say healing, on sun-damage areas, too (using it on winter skin in the northern hemisphere at the moment). I like that its edible skin care, and more so that its a delicious food. Will be repurchasing this product.

You can probably run it to the side and behind the belt and it'll be fine, but I don't. The horizontal strap works by just wrapping it around the back pad, but if you want to you can run it behind the frame stays or just behind the pad, depending on where you have it adjusted. Might be a little difficult to cinch down the strap behind the stays, but it will go through there and be out of the way.

It's worth it, and not even "worth it for the money", which really means "It's actually a POS, but it's a cheap POS". This is not a POS, but a well-made product at a good price. But, again, this is based only on the one I got. The one you get might be complete crap.

Be Very Careful With This Herb. Fadogia has been shown to raise testosterone levels significantly (at least in rat studies) and has been recommended by many for this purpose in humans. So, it likely will work in this regard, at least to a degree.

I believe in supplements and take a lot of them, but I am also very careful with what I put in my body. The research on this herb is emerging and it is important to be very careful. I recommend caution. If you use it, I suggest a low dose (no more than one pill) and alternating use on-and-off.

Many gloves have a sort if lightbulb shape to them, rounded around the knuckles. Fairtex gloves are more flat across the knuckles, giving an evenly distributed amount of padding across the hand.

Their padding is also dense. This has 2 advantages:

1. The gloves are more compact, so during sparring they can slip through guards a bit easier.

2. They have a very satisfying sound and feel while hitting mitts and bags compared to more squishy gloves on the market.

After reading up on nano silver, I decided that since it's a fairly new additive and is now being added to quite a variety of products, I'd rather wait and see whether "they" find that it causes problems down the line. So I switched to the powder.

The jar is surprisingly small (compared to how it looks on my laptop), only 2-1/4 " in diameter -- but that means it fits very nicely in my medicine cabinet. Besides, it's sold by net weight, not by the size of the jar! At the three-week mark, I've used nearly half the jar, so I estimate it'll last 6 to 8 weeks.

I like spearmint flavor in moderation, and several reviews said this product has a mild flavor, so that's what I ordered. I wasn't sure I'd like it unsweetened, but it's nice -- like chewing on a mint leaf (rather than mint chewing gum). It does burn just a little, but far less than the vast majority of toothpastes. I may try the citrus flavor next, or could try mixing the two.

One review said that dipping a wet toothbrush into the powder was fine at first, but eventually made the powder get all clumpy. Also, I found that dipping my wet brush into the jar picks up more powder than necessary, so I give my toothbrush a shake after wetting it, before dipping it, and I put a tiny bit of water in my mouth. With the right water-to-powder ratio, it's pretty much like brushing with paste.

Another review mentioned needing to brush again with just water after rinsing, in order to get all the powder off their teeth. I suspect that they were using it like scouring powder, rather than using enough water to make a soft paste. Just a regular rinse works fine for me.

I've been using the powder for three weeks now, and so far I like it just fine -- though I still wish they hadn't added the nano silver to the paste, which I find a bit easier to use. On the other hand, the jar is recyclable and the tube isn't. And I should easily be able to get every last bit of powder out of the jar.

review_text:
Excellent company, however not my favorite cardio machine. I'm baffled on this product; I don't know why my experience isn't in line with all the glowing reviews. I've now had this machine for about six months and have used it 1-2x weekly since I got it.

Assembly was a bear and I could not have done it without my husbands strength and his own helper-tools, because the parts are heavy, unwieldy, and the predrilled holes do not perfectly line up. Once it was assembled, we could feel how sturdy and substantial the machine is.

During the first few uses, I noticed a noise coming from the chain in the front of the unit. SO many reviews said the machine was extremely quiet I was expecting really quiet. However, the machine has always produced a whirring noise during use, due to the chain wrapping around the gear and the rotation of the parts. No big deal, it's not as loud as my old treadmill.

Operation is smooth. The seat is comfortable, though I tend to sit towards the first 1/3 of the seat, so can't say how it would be for someone with longer legs.

The motion of this machine feels very unnatural to me! It's definitely not a rower machine motion, as it is indeed a seated elliptical. It feels awkward every time I use it. The range of motion is limited and compact, meaning you never fully straighten your legs and your arms only move a small distance forward and back. Despite the restricted range of motion, my arms begin to burn and tire out first, while my legs feel like they're not doing much of anything.

For a cardio machine, it does not get me huffing and puffing like my other machines. If you pick up speed, momentum is created that begins to assist your movement. If you increase the resistance so you can't go as fast, then it becomes an upper body muscle workout, as opposed to cardio. I have a treadmill, a stationary bicycle, and a more traditional rower. For time efficiency during my workouts, I much prefer the cardiovascular benefit my other machines provide.

I kept my Teeter hoping that one day the motion would 'click' with me and I'd suddenly appreciate it like so many other reviewers do. Also, there was no way I would have been able to disassemble the machine to return it. I still use it, but it is my least favorite cardio machine in my home gym.

product_name: Travelon Hand Soap Toiletry Sheets, 50-Count
review_text:
An Effective Clean, At Home or On the Road. This product is comparable to putting a capful of Woolite into a sink to hand-wash your clothes. It’s pure detergent, without any water in it, but water-soluble, so you can just drop one or two sheets into the sink, swish the water around until the detergent dissolves, then you can scrub your clothes by hand. It uses less water, isn’t laden with unnecessary perfumes, and doesn’t leave a heavy soapy residue. It’s just pure, compressed cleaning.

Notice, this is a detergent, not a soap. This means you don’t have to use hot water to maximize cleaning; you can achieve best results with cold water. (Though if you’re hand-washing, you may want to use lukewarm water for comfort.) If you have a conventional double kitchen sink, you can wash in one, rinse in the other, and hang your laundry up to dry. It requires very little water, and no electricity, to do your laundry with this product.

Chances are, if you’re considering buying this product, you’re probably considering it for its travel qualities. I’ve used this detergent in the kinds of washbags or hand-cranked washing machines that many people take camping with them, and had equal success. Of course, camping washers do develop an odor over time, and this detergent doesn’t eliminate that odor; you need to use the recommended washing agents that will remove odor from high-efficiency machines.

I’ve read a few people complaining that you need a large amount of this detergent to produce suds. But I respond that this isn’t accidental: manufacturers put lathering agents into many soaps simply because customers associate suds with clean. If you’ve ever watched your laundry in a glass-door washing machine, you already know that most commercial detergents don’t create suds, because suds don’t actually clean. They’re ornamental, nothing more.

You still need to take the usual prewash steps, such as pretreating stubborn stains. This product won’t remove anything set-in or persistent, just like a standard washing machine won’t. Sad to say, I failed to do this with a couple of shirts, which now have their stains set for life. If you want to use this product for maximum efficiency, you need to remain just as diligent about prewashing and stain-treating as you would if using an electric washing machine.

That said, if you travel or camp frequently, or if you prefer a low-electricity lifestyle that favors hand-washing clothes, this detergent should work well for you. I’ve used it for some time, both at home and on the road, with consistent success. As long as you treat the product as seriously as you would with the detergent you’d put into a conventional electric washer, you’ll get clothes that are clean, minimally faded, and comfy to wear.
